After each successful `LDCS ASI_STATUSA` link probe inside `updi_open()`, the function shall read the target's 32-byte System Information Block by transmitting `SYNCH` (`0x55`) followed by opcode `UPDI_OP_KEY_SIB` (`0xE6`) and reading exactly `UPDI_SIB_LEN` (32) bytes of response — looped over `read()` until the full block is collected. The SIB read serves two purposes: (1) it confirms the link end-to-end (target must be actively responding to return non-echo bytes), and (2) it wakes a target that was left in UPDI SLEEP from a prior debug session. Without this step a sleeping target will appear to accept every link-layer probe (STCS, LDCS) — those frames merely echo on the half-duplex line — yet reject every memory access, manifesting as `updi_mem_read()` returning -1 immediately after a successful `updi_open()`. avrdude's `serialupdi` issues this exact 32-byte SIB read on every connect; the response payload (e.g. `" AVR P:2D:1-3M2 (A7.KV001.0)\0"`) is discarded by `updi_open()` since the caller currently only needs the wake side-effect. If the SIB read times out or returns fewer than 32 bytes the attempt shall be abandoned and the next cold-start attempt shall begin.

`updi_enter_debug()` shall arm the AVR-Dx OCD by transmitting the UPDI `KEY` opcode (`0xE0`) followed by the 8-byte key string `"OCD "` (ASCII `0x20 0x20 0x20 0x20 0x20 0x44 0x43 0x4F` — `"OCD"` reversed and right-padded with spaces, per the AVR-Dx datasheet KEY-string LSB-first convention), then pulsing `ASI_RESET_REQ` with `0x59` followed by `0x00`, then polling `ASI_OCD_STATUS` for the STOPPED bit. It shall be called once per session by `main.c` after `updi_open()` and before `rsp_listen()`. Returns 0 on success, -1 on UPDI failure or if STOPPED is never observed.

`updi_ocd_poll_halted(fd, timeout_ms)` shall poll `ASI_OCD_STATUS` via LDCS at ≈1 ms intervals until either `ASI_OCD_STATUS_STOPPED` (0x01) is set or `timeout_ms` elapses. Returns 0 if STOPPED is observed, +1 if the deadline elapses with the CPU still running, and -1 on UPDI failure. The RSP `c` handler uses this primitive with a short (≈1 ms) deadline to multiplex OCD polling with select() on the GDB client socket.

`updi_ocd_read_halt_status(fd, *st0, *st1)` shall read the two OCD halt-cause bytes from `OCD_STATUS0` (`0x0F8C`) and `OCD_STATUS1` (`0x0F8D`) via UPDI LDS and store them in the caller's buffers. The bits in `OCD_STATUS1` distinguish the halt cause: `OCD_STATUS1_EXTBRK` (0x10) is set when the CPU halted due to an external break (STOP via STCS or Ctrl-C), `OCD_STATUS1_BP1`/`BP0STEP`/`SWBP`/`JMP`/`INT` indicate hardware-breakpoint/step/BREAK-opcode/change-of-flow/interrupt halts. Returns 0 on success, -1 on UPDI failure.

`updi_ocd_read_gpr(fd, n, *val)` and `updi_ocd_write_gpr(fd, n, val)` shall read or write byte register `r<n>` (`n` in `0..31`) via UPDI LDS/STS to `OCD_REGFILE + n` (`0x0FA0 + n`). The CPU must be halted; behaviour against a running CPU is undefined. Returns 0 on success, -1 on UPDI failure or out-of-range `n`.

`updi_ocd_read_sreg(fd, *val)` and `updi_ocd_write_sreg(fd, val)` shall read or write the AVR status register via UPDI LDS/STS to `OCD_SREG` (`0x0F9C`). The CPU must be halted. Returns 0 on success, -1 on UPDI failure.

`updi_ocd_read_sp(fd, *val)` and `updi_ocd_write_sp(fd, val)` shall read or write the 16-bit AVR stack pointer (little-endian SPL|SPH) via UPDI LDS/STS at `OCD_SP` (`0x0F98`). `updi_ocd_read_pc(fd, *byte_addr)` and `updi_ocd_write_pc(fd, byte_addr)` shall read or write the 16-bit OCD program-counter register at `OCD_PC` (`0x0F94`), converting between the silicon's word-aligned PC+1 storage and the GDB byte address — read shifts the stored 16-bit word left by one and subtracts the AVR `+1` post-increment; write performs the inverse. The CPU must be halted. Returns 0 on success, -1 on UPDI failure.

`updi_ocd_set_hw_bp(fd, idx, byte_addr)` shall program hardware breakpoint comparator `idx` (0 or 1) to the supplied AVR byte address by writing the 3-byte little-endian address to `OCD_BP0A` (`0x0F80`) for slot 0 or `OCD_BP1A` (`0x0F84`) for slot 1 via UPDI STS, then setting the matching `OCD_CTRL1_BP0` / `OCD_CTRL1_BP1` enable bit and the global `OCD_CTRL0_HWBP` enable bit. Returns 0 on success, -1 on UPDI failure or invalid `idx`.

`updi_nvm_write_eeprom(fd, addr, data, len)` shall write `len` bytes from `data` to the EEPROM window `[UPDI_EEPROM_BASE, UPDI_EEPROM_BASE + UPDI_EEPROM_SIZE)` (`0x814000`–`0x8143FF`). The function shall reject zero-length writes, an `addr` below the window, or `addr + len` past the window end with -1 and without issuing any UPDI traffic. It shall enter NVM programming mode via the standard NVMPROG KEY + reset pulse + `ASI_SYS_STATUS.NVMPROG` poll, then for each byte: (1) `STS NVMCTRL_CTRLA = EEERWR` (`0x13`); (2) `STS addr+i = data[i]`; (3) poll `NVMSTATUS.EEBUSY` (bit 1) clear up to 200 ms. After the final byte it shall write `NVMCTRL_CTRLA = NOCMD` to release the controller. Returns 0 on success, -1 on UPDI failure or BUSY timeout.

`updi_nvm_write_userrow(fd, addr, data, len)` shall write the USERROW window `[UPDI_USERROW_BASE, UPDI_USERROW_BASE + UPDI_USERROW_SIZE)` (`0x810080`–`0x8100FF`, 128 bytes) using the identical NVMPROG + `EEERWR` per-byte sequence as LLR-UPDI-23, with `EEBUSY` polling between bytes. Out-of-window addresses or oversize writes shall return -1 without UPDI traffic. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

`updi_nvm_write_fuses(fd, addr, data, len)` shall write the FUSES window `[UPDI_FUSES_BASE, UPDI_FUSES_BASE + UPDI_FUSES_SIZE)` (`0x820000`–`0x82001F`, 32 bytes) using the same NVMPROG + `EEERWR` per-byte sequence with `EEBUSY` polling. Out-of-window addresses or oversize writes shall return -1 without UPDI traffic. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

`updi_nvm_write_lockbits(fd, addr, data, len, allow_updi_disable)` shall write the LOCK window `[UPDI_LOCK_BASE, UPDI_LOCK_BASE + UPDI_LOCK_SIZE)` (`0x820040`–`0x820043`, 4 bytes) using the same NVMPROG + `EEERWR` per-byte + `EEBUSY` poll sequence. Two safety interlocks gate the write: (a) it shall LDCS-read `ASI_SYS_STATUS` and return `UPDI_ERR_LOCKED` (-3) if `LOCKSTATUS` (bit 1, mask `0x02`) is asserted — the device must already have been chip-erased to clear LOCKSTATUS; (b) when `allow_updi_disable` is false and `len == 4`, it shall reject any payload whose little-endian 4-byte value is not the unlock pattern `UPDI_LOCK_UNLOCKED` (`0x5CC5C55C`), returning `UPDI_ERR_LOCKED` — this prevents accidentally setting bit patterns that would assert `UPDIDIS` and permanently disable the UPDI interface. Out-of-window addresses shall return -1 without UPDI traffic. Returns 0 on success, -1 on UPDI failure or BUSY timeout, `UPDI_ERR_LOCKED` on safety-interlock rejection.

`updi_ocd_clear_hw_bp(fd, idx)` shall disable hardware breakpoint comparator `idx` (0 or 1) by clearing the matching `OCD_CTRL1_BP0` / `OCD_CTRL1_BP1` enable bit via UPDI LDS/STS read-modify-write on `OCD_CTRL1` (`0x0F89`). The function shall not clear the global `OCD_CTRL0_HWBP` bit (the other comparator may still be armed). Returns 0 on success, -1 on UPDI failure or invalid `idx`.

The UPDI module shall publish a `UpdiDeviceMap` struct (family name; USERROW base/size; EEPROM base/size; FUSES base/size; LOCK base/size; SIGROW base; `hw_tested` flag) and a static `g_device_table[]` with one entry per supported family populated from the published datasheet memory maps: AVR-DA (USERROW `0x1080`/32 B, EEPROM `0x1400`/512 B, SIGROW `0x1100`, hw-tested), AVR-DB (identical to DA, untested), AVR-DD (USERROW `0x1080`/128 B, EEPROM `0x1400`/256 B, SIGROW `0x1100`, untested), AVR-DU (USERROW `0x1200`/512 B, EEPROM `0x1400`/256 B, SIGROW `0x1080`, untested), AVR-SD (identical to AVR-DU, untested). FUSES `0x1050`/16 B and LOCK `0x1040`/4 B are identical across all five families. The module shall expose two entry points: (a) `int updi_select_device(int fd, const char *force_family)` — when `force_family` is non-NULL and non-empty, find the entry whose `family` matches `force_family` case-insensitively and set the module's `g_device` pointer to it (emitting a `stderr` warning when `hw_tested` is false); otherwise read SIGROW DEVICEID0..2 at the canonical address `0x1100` and look up the matching autodetect signature for AVR-DA/DB, returning -1 with a diagnostic that lists all five families and the `--force-device` option when DEVICEID0 is not `0x1E` or the signature is unknown; (b) `const UpdiDeviceMap *updi_get_device(void)` — return the current `g_device` pointer (defaulting to the AVR-DA entry so callers that bypass `updi_select_device()` still see the historical AVR-DA constants). All four NVM writer functions (`updi_nvm_write_eeprom`, `updi_nvm_write_userrow`, `updi_nvm_write_fuses`, `updi_nvm_write_lockbits`) shall obtain their window base and size from `updi_get_device()` rather than the compile-time `UPDI_*_BASE/_SIZE` macros. The USERROW writer shall use a stack buffer of size `UPDI_USERROW_ROW_LEN_MAX` (512 B, sized for AVR-DU/SD) and the actual row length from `dev->userrow_size`. Returns 0 on success, -1 on autodetect failure or unknown family name.

The UPDI module shall publish `const char *updi_family_from_partname(const char *partname)`, a table-driven classifier that maps a lowercase Microchip AVR part-name string (the form emitted by the ELF `.note.gnu.avr.deviceinfo` note, e.g. `"avr128da28"`, `"avr64dd32"`, `"avr32sd20"`) onto one of the five family strings already published by `g_device_table[]`. The classifier shall accept the prefix `"avr"` followed by one or more ASCII digits (the flash-size field), followed by exactly two lowercase family-letters: `da`→`AVR-DA`, `db`→`AVR-DB`, `dd`→`AVR-DD`, `du`→`AVR-DU`, `sd`→`AVR-SD`. Any other input — `NULL`, the empty string, a string not beginning with `"avr<digit>"`, or a family-letter pair not in the table (notably `ea`/`eb`, which are the unsupported NVMCTRL v3 families) — shall return `NULL`, signalling the caller that the ELF carries no usable family identification and the SIGROW autodetect fallback in `updi_select_device()` must run. The classifier is intentionally co-located with `g_device_table[]` so that adding a new family requires updating both in the same commit.

`updi_nvm_read(fd, addr, buf, len)` shall read `len` bytes from the supplied UPDI unified-address `addr` into the caller-supplied `buf` using the existing `updi_mem_read()` block-transfer primitive (LLR-UPDI-04). It is a thin wrapper that exists so that Phase 9 verify and fuse-decode call sites read against an API named for the abstraction (NVM read) rather than the transport (UPDI memory read), and so it can be wrapped in unit tests independently of `updi_mem_read()`. The function shall not enter NVMPROG mode (NVM read does not require it) and shall not halt the CPU. Returns 0 on success, -1 on UPDI failure or timeout.

`updi_crc32(buf, len)` shall compute the IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 of the supplied byte buffer using the reflected polynomial `0xEDB88320`, an initial value of `0xFFFFFFFF`, and a final XOR with `0xFFFFFFFF`. The implementation shall be a portable bit-wise loop (no precomputed table) because it is invoked only on verify-mismatch paths where speed is not critical. The function is published purely for the verify diagnostic line so that operators can correlate read-back failures against externally computed checksums (e.g. `crc32 < file`). Returns the computed 32-bit checksum.

The UPDI module shall publish a `UpdiBaudReport` typedef carrying `int baud, int errors, int samples`, the candidate baud ladder `const int updi_baud_ladder[] = {230400, 200000, 150000, 115200, 57600, 38400, 19200}` with `updi_baud_ladder_count = 7`, and the probe function `int updi_probe_baud(const char *serial_device, int samples, void (*visitor)(const UpdiBaudReport *, void *), void *user)`. The probe shall, for each rung in `updi_baud_ladder[]` in order, open the UART at the candidate rate (full cold-start handshake per LLR-UPDI-02 not required — a minimal `updi_open()` is sufficient), issue exactly `samples` `LDCS ASI_STATUSA` probes, count as an error each probe whose response byte is negative (read failure) or whose upper nibble is zero (UPDIREV must be non-zero on a live link), close the UART, and invoke `visitor(&report, user)` with the captured `{baud, errors, samples}`. After walking the entire ladder the function shall return the first rung that observed zero errors (highest-rate first because the ladder is ordered high-to-low), or `-1` if no rung observed zero errors. The probe is read-only: it issues no STCS write, no NVM operation, no system-reset pulse, and does not call `updi_enter_debug()`.

trace.name: Auto-Baud Link-Quality Probe in Device Mode

llr.text: `updi_format_fuses(family, fuse_buf, fuse_len, lock_buf, lock_len, out, out_size)` shall format a human-readable decode of the supplied FUSES window and 4-byte LOCK window into the caller-supplied `out` buffer (NUL-terminated, truncating at `out_size - 1` characters). The decode shall consist of: (1) a header line `Fuses (<family>, <fuse_len> bytes):`; (2) for each byte covered by the per-family fuse table, one indented line ` 0x%02X <FUSE_NAME>%-22s = 0x%02X` followed by indented sub-lines naming each documented bit-field with human-readable enum names (e.g. `WDTCFG.PERIOD = 8K`); (3) for each fuse byte without a registered decoder, one indented line ` 0x%02X (reserved) raw=0x%02X`; (4) a final line `Lock: 0x%08X (UNLOCKED|LOCKED)` where `UNLOCKED` is the canonical 4-byte little-endian value `UPDI_LOCK_UNLOCKED = 0x5CC5C55C` and any other value is reported as `LOCKED`. The decoder tables (`FuseField` struct and `g_avr_dx_fuses[]`) shall live alongside `g_device_table[]` in `src/updi.c` so they are selected by the same `updi_select_device()` runtime path. Phase 9 ships the AVR-DA/AVR-DB table; for other families the function shall emit only the reserved-style lines for every byte (no bit-field decoding). Returns the number of bytes written to `out` (excluding the terminating NUL).

`updi_set_ptr(fd, addr)` shall ALWAYS set the UPDI burst pointer with the 24-bit `ST_PTR_LONG` (`0x6A`) form — `SYNCH`, `ST_PTR_LONG`, `addr` bytes 0..2 in little-endian order, single ACK — for every address, including addresses ≤ 0xFFFF. The 16-bit `ST_PTR_WORD` (`0x69`) form shall never be used. Rationale: `ST_PTR_WORD` updates only the low two pointer bytes and leaves the high byte (bits 16..23) at whatever a previous `ST_PTR_LONG` left it. AVR-Dx mapped-Flash reads set that high byte to `0x80`, so a following 16-bit SRAM read (UPDI `0x004000..0x007FFF`) was misdirected to `0x80xxxx` (mapped Flash) and returned erased `0xFF` on a sparsely-programmed part. Because GDB interleaves Flash reads (code and line tables) with stack reads, this surfaced as intermittently garbage local-variable values and bogus `0x1fffe` backtraces whenever a Flash read preceded a stack read. Emitting the full 24-bit pointer on every pointer-set removes the stale-high-byte hazard (this is also what avrdude's `serialupdi` does). Verified on hardware: an interleaved 16-bit-vs-24-bit A/B test in the same fault window was 0/12 vs 12/12 correct.

`updi_ocd_step_inject_word0(fd, word0)` shall execute exactly one instruction at the current program counter by *injecting* its first opcode word and single-stepping, rather than letting the core fetch from Flash. It shall write the low and high bytes of `word0` to `OCD_INSN0` / `OCD_INSN0+1` and then call `updi_step()` WITHOUT setting `OCD_CTRL0.PCHOLD`, so the core executes the injected instruction and advances the PC normally (per `doc/reference/guesswork.md`: a single-word instruction advances PC by one; for a two-word instruction only the first word is injected and the second word is fetched from Flash, advancing PC by two). The CPU must be halted on entry and remains halted on return; the function returns 0 on success or −1 on any UPDI error. This is the canonical "step over a software `BREAK` / freshly-written PC" primitive: because the opcode is fed to the core directly, it reliably executes the real instruction regardless of (a) a `BREAK` opcode patched into Flash at PC, or (b) the one-instruction skip the silicon performs on the first step/run after a fresh `OCD.PC` write (the inverse hazard documented for `updi_ocd_write_pc()`). It is consumed by the RSP resume path (LLR-RSP-50).

trace.name: True Software Breakpoints via Flash BREAK Opcode

llr.text: The debug-in-sleep policy (HLR-077) shall be a process-global flag, enabled by default, controlled by `updi_set_debug_in_sleep(bool enable)`. `updi_enter_debug()`, immediately after confirming the `STOPPED` bit (the success path), shall call `updi_apply_debug_in_sleep(fd)`, which — when the policy is enabled — issues `STCS ASI_SYS_CTRLA = ASI_SYS_CTRLA_CLKREQ` (bytes `0x55 0xCA 0x01`: SYNCH, `STCS|0x0A`, `CLK_REQ`) to keep the system clock running through `SLEEP`, and — when disabled — performs no write and returns 0. Because the flag is process-global, the policy is honoured at every `updi_enter_debug()` call site (startup and post-`monitor reset`). `updi_apply_debug_in_sleep()` returns 0 on success (including the disabled no-op) or −1 on a UPDI link error.

trace.name: Debug-in-Sleep (preserve the wake source across the SW-breakpoint reset)

llr.text: `updi_save_peripherals(fd, buf)` and `updi_restore_peripherals(fd, buf)` shall snapshot and restore the target peripheral I/O register window `[UPDI_PERIPH_BASE, UPDI_PERIPH_BASE + UPDI_PERIPH_LEN)` = `[0x0040, 0x0C00)` via `updi_mem_read()` / `updi_mem_write()`, so the firmware's configured `SLEEP` wake source survives the NVMPROG system reset of a SW-breakpoint flash patch (HLR-077). The window spans the extended-I/O peripherals (RSTCTRL, SLPCTRL, CLKCTRL, CPUINT, RTC, EVSYS, PORTMUX, PORTs, TCA/TCB, USART, SPI, TWI, AC/ADC/DAC); the low I/O `0x00..0x3F` (CPU core registers + VPORTs — restored separately via the OCD register file and the PORT registers) and NVMCTRL (`0x1000`) are excluded. Both functions shall be gated by the debug-in-sleep flag (LLR-UPDI-35): when disabled (`--sleep`) each shall return 0 immediately without any UPDI traffic. They return 0 on success or −1 on a UPDI link error.

trace.name: Debug-in-Sleep (preserve the wake source across the SW-breakpoint reset)

llr.text: `updi_detach(fd)` shall tear down the serial link WITHOUT pulsing a system reset: it shall `tcdrain()` and `close()` the fd but shall NOT touch `ASI_RESET_REQ` or `ASI_CTRLB`/UPDIDIS. This leaves the target in its current OCD run state (e.g. halted under OCD) so `--stop` keeps the CPU halted after the tool exits, in contrast to `updi_close()` which asserts/releases reset (letting the CPU run) and disables UPDI. A NULL/negative fd shall be a no-op.

function.title: src/gdb_rsp.c — GDB Remote Serial Protocol Server
function.name: rsp
function.intro: Requirements for RSP packet framing, dispatch, GDB packet handlers, session lifecycle, and socket configuration.

llr.text: `rsp_listen()` shall set `SO_REUSEADDR` on the listener socket before calling `bind()`. After `rsp_accept()` returns a connected client socket, the client socket shall have `TCP_NODELAY` set to disable Nagle's algorithm.

`rsp_recv_packet()` shall scan incoming bytes discarding pre-packet ACK/NAK characters until a `$` delimiter is received. It shall accumulate the payload with a running XOR checksum until `#` is received, then compare the computed checksum against the two ASCII-hex checksum bytes that follow. On match it shall write `+` to the socket and return the payload length; on mismatch it shall write `-` and return -1.

The `on_read_regs` handler for the `g` packet shall produce a 78-character hex string in GDB's AVR register-block layout: R0-R31 at hex positions 0-63, SREG at 64-65, SPL at 66-67, SPH at 68-69, and PC as 4-byte little-endian byte-address at positions 70-77. All `g` reads shall use the live OCD register file via `updi_ocd_read_gpr()`, `updi_ocd_read_sreg()`, `updi_ocd_read_sp()`, and `updi_ocd_read_pc()` — the live CPU is the sole GDB thread.

The `on_write_regs` handler shall accept both the full-register `G<78 hex>` and single-register `P<n>=<hex>` packets and shall route each register slot to the matching OCD writer: `updi_ocd_write_gpr()` for registers 0..31, `updi_ocd_write_sreg()` for register 32, `updi_ocd_write_sp()` for register 33 (little-endian 16-bit), and `updi_ocd_write_pc()` for register 34 (little-endian 32-bit byte-address). On success the handler shall reply `OK`; on any OCD failure or hex parse error it shall reply `E01`.

The `on_read_mem` handler for `m addr,len` shall translate the GDB unified-address `addr` to a UPDI physical address by flipping bit 23 (GDB FLASH at `< 0x800000` maps to UPDI `0x800000+`; GDB data space at `>= 0x800000` maps to UPDI `0x000000+`), then call `updi_mem_read()` and return the result as a hex string. Both FLASH and SRAM addresses shall be accepted.

The `on_write_mem` handler for `M addr,len:data` (hex-encoded) and `X addr,len:data` (binary-encoded) packets shall route by the GDB address space: writes with bit 23 set (data space) shall go to `updi_mem_write()` against the GDB-byte address with bit 23 cleared; writes with bit 23 clear (program space) shall go to `updi_nvm_write_flash()` against the GDB address OR'd with `UPDI_FLASH_BASE` (`0x800000`). Returns `OK` on success, `E01` on failure.

The `on_insert_bp` handler for `Z0` and `Z1` shall route both kinds to the same two AVR-Dx OCD hardware comparators tracked by `RspContext.hw_bp_addr[0..1]`. If the supplied address is already present in either slot the handler shall reply `OK` without re-programming silicon. Otherwise the handler shall find an empty slot (sentinel `0xFFFFFFFF`), call `updi_ocd_set_hw_bp()` with the GDB-byte address masked to 23 bits, record the address in the shadow, and reply `OK`. The handler shall not call `updi_nvm_write_flash()` — patching the AVR BREAK opcode into FLASH at runtime is incompatible with maintaining live OCD register state.

The `on_remove_bp` handler for `z0` and `z1` shall locate the supplied address in `RspContext.hw_bp_addr[0..1]`, call `updi_ocd_clear_hw_bp()` for that slot, reset the slot to the empty sentinel, and reply `OK`. If the address is not present in either slot (e.g. the server has been restarted mid-session and lost the shadow) the handler shall reply `OK` rather than an error so a GDB resync after reconnect is non-fatal.

When `on_insert_bp` is called and the single user `RspContext.hw_bp_addr[]` slot (slot 0) is occupied, and the requested address does not match that slot, the handler shall not call `updi_ocd_set_hw_bp()` and shall reply with the GDB error packet `E08`. This surfaces the fact that although AVR-Dx has two comparators, one is permanently reserved for the 32-bit stepping errata workaround, leaving exactly one hardware breakpoint slot available for the user.

The `on_step` handler for `s`/`vCont;s` shall read the current PC and the corresponding opcode. If the instruction is a 32-bit `CALL`, `JMP`, `LDS` or `STS`, it shall calculate the target PC of the next instruction, install a temporary hardware breakpoint at that target PC using `BP1` (slot 1), call `updi_run()` and await a halt, then immediately clear the `BP1` comparator. Otherwise, it shall call `updi_step()`. In either case, it subsequently invalidates the FSM thread cache, rebuilds the thread list, and then replies with the stop-reason packet `T<sig>thread:<active_id>;` produced by the `on_halt_reason` handler. The signal returned by `signal_for_halt_status()` shall be `T02` (SIGINT) if `OCD_STATUS1.EXTBRK` is observed (e.g. the step landed back inside a software-halt window) and `T05` (SIGTRAP) otherwise.

The `on_continue` handler for `c`/`vCont;c` shall, before resuming, call the `continue_step_over_leading_cof(ctx)` helper to compensate for the AVR-Dx OCD "first change-of-flow after RUN" errata (issue #40, HLR-062): the helper reads the live PC via `updi_ocd_read_pc()` and the 4 opcode bytes at that PC via `updi_mem_read(fd, pc | UPDI_FLASH_BASE, buf, 4)`, and — if the instruction is a direct 32-bit `CALL` (`(w0 & 0xFE0E) == 0x940E`) or `JMP` (`(w0 & 0xFE0E) == 0x940C`), decoding the branch target `k = w1 | ((w0 & 0x0001) << 16) | (((w0 & 0x01F0) >> 4) << 17)` — emulates the change-of-flow over OCD via `updi_ocd_emulate_cof_32bit()` (return address `pc + 4` pushed for `CALL`, `0` i.e. no push for `JMP`; branch byte target `k * 2`) so the subsequent free-run resumes at a non-CoF instruction. 16-bit change-of-flow (`RJMP`/`RCALL`/branches/`RET`/`ICALL`) and the resume-from-SW-BREAK case read back as non-matching opcodes and fall through to a plain run unchanged. The helper returns 0 (with or without an emulation) or -1 on UPDI error, in which case the handler replies `E01`. The handler shall then call `updi_run()` and `fsm_invalidate()`, then enter a poll loop that waits for either (a) a spontaneous CPU halt detected by `updi_ocd_poll_halted()` or (b) an async-interrupt byte (`\x03`) on the GDB client socket. The loop shall multiplex the two events using `select()` with a 5 ms timeout on the client socket; on socket-readable it shall consume one byte and break on `0x03`; on select-timeout it shall poll OCD with a 1 ms deadline. After the loop breaks the handler shall call `updi_halt()` to guarantee the CPU is stopped, rebuild the FSM thread list, and reply with `T02thread:<id>;` if Ctrl-C was received or `T05thread:<id>;` otherwise. The handler shall give up after `UPDI_FAIL_MAX` (8) consecutive `updi_ocd_poll_halted()` failures and reply `E01` rather than spinning indefinitely on a degraded UPDI link.

`rsp_dispatch()` shall handle the following packets inline without invoking any `RspHandlers` slot, because each response is a fixed string requiring no target interaction: `qSupported` (responds with `PacketSize=800;QStartNoAckMode+;multiprocess-;vContSupported+`), `qAttached` (responds `1`), `QStartNoAckMode` (calls `rsp_set_noack(true)` and responds `OK`), and `vCont?` (responds `vCont;c;s`).

The `on_detach` handler for the `D` packet shall release both AVR-Dx OCD hardware-breakpoint comparators by calling `updi_ocd_clear_hw_bp()` for every occupied `RspContext.hw_bp_addr[]` slot and resetting the shadow to the empty sentinel, then call `updi_run()` to resume the target, send the `OK` reply, close the GDB client socket, and reset `*ctx->gdb_fd_p` to -1 so the event loop re-enters the listening state. The server process shall not exit. Without the comparator cleanup, BP0/BP1 remain armed in silicon and the next GDB session inherits stale breakpoints from the previous client.
The `on_detach` handler for the `k` (kill) packet shall set `g_quit = 1` to cause the event loop to exit, triggering the full resource teardown sequence defined by LLR-MAIN-07.

The `on_monitor` handler for `qRcmd` shall pass the raw ASCII-hex-encoded command body directly to `monitor_dispatch()` without pre-decoding it, and relay the return code to the GDB client as `OK` on success (return 0), an O-packet error message on UPDI failure (return -1), or an empty reply on unrecognised sub-command (return -2).

The `H` (set-thread) packet handler shall store the requested GDB thread ID in the session context. The live CPU is the sole GDB thread (TID 1); thread IDs -1 (all threads) and 0 (any thread) shall both be interpreted as the live-CPU thread. Register and memory operations always target the live CPU.

The `signal_for_halt_status()` helper shall read `OCD_STATUS0`/`OCD_STATUS1` via `updi_ocd_read_halt_status()` and return the stop-signal string `"T02"` (SIGINT) if `OCD_STATUS1_EXTBRK` (0x10) is set in `OCD_STATUS1`, or `"T05"` (SIGTRAP) otherwise (covering hardware-breakpoint match, BREAK opcode, single-step, change-of-flow, and interrupt halts). On OCD read failure the helper shall default to `"T05"` so a degraded link still surfaces a non-empty stop reason to GDB.

The `hw_bp_clear_all(ctx)` helper shall check `ctx->hw_bp_addr[0]` and, if it is not equal to the empty sentinel (`0xFFFFFFFF`), call `updi_ocd_clear_hw_bp()` and reset the slot. It shall be called by `on_detach` for the `D` packet to guarantee the user's silicon comparator is released before the target is resumed. (Slot 1 is temporarily utilized by `dh_step` and cleared immediately within that function.)

The `dh_query_c()` default handler (`qC`) shall reply with `QC<hex>` where `<hex>` is the lowercase-hexadecimal GDB thread id currently selected for `c`/`s` operations (the most recent `Hc<tid>` value, stored at `*ctx->c_thread_p`). If no `c`-thread has been selected, or the selected value is zero or negative, the reply shall be the literal `QC0`. The handler shall not touch the UPDI link, the FSM context, or any OCD register.

trace.name: Protocol Cleanup — qC, qOffsets, T, R

llr.text: The `dh_query_offsets()` default handler (`qOffsets`) shall reply with the fixed literal string `Text=0;Data=0;Bss=0`. The AVR reset vector is anchored at FLASH address zero and avrOS performs no position-independent loading, so all three section offsets are reported as zero unconditionally. The handler shall not touch the UPDI link, the FSM context, or any OCD register.

trace.name: Protocol Cleanup — qC, qOffsets, T, R

llr.text: The `dh_thread_alive()` default handler (`T<tid>`) shall parse `<tid>` as a hexadecimal GDB thread id and reply `OK` when the id is present in `ctx->fsm->threads[].gdb_id` (with `ctx->fsm->valid == true`), `E01` otherwise. When the FSM context is unset or invalid the handler shall accept thread id `1` only (the default active thread on a freshly-attached session) and reject all others with `E01`. The handler shall not touch the UPDI link or any OCD register.

trace.name: Protocol Cleanup — qC, qOffsets, T, R

llr.text: The `dh_restart()` default handler (`R<XX>`) shall implement the extended-remote restart semantics by: (1) calling `updi_enter_debug()` to pulse `ASI_RESET_REQ` and re-enter OCD halted at the reset vector, replying `E01` and returning if the UPDI primitive fails; (2) calling `fsm_invalidate()` to drop the stale virtual-thread cache; and (3) delegating to `dh_continue()` with a synthetic `c` packet so the target resumes, the thread list is rebuilt on the next halt, and the resulting stop-reply packet is emitted to GDB. The `<XX>` byte of the inbound packet shall be ignored per the GDB protocol.

trace.name: Protocol Cleanup — qC, qOffsets, T, R

llr.text: The `dh_vrun()` default handler (`vRun;[<filename>][;<arg>...]`) shall implement extended-remote start-new-program by ignoring the filename and argument list (the target program is already in FLASH and there is no host-side filesystem), then performing a reset-and-halt-at-entry sequence: call `updi_enter_debug()` (reply `E01` on failure) to halt the CPU at the reset vector, call `fsm_invalidate()`, call `fsm_build_thread_list()` to rebuild the per-FSM thread cache, and delegate to `dh_halt_reason()` (`?`) to emit a `T05` stop reply. Per the GDB Remote Serial Protocol, `vRun` must return a stop reply immediately — the client decides when to start execution via its own `c` / `s` packets; the handler must NOT call `updi_run()` or otherwise resume the CPU.

The `dh_vattach()` default handler (`vAttach;<pid>`) shall implement extended-remote attach by ignoring `<pid>` (the AVR target has no process namespace), then: (1) calling `updi_enter_debug()` to halt the running target and re-enter OCD, replying `E01` on UPDI failure; (2) calling `fsm_invalidate()` and `fsm_build_thread_list()` so virtual-thread state is fresh; and (3) delegating to `dh_halt_reason()` to emit a SIGTRAP stop reply containing the active `thread:<hex>;` so GDB knows the target is halted and ready for register and memory queries.

The `dh_vkill()` default handler (`vKill[;<pid>]`) shall close the current GDB session without terminating the avrOSdb process. It shall ignore `<pid>` and, in order: (1) call `updi_halt()` on the target so the next attached session sees a stopped CPU; (2) release both AVR-Dx OCD HW-breakpoint comparators via `rsp_hw_bp_clear_all(ctx)`; (3) clear the per-session SW-breakpoint shadow via `rsp_sw_bp_clear_all(ctx)`; (4) reply `OK` to the client; (5) set `ctx->disconnect_reason = "vKill"` so `event_loop()` emits the lifecycle log line per LLR-MAIN-22; (6) close `*ctx->gdb_fd_p` (when ≥ 0) and set the pointed-at fd to `-1`. The handler shall **not** set `*ctx->quit_p`. This makes vKill a per-session disconnect (HLR-064) rather than a server-shutdown command; the legacy `k` packet path in `dh_detach` retains the old quit behaviour for operators relying on it.

The inline `qSupported` reply shall be the literal string `PacketSize=800;QStartNoAckMode+;multiprocess+;vContSupported+;vRun+;vAttach+;vKill+`. The `multiprocess+` feature is advertised even though the AVR target supports only a single process — it informs GDB that the server understands `<pid>.<tid>` thread-id syntax and accepts the extended-remote `v*` packets. `vRun+`, `vAttach+`, and `vKill+` advertise the corresponding handlers added by HLR-058. The inbound `vAttach?` capability probe shall be answered with `OK`.

The `dh_insert_bp()` handler shall recognise the GDB watchpoint request prefixes `Z2`, `Z3`, and `Z4` and reply with the empty RSP packet (payload of length zero, on-the-wire `$#00`). The `dh_remove_bp()` handler shall do the same for `z2`, `z3`, and `z4`. The empty reply is the documented RSP signal for "feature unsupported" and causes GDB to silently fall back to software watchpoints. No call into the UPDI layer is made; no shadow state is consulted or updated; and no `qSupported` capability advertises watchpoints.

The `dh_vflash_erase()` default handler (`vFlashErase:<addr>,<length>`) shall parse the two hex fields and refuse with `E22` if either is malformed, `length` is zero, or any address in the range `[addr, addr+length)` has the data-space flag set (i.e. `(addr | (addr+length-1)) & GDB_AVR_DATA_FLAG`) — this rejects EEPROM, USERROW, FUSES, LOCK, and SIGROW windows since `gdb load` provides no per-window verb. Lengths larger than 1 MB shall also be refused with `E22` as a runaway-allocation guard. On success the handler shall (re-)allocate `RspContext.flash_xact_buf` to span the page-aligned union of any prior erased range and `[floor_page(addr), ceil_page(addr+length))`, pre-filling new pages with `0xFF`, and reply `OK`. Erase-on-silicon is deferred until `dh_vflash_done()` because `updi_nvm_write_flash()` performs an FLPER per page before each FLWR.

The `dh_vflash_write()` default handler (`vFlashWrite:<addr>:<binary>`) shall refuse with `E22` (and discard any in-progress page buffer) if no `vFlashErase` is active, the address is malformed, the address has the data-space flag set, or the address is below `RspContext.flash_xact_base`. Otherwise it shall decode RSP binary-protocol escapes (`0x7D <b>` → `b XOR 0x20`) in the payload and copy the resulting bytes into `flash_xact_buf` at offset `addr - flash_xact_base`, replying `E22` on buffer overflow and `OK` on success. The payload byte count is derived from the `plen` argument threaded through `rsp_dispatch_n()` so embedded NUL bytes do not truncate the copy.

The `dh_vflash_done()` default handler (`vFlashDone`) shall (a) if no transaction is active, reply `OK` immediately (treating the packet as a no-op); (b) otherwise call `updi_nvm_write_flash(updi_fd, UPDI_FLASH_BASE + flash_xact_base, flash_xact_buf, flash_xact_len)`, freeing the buffer and clearing `flash_xact_base/len` regardless of outcome, then reply `E22` on UPDI failure or — on success — call `rsp_hw_bp_clear_all()` (because the FLASH word at each shadowed HW-BP address may have been overwritten by the load), call `updi_enter_debug()` to leave the CPU halted at reset, and reply `OK`. Any `g`/`G`/`P`/`m`/`M`/`X`/`c`/`s` packet that arrives between `vFlashErase` and `vFlashDone` shall be rejected with `E22` by `rsp_dispatch_n()` and the in-progress page buffer shall be discarded.

The `qSupported` inline reply shall additionally advertise `vFlashErase+;vFlashWrite+;vFlashDone+` so GDB enables the `vFlash*` flow for the `load` command. The length-carrying `rsp_dispatch_n(fd, packet, plen, handlers)` entry point shall be the public dispatch API used by the main event loop; the legacy `rsp_dispatch()` shall remain as a thin wrapper that derives `plen` from `strlen(packet)`, for tests and any caller that knows the packet is ASCII-only.

The `dh_insert_bp()` default handler shall route `Z0,<addr>[,<kind>]` according to `ctx->bp_mode`: to the software-breakpoint installer when `RSP_BP_MODE_SW`, to the legacy hardware-comparator path when `RSP_BP_MODE_HW_ONLY` (per HLR-055 `monitor bp-mode hw-only`), and — when `RSP_BP_MODE_AUTO` (the default, HLR-055) — to a free user HW comparator if one is available (`ctx->hw_bp_addr[i] == HW_BP_SLOT_EMPTY` for `i < RSP_HW_BP_USER_SLOTS`), otherwise falling back to the software-breakpoint installer. In `auto` mode the handler shall first short-circuit a duplicate `Z0` that already matches a `ctx->sw_bp[]` shadow entry or a `ctx->hw_bp_addr[]` comparator with `OK`, so a re-insert of an address already held on the now-occupied comparator does not wrongly install a second SW patch at the same address; a data-space address (`GDB_AVR_DATA_FLAG`) shall be refused with `E22` before either decision. Addresses with the `GDB_AVR_DATA_FLAG` (0x800000) bit set — EEPROM, USERROW, FUSES, LOCK, SIGROW — shall be refused with `E22` on the SW path because the AVR `BREAK` opcode is only meaningful when fetched from FLASH. A duplicate `Z0` on an address already shadowed shall reply `OK` without re-patching. When all `RSP_MAX_SW_BREAKPOINTS` (64) shadow slots are occupied the SW path shall reply `E08`. Z1 packets continue to alias to the OCD HW comparators regardless of `bp_mode` (HLR-016).

trace.name: True Software Breakpoints via Flash BREAK Opcode

llr.text: The SW-BP install path (`sw_bp_patch_flash()`) shall, for each `Z0` accepted in `RSP_BP_MODE_SW`, (1) snapshot R0–R31 via `updi_ocd_read_gpr()`, SREG via `updi_ocd_read_sreg()`, SP via `updi_ocd_read_sp()`, and PC via `updi_ocd_read_pc()`; (1b) snapshot the target peripheral I/O window via `updi_save_peripherals()` (HLR-077 / LLR-UPDI-36) so the firmware's `SLEEP` wake source survives the NVMPROG reset; (2) read the 2-byte original opcode at `UPDI_FLASH_BASE + (addr & GDB_AVR_ADDR_MASK)` via `updi_mem_read()`; (3) write `{0x98, 0x95}` (`BREAK` opcode, little-endian) to the same FLASH word via `updi_nvm_flash_patch()`; (4) call `updi_enter_debug()` to leave NVMPROG and re-enter OCD; (5a) restore the peripheral I/O window via `updi_restore_peripherals()`; (5b) restore R0–R31, SREG, SP, and PC via the matching `updi_ocd_write_*()` primitives (PC last, per the `pc_dirty` handling of LLR-RSP-50); and (6) record `(addr, orig[0], orig[1], in_use=true)` in the first free `RspContext.sw_bp[]` slot. The peripheral save/restore in (1b)/(5a) is a no-op when debug-in-sleep is disabled (`--sleep`). Any UPDI link error during the sequence shall cause the handler to reply `E01` without partially populating the shadow slot.

Debug-in-Sleep (preserve the wake source across the SW-breakpoint reset)

llr.text: The `dh_remove_bp()` default handler, on `z0,<addr>` in `RSP_BP_MODE_SW` or `RSP_BP_MODE_AUTO`, shall scan `ctx->sw_bp[]` for a slot whose `addr` matches and, when found, repeat the snapshot/patch/restore sequence of LLR-RSP-37 — writing the saved `orig[0..1]` bytes back to FLASH at `UPDI_FLASH_BASE + (addr & GDB_AVR_ADDR_MASK)` — then mark the slot `in_use=false` and reply `OK`. When no SW shadow slot matches, the handler shall fall through to the HW-comparator removal path so a `z0` after a `monitor bp-mode` toggle — or an `auto`-mode breakpoint that took the HW comparator instead of the SW table — still drains the correct shadow table. A UPDI link error during the FLASH patch shall reply `E01`.

trace.name: True Software Breakpoints via Flash BREAK Opcode

llr.text: The helper `rsp_sw_bp_clear_all(RspContext *ctx)` shall clear every entry in `ctx->sw_bp[]` (`in_use=false`, `addr=0`, `orig[0]=orig[1]=0`) without issuing any UPDI I/O. It shall be invoked by `dh_vflash_done()` (HLR-053) on successful flush, and by the `monitor reset` / `monitor erase` / `monitor chip-erase` verbs (HLR-055) immediately after their UPDI side-effect, because the underlying FLASH instruction (and therefore the `BREAK` opcode that would otherwise persist) is no longer present.

trace.name: True Software Breakpoints via Flash BREAK Opcode

llr.text: `RspContext` shall expose a new field `const char *disconnect_reason` (default `NULL`). The `dh_detach()` handler shall set this field to the static string `"D"` immediately before closing the GDB socket on the `D`-packet path. The `dh_vkill()` handler shall set it to the static string `"vKill"` immediately before closing the GDB socket per LLR-RSP-25 (HLR-064 listener-survival semantics). The protocol layer shall never call into the entry/event-loop layer to log; the field is the sole upward signal channel and is consumed (read and reset to `NULL`) by `event_loop()` in `src/main.c` per LLR-MAIN-22. This preserves the layered-architecture constraint (SDD §2.2) — no new include from `gdb_rsp.c` to `main.c`.

`gdb_rsp.c` shall define a private `enum RspStopCause { SC_NONE = 0, SC_SWBREAK, SC_HWBREAK, SC_STEP, SC_INTR }` and a private function `static int classify_stop_cause(RspContext *ctx, int hint)` that returns one of those values. The classifier shall: (1) read the live PC via `updi_ocd_read_pc(ctx->updi_fd, &pc)`; on UPDI failure return `hint` (the caller-supplied fallback); (2) if any `ctx->sw_bp[i].in_use` slot has `ctx->sw_bp[i].addr == pc` return `SC_SWBREAK`; (3) else if either `ctx->hw_bp_addr[i] != HW_BP_SLOT_EMPTY` slot equals `pc` return `SC_HWBREAK`; (4) else return `hint`. Callers pass `SC_INTR` from the `dh_continue` path when `got_ctrl_c` is set, `SC_STEP` from the `dh_step` path, and `SC_NONE` from the bare `?` (`dh_halt_reason`) and `vRun` / `vAttach` delegated paths. The classifier shall not call `updi_ocd_read_halt_status()` (the EXTBRK-as-SIGINT decision is owned by `signal_for_halt_status()` and remains there) and shall not adjust the PC.

The `qSupported` reply emitted by `rsp_dispatch()` shall append the literal substring `;swbreak+;hwbreak+` to the existing capability list, immediately after `vFlashDone+`. A new private helper `static int format_stop_reply(int fd, RspContext *ctx, int sig_t05_or_t02, int cause)` shall build a single packet of the form `<sig><tag>thread:<hex_tid>;` where `<sig>` is `"T05"` or `"T02"` (chosen by the caller via `sig_t05_or_t02 == 5` ⇒ `T05`, otherwise `T02`), `<tag>` is `"swbreak:;"` for `SC_SWBREAK`, `"hwbreak:;"` for `SC_HWBREAK`, and the empty string for every other cause, and `<hex_tid>` is the active FSM thread id (`fsm_get_active_thread()`, defaulting to `1`). `dh_halt_reason()`, the final stop emission inside `dh_continue()`, and `dh_step()` (via `dh_halt_reason()` after setting `ctx->last_stop_cause = SC_STEP`) shall route through this single formatter. `dh_continue()` shall set `ctx->last_stop_cause = classify_stop_cause(ctx, got_ctrl_c ? SC_INTR : SC_NONE)` immediately before formatting; `dh_step()` shall set it to `classify_stop_cause(ctx, SC_STEP)`; `dh_halt_reason()` shall set it to `classify_stop_cause(ctx, SC_NONE)` if it has not already been set by the previous-packet path. The previous-packet hint shall be cleared (`ctx->last_stop_cause = SC_NONE`) at the start of every fresh resume (`dh_continue`, `dh_step`, `dh_vrun`, `dh_vattach`) so a stale tag never bleeds across halts.

`rsp_dispatch()` shall recognise packets that begin with the literal prefix `vCont;r` (after the seven-byte `vCont;r` and before any `:<thread>` suffix) and route them to a new private handler `static int dh_range_step(int fd, const char *pkt, void *vctx)`. The handler shall: (1) parse two comma-separated 32-bit hex fields `start,end` immediately after the `r`; on parse failure reply `E22`; (2) reset `ctx->last_stop_cause = SC_NONE`; (3) run the shared core step loop `bp_step_range(ctx->updi_fd, start, end, rsp_step_abort_cb, &ab)` (LLR-RSP-53) — single-step while `start <= pc < end`, bounded by the core's `BP_STEP_RANGE_MAX = 100000` — passing an abort callback that peeks the GDB socket via `select()` (0 ms timeout) for a Ctrl-C (`\x03`) or a peer disconnect; on its return, a UPDI error replies `E01`, a disconnect (`ab.disconnected`) halts and returns -1, and an abort-but-connected sets `got_ctrl_c = true` (range-exit and the cap are ordinary step stops); (4) call `fsm_invalidate(ctx->fsm)` and `fsm_build_thread_list()` after the loop; (5) classify and emit via the LLR-RSP-45 formatter: `ctx->last_stop_cause = classify_stop_cause(ctx, got_ctrl_c ? SC_INTR : SC_STEP); return format_stop_reply(fd, ctx, got_ctrl_c ? 2 : 5, ctx->last_stop_cause);`. The `vCont?` reply shall be extended from `"vCont;c;s"` to `"vCont;c;s;r"`. The new handler shall be wired into the dispatcher in `rsp_dispatch()` as `if (strncmp(packet, "vCont;r", 7) == 0) return dh_range_step(fd, packet, h->ctx);` placed immediately after the existing `vCont;s` route (so `vCont;c` and `vCont;s` continue to match first by virtue of having distinct seventh bytes). The handler shall live alongside `dh_continue` / `dh_step` in `src/gdb_rsp.c` and shall not be added to the `RspHandlers` vtable (the dispatcher invokes it directly because it has no per-test override use case).

`rsp_dispatch()` shall recognise packets that begin with the literal prefix `qXfer:memory-map:read::` (23 bytes) and route them to a new private handler `static int dh_qxfer_memory_map(int fd, const char *pkt, void *vctx)`. The qSupported reply (currently `"PacketSize=800;QStartNoAckMode+;multiprocess+;vContSupported+;vRun+;vAttach+;vKill+;vFlashErase+;vFlashWrite+;vFlashDone+;swbreak+;hwbreak+"`) shall be extended with the suffix `";qXfer:memory-map:read+"`. The handler shall: (1) `strtoul()` two hex fields `<offset>,<length>` immediately after the prefix and reply `E00` on a missing comma or non-hex digits; (2) when both `ctx->flash_size == 0` and `ctx->sram_size == 0`, reply `l` (end-of-transfer with no data) so GDB falls back to its built-in defaults; (3) otherwise render an XML document into a stack `char xml[1024]` via a `snprintf()`-driven append loop, emitting the regions in this order — wrapped in `<memory-map>...</memory-map>`: `<memory type="flash" start="0x0" length="<flash_size>"><property name="blocksize">0x200</property></memory>` (Flash, only when `ctx->flash_size != 0`); `<memory type="ram" start="<sram_base>" length="<sram_size>"/>` (SRAM, only when `ctx->sram_size != 0`); EEPROM at `ELF_VMA_EEPROM = 0x810000` length `UPDI_EEPROM_SIZE = 0x200` typed `flash` blocksize `0x1`; FUSES at `ELF_VMA_FUSES = 0x820000` length `UPDI_FUSES_SIZE = 0x10` typed `flash` blocksize `0x1`; LOCK at `ELF_VMA_LOCK = 0x830000` length `UPDI_LOCK_SIZE = 0x4` typed `flash` blocksize `0x1`; SIGROW at `ELF_VMA_SIGROW = 0x840000` length `UPDI_SIGROW_SIZE = 0x40` typed `rom` (no blocksize child); USERROW at `ELF_VMA_USERROW = 0x850000` length `UPDI_USERROW_SIZE = 0x20` typed `flash` blocksize `0x20`; and — only when `ctx->idx != NULL` and `ctx->map.flash_size != 0` — the mapped-flash data window as `<memory type="rom" start="0x808000" length="0x<min(flash_size,0x8000)>"/>` (HLR-063), where `0x808000 = GDB_AVR_DATA_FLAG | AVR_MAPPED_FLASH_OFF`. The five non-FLASH NVM regions are emitted unconditionally whenever the all-zero short-circuit at step (2) does not fire. On `snprintf` overflow the handler shall reply `E01`. (4) Slice `xml[offset, offset+length)` into the reply, prefix with `'l'` when the slice reaches end-of-document or `'m'` otherwise, and emit via `rsp_send_packet()`; offsets at or past the document length shall reply `l` with no payload. `RspContext` shall gain three sibling fields `uint32_t flash_size; uint32_t sram_base; uint32_t sram_size;` (declared adjacent to `last_stop_cause` in `src/gdb_rsp.h`); `src/main.c` shall populate them from `elf_ctx.flash_size` / `.sram_base` / `.sram_size` at the same designated-initialiser site that already sets `.idx`. The handler shall be inlined into `rsp_dispatch()` (sibling of the `qSupported` / `qAttached` inline routes, before the `case 'q':` switch arm) and shall not consume a `RspHandlers` vtable slot.

`rsp_recv_packet()` and `rsp_send_packet()` shall check a file-scoped boolean flag `g_log_rsp`. If true, `rsp_recv_packet()` shall output `RSP < <packet>` to `stderr` after receipt, and `rsp_send_packet()` shall output `RSP > <packet>` to `stderr` before sending. The flag shall be mutated via a new `rsp_set_logging(bool)` setter exposed in `gdb_rsp.h`.

`dh_read_mem()` shall, immediately after parsing and length-validating the `m<addr>,<len>` packet (and before the GDB↔UPDI bit-23 address translation), call a new file-private helper `static bool mm_range_in_advertised_region(const RspContext *ctx, uint32_t addr, uint32_t len)` and, when the helper returns `false`, return `reply_err(fd, "E14")` instead of invoking `updi_mem_read()`. The helper shall return `false` for `len == 0` or when the 32-bit sum `addr + len` wraps; it shall return `true` when both `ctx->flash_size == 0` and `ctx->sram_size == 0` (no memory map advertised — permissive fallback for HLR-063's no-ELF case); otherwise it shall return `true` iff the half-open range `[addr, addr+len)` lies entirely within one of these seven regions (using the same constants HLR-063's advertisement emits): `[0, ctx->flash_size)` when `flash_size != 0`; `[ctx->sram_base, ctx->sram_base + ctx->sram_size)` when `sram_size != 0`; `[ELF_VMA_EEPROM, ELF_VMA_EEPROM + UPDI_EEPROM_SIZE)`; `[ELF_VMA_FUSES, ELF_VMA_FUSES + UPDI_FUSES_SIZE)`; `[ELF_VMA_LOCK, ELF_VMA_LOCK + UPDI_LOCK_SIZE)`; `[ELF_VMA_SIGROW, ELF_VMA_SIGROW + UPDI_SIGROW_SIZE)`; `[ELF_VMA_USERROW, ELF_VMA_USERROW + UPDI_USERROW_SIZE)`. The helper shall be defined immediately above `dh_read_mem()` in `src/gdb_rsp.c` and shall be `static` (file scope) so it is exclusively callable from the `m`-read path. The check shall NOT be wired into `dh_write_mem()` for this requirement — symmetric write enforcement is deferred. UPDI shall not be touched on a bounds rejection (`mock_read_count` MUST remain 0 in the negative unit test). Mapped-flash reads (LLR-RSP-52) are detected and served before this helper is consulted, so they are not subject to — and do not require an entry in — this advertised-region check.

Installing or removing a software breakpoint via `sw_bp_patch_flash()` enters NVMPROG, which issues a system-reset pulse; the original PC is therefore re-written with `updi_ocd_write_pc()` during `sw_bp_restore_cpu()`. A fresh `OCD.PC` write makes the silicon skip the instruction at PC on the very next step/run, so after such a restore `sw_bp_patch_flash()` shall set `RspContext.pc_dirty = true`. On the next resume, both `dh_continue()` and `dh_step()` shall call a file-private helper `static int consume_pc_skip(RspContext *ctx)` before resuming. The helper shall: return 0 immediately when `pc_dirty` is false; otherwise clear `pc_dirty`, read the live PC and its 4 opcode bytes, and — when the first opcode word is a direct 32-bit `CALL`/`JMP` (`(w0 & 0xFE0E) == 0x940E` or `0x940C`) — return 0 to leave change-of-flow handling to the existing `continue_step_over_leading_cof()` / `dh_step()` emulation (which rewrites `OCD.PC` to the target anyway, so the skip is moot); for any other instruction it shall execute it exactly once via `updi_ocd_step_inject_word0()` (LLR-UPDI-34) — substituting the saved original opcode from the `sw_bp[]` shadow when a `BREAK` is currently patched at PC — and return 1. `dh_continue()` shall call the helper before `continue_step_over_leading_cof()` and `updi_run()`; `dh_step()` shall, when the helper returns 1, treat that injected execution as the single step (rebuild the FSM list, classify the stop cause as `SC_STEP`, and emit the stop reply) without a further `updi_step()`. This prevents the instruction the CPU was halted on (e.g. an argument-setup `ldi` at a breakpoint) from being silently skipped on the next continue/step, which otherwise corrupts downstream execution (observed on hardware as function arguments read as 0).

trace.name: True Software Breakpoints via Flash BREAK Opcode

llr.text: `src/gdb_rsp.c` — the GDB-RSP protocol front-end — shall reach the protocol-agnostic debug core exclusively through the single aggregating include `src/debug_core.h` (which re-exports `updi.h`, `elf_parser.h`, `fsm_mapper.h`, and `monitor.h`), rather than including those core module headers individually. This makes the front-end/core seam explicit and gives a future DAP front-end one documented include over the same core. Phase 15 establishes the seam by aggregation only: the breakpoint arbiter, software-breakpoint shadow/step-over model, and stop-cause classifier remain as core policy inside `gdb_rsp.c` pending the deferred extraction into a dedicated debug-core translation unit; no NEW protocol-agnostic policy shall be added to the front-end's wire-framing paths.

`dh_read_mem()` shall, after parsing and length-validating the `m<addr>,<len>` packet, detect a read in the AVR-Dx mapped-flash data window — `(addr & GDB_AVR_DATA_FLAG) != 0` and `(addr & 0xFFFF) >= AVR_MAPPED_FLASH_OFF` (0x8000) and `ctx->idx != NULL` — and, for such a read, compute the UPDI address as `flash_to_updi((addr & 0xFFFF) + ctx->idx->flash_lma_off)` (the 16-bit mapped VMA translated to its physical flash LMA, then routed through the UPDI flash mirror), exactly as `read_flash_string()` in `fsm_mapper.c` does. This branch shall be taken before the LLR-RSP-48 advertised-region check (the window is read-only FLASH and always present, so it is exempt from the SRAM-fault gate). When the read is not a mapped-flash read, the existing behaviour is unchanged: the LLR-RSP-48 bounds check runs and, on success, the GDB↔UPDI bit-23 translation selects `addr & GDB_AVR_ADDR_MASK` for data-space reads or `addr | UPDI_FLASH_BASE` for program-space reads. The constants `AVR_MAPPED_FLASH_OFF = 0x8000` and `AVR_MAPPED_FLASH_LEN = 0x8000` shall be defined file-private in `src/gdb_rsp.c`. This makes a flash-resident `.rodata` string reachable through a generic `char *` (e.g. `print stateMachine->currStateName`), which GDB reads as data at `0x80_8xxx`; without the translation such a read returned `E14` (window undescribed) or, if forced, FLMAP-dependent garbage. The capability is avrOS-session only (it requires `flash_lma_off` from the ELF index).

`bp_step_range(int updi_fd, uint32_t lo, uint32_t hi, bool (*should_abort)(void *), void *abort_ctx)` (in the shared core, `src/debug_bp.c`) shall single-step the target while the live PC stays in the half-open byte-address range `[lo, hi)`: each iteration reads the PC (`updi_ocd_read_pc`), returns 0 when `pc < lo || pc >= hi`, returns 1 when the `BP_STEP_RANGE_MAX = 100000` safety cap is reached, else single-steps (`updi_step`) — on a step error it halts the target and returns -1 — and, when `should_abort` is non-NULL, returns 2 if `should_abort(abort_ctx)` is true. It is the protocol-agnostic step loop shared by the GDB-RSP `vCont;r` handler (LLR-RSP-46, which supplies a Ctrl-C/disconnect probe) and the DAP source-line step handlers (LLR-DAP-19, which pass NULL).
