function.title: src/elf_parser.c — ELF/DWARF Adapter (elfutils)
function.name: elf
function.intro: Requirements for the thin elfutils adapter `src/elf_parser.c`: `elf_open()`, `elf_close()`, `elf_find_avros_tables()`, `elf_flash_addr()`, `elf_phys_flash_byte_addr()`, and the DWARF source-line accessors (`elf_dwarf_available()`, `elf_addr_to_line()`, `elf_line_to_addr()`). ELF parsing is delegated to libelf (GElf API); DWARF to libdw.

llr.text: `elf_open()` shall open the file via libelf — `elf_version(EV_CURRENT)` then `elf_begin(fd, ELF_C_READ, NULL)` — and validate it through libelf: `elf_kind() == ELF_K_ELF`, `gelf_getclass() == ELFCLASS32`, and (via the cached header, LLR-ELF-10) `e_machine == EM_AVR` (0x0053). Any validation failure shall cause `elf_open()` to log a warning (including `elf_errmsg()` where applicable), release the libelf handle and fd, and return -1.

trace.name: ELF and DWARF Parsing via elfutils

llr.text: `elf_open()` shall retain the libelf `Elf*` handle in `ctx->elf` for the lifetime of the context and shall access the symbol and string tables through that handle (the GElf API) on demand — it shall NOT copy `.symtab`/`.strtab` into application-owned heap buffers. The `ElfContext` shall therefore expose no `symtab`/`strtab`/`sym_count`/`strtab_size` fields; all symbol enumeration is performed by `elf_find_avros_tables()` (LLR-ELF-03) directly over libelf data.

trace.name: ELF and DWARF Parsing via elfutils

llr.text: `elf_find_avros_tables()` shall locate the first `SHT_SYMTAB` section through libelf (`elf_nextscn`/`gelf_getshdr`), obtain its `Elf_Data` (`elf_getdata`), and perform a single O(sym_count) scan with `gelf_getsym`, resolving each name via `elf_strptr(elf, sh.sh_link, st_name)` and comparing against the 8 avrOS sentinel names defined in SDD §6.3.3 to populate the corresponding fields of `AvrOsSymbolIndex` for each match. The function shall return 0 (success, even if partial) or -1 only on an internal ELF read error.

trace.name: ELF and DWARF Parsing via elfutils

llr.text: `elf_flash_addr()` shall convert an ELF virtual memory address to a physical FLASH word address using the formula `physical_word_addr = (vma - ctx->flash_base) / 2`. The FLASH-resident avrOS table addresses stored in `AvrOsSymbolIndex` shall be translated to their physical FLASH byte address (LMA) via `elf_phys_flash_byte_addr()` (the mapped-flash-window translation, LLR-ELF-08), while the SRAM-resident `currStateMachine` address shall be stored as a raw VMA. `elf_find_avros_tables()` shall additionally record `idx->flash_lma_off = idx->fsm_table_addr - (fsm_start & 0xFFFF)` — the delta from a 16-bit mapped-flash data-space pointer (the 0x8000..0xFFFF `char *` values stored in FSM descriptors and `currStateName`) to its physical FLASH LMA. The `& 0xFFFF` mask is required because `flash_lma_off` is consumed by adding it to 16-bit C pointers (fsm_mapper/monitor name reads, and the RSP `dh_read_mem` mapped-flash path, LLR-RSP-52); avr-gcc 14.2 emits `.rodata`/`FSM_TABLE` at a full mapped-flash VMA (e.g. 0x00a08000), so subtracting the full `fsm_start` VMA would yield a bogus negative delta and misdirect every flash-string read. The result is the same as the legacy 16-bit-VMA convention because masking is a no-op there.

When `elf_find_avros_tables()` completes the symbol scan and fewer than the expected avrOS symbols were found, it shall return 0 (not -1). Fields of `AvrOsSymbolIndex` for absent symbols shall retain their zero-initialised values, and the function shall log an informational message identifying which symbols were not found.

`elf_close()` shall release the elfutils handles in order — `dwarf_end(ctx->dwarf)` (if non-NULL), then `elf_end(ctx->elf)` — and close `ctx->fd`. After returning, `ctx->dwarf` and `ctx->elf` shall be NULL and `ctx->fd` shall be -1. `elf_close()` shall be safe to call on a zero-initialised or partially initialised `ElfContext` (e.g., after a failed `elf_open()`).

`src/elf_parser.c` shall delegate all ELF and DWARF format parsing to elfutils — libelf via the class-independent GElf API for the ELF container, and libdw for DWARF — and shall not hand-decode ELF byte layouts. elfutils is a required build and runtime dependency; the bundled ELF type shim formerly at `src/elf.h` is removed, and ELF32 type definitions (`Elf32_Ehdr`, `Elf32_Phdr`, `EM_AVR`, `PT_LOAD`, etc.) used by this module and its consumers come from the system `<elf.h>` that elfutils requires. The build shall link `-ldw -lelf` unconditionally (no compile-time feature detection).

trace.name: ELF and DWARF Parsing via elfutils

llr.text: `elf_open()` shall walk the ELF program headers via libelf (`elf_getphdrnum()` / `gelf_getphdr()`) and identify `PT_LOAD` segments. The first `PT_LOAD` segment shall be treated as the FLASH load segment: its `p_vaddr` and `p_filesz` shall be stored in `ctx->flash_base` and `ctx->flash_size`. The second `PT_LOAD` shall be the SRAM segment: its `p_vaddr` and `p_filesz` shall be stored in `ctx->sram_base` and `ctx->sram_size`. Each `PT_LOAD`'s `p_vaddr`/`p_paddr`/`p_memsz` shall also be recorded in `ctx->loads[]` (up to `ELF_MAX_PT_LOAD`) for the mapped-flash VMA→LMA translation performed by `elf_phys_flash_byte_addr()`. If fewer than two `PT_LOAD` segments are present the absent values shall remain zero.

`elf_open()` shall best-effort extract the lowercase Microchip part-name string from the `.note.gnu.avr.deviceinfo` ELF note emitted by avr-gcc + Microchip device packs. The parser shall walk every `SHT_NOTE` section via libelf (`elf_nextscn` / `gelf_getshdr` / `elf_getdata`) and scan the note section data for the first NUL-terminated ASCII run starting with `"avr"` followed immediately by an ASCII digit. Up to `ELF_DEVICE_NAME_MAX - 1` (15) bytes shall be copied into the `ElfContext.device_name` field and NUL-terminated. The note-format heuristic — scanning for `"avr<digit>…"` rather than decoding the descriptor's full struct — is intentional, so the parser survives binutils version drift in the descriptor layout. When the note is absent, malformed, or contains no recognised part-name, `device_name` shall remain the empty string the entry path cleared (`ctx->device_name[0] = '\0'`), which `app_main()` (LLR-MAIN-13) treats as "ELF carries no device identification" and which `updi_family_from_partname()` (LLR-UPDI-28) maps to `NULL`. This LLR shall not cause `elf_open()` to fail on any input that already passes the ELF32/EM_AVR validation in LLR-ELF-01.

`elf_open()` shall cache the ELF header via libelf's `elf32_getehdr()` into `ctx->ehdr` (an `Elf32_Ehdr`) so consumers that walk program headers directly from `ctx->fd` — notably `main.c`'s flash-load and verify paths — retain access to `e_phnum` / `e_phoff` / `e_entry`. A NULL return from `elf32_getehdr()` shall be treated as a validation failure (LLR-ELF-01).

trace.name: ELF and DWARF Parsing via elfutils

llr.text: `elf_open()` shall open a libdw handle with `dwarf_begin_elf(ctx->elf, DWARF_C_READ, NULL)` and store it in `ctx->dwarf`; the handle shares the libelf `Elf*`, so `elf_close()` releases it with `dwarf_end()` before `elf_end()` (LLR-ELF-06). A NULL result (the ELF carries no `.debug_*` sections) shall be non-fatal — `ctx->dwarf` stays NULL and `elf_open()` still returns 0. `elf_dwarf_available()` shall return 1 (libdw is always linked, since elfutils is a required dependency).

`elf_addr_to_line()` shall map a code-space byte address to its source `file:line` using libdw: `dwarf_addrdie()` to find the compilation-unit DIE containing the address, then `dwarf_getsrc_die()` and `dwarf_lineno()`/`dwarf_linesrc()`. On success it shall return 0, store the 1-based line in `*line` (when non-NULL), and copy the NUL-terminated source path (truncated to `file_cap`) into `file` (when non-NULL). The source path shall be made **absolute**: DWARF frequently records it relative to the compilation directory (e.g. `../../sys/fsm.c`), which a DAP client cannot open — so when `dwarf_linesrc()` returns a relative path it shall be joined to the CU's `DW_AT_comp_dir` (`dwarf_attr()`/`dwarf_formstring()`); an already-absolute path is copied verbatim. (The lexical join may retain `..` segments, which the client/OS normalises on open.) It shall return -1 — leaving the outputs untouched and never aborting — when `ctx->dwarf` is NULL or the address has no line-table entry.

`elf_line_to_addr()` shall resolve a `file:line` to the first matching code-space byte address using libdw: iterate compilation units with `dwarf_nextcu()`/`dwarf_offdie()`, enumerate each CU's line table with `dwarf_getsrclines()`/`dwarf_onesrcline()`, match on `dwarf_lineno()` and on the requested file by basename (`dwarf_linesrc()`), and return the address from `dwarf_lineaddr()`. On success it shall return 0 and store the address in `*byte_addr`; it shall return -1 when `ctx->dwarf` is NULL or no matching row exists.

`elf_cfi_cfa()` shall return the Canonical-Frame-Address rule at a code-space byte address by interpreting the ELF's `.debug_frame` section directly (libdw's `dwarf_cfi_addrframe()` returns an error on AVR `.debug_frame`). It shall locate `.debug_frame` via libelf (`elf_getshdrstrndx`/`elf_nextscn`/`elf_strptr`), walk its CIE/FDE entries, and on the FDE whose `[initial_location, +address_range)` covers the address, run a minimal CFI state machine over the CIE-initial then FDE instructions up to that PC — tracking only the CFA-defining opcodes (`DW_CFA_def_cfa`/`_register`/`_offset` and their `_sf` forms, plus `advance_loc`/`set_loc` and operand-skipping of the register-save and expression opcodes). On success it shall store the CFA base register in `*cfa_reg` (decoded from `def_cfa_register`; AVR: 28 = the Y pair r28:r29, 32 = SP) and the signed byte offset in `*cfa_offset`, so CFA = value(cfa_reg) + cfa_offset, and return 0. It shall return -1 when the ELF has no `.debug_frame`, the PC is not covered by any FDE, the entry uses 64-bit DWARF or a `z`-augmented/CFA-expression form, or no CFA rule is established.

`elf_var_addr()` shall resolve a variable `name` visible at a code byte address `pc` to its 16-bit data-space address, byte size, and signedness, evaluating its DWARF location against live frame registers (`ElfFrameRegs`: the CFA, the Y pair r28:r29, and SP). It shall obtain the CU via `dwarf_addrdie()`, the lexical scope chain via `dwarf_getscopes()`, and the matching variable DIE via `dwarf_getscopevar()` (which searches locals/parameters then outward to file scope). It shall decode the single-operation location forms avr-gcc -O0 emits: `DW_OP_addr` → the absolute (data-space) address; `DW_OP_breg28`/`DW_OP_bregx 28` + offset → `fr->y + offset`; `DW_OP_bregx 32` + offset → `fr->sp + offset`; and `DW_OP_fbreg` + offset → `fr->cfa + offset` when the enclosing subprogram's `DW_AT_frame_base` is `DW_OP_call_frame_cfa`. The result address shall be masked to 16 bits (the SRAM data space). Size/signedness shall come from the peeled (`dwarf_peel_type`) `DW_AT_type` — `dwarf_bytesize()` clamped to 1..4 (default 2) and `DW_AT_encoding` (`DW_ATE_signed`/`signed_char` ⇒ signed). It shall return 0 on success, or -1 with no DWARF, when `name` is not in scope, or for an unsupported location/type form.

`elf_addr_to_func()` shall resolve a code byte address to the name of the enclosing function. It shall obtain the CU via `dwarf_addrdie()` and the lexical scope chain via `dwarf_getscopes()`, find the innermost `DW_TAG_subprogram` scope, and copy its `dwarf_diename()` into the caller's `name` buffer (NUL-terminated, truncated to `cap`). It shall return 0 on success, or -1 when the ELF lacks DWARF or `pc` is inside no subprogram (e.g. the C-runtime frame above `main`), so the DAP front-end can fall back to the raw address for the frame name.

`elf_var_enum()` shall enumerate the variables visible at a code byte address in a scope. For `ELF_SCOPE_LOCALS` it shall walk every lexical scope containing the PC (`dwarf_getscopes`), and for each `DW_TAG_subprogram`/`lexical_block`/`inlined_subroutine` scope list its direct `DW_TAG_variable`/`DW_TAG_formal_parameter` children whose location resolves against the live `ElfFrameRegs`. For `ELF_SCOPE_GLOBALS` it shall list the CU's direct `DW_TAG_variable` children with a `DW_OP_addr` location. Each entry is `{name, 16-bit data-space addr, type DIE offset}`; the location is decoded by a shared `eval_var_loc()` helper (DW_OP_addr / breg28 (Y) / bregx32 (SP) / fbreg (CFA)). Returns the count (capped at `max`), or -1 with no DWARF.

`elf_type_render()` shall render the value at (`addr`, `type_off`) to a human string, fetching target bytes through a caller-supplied `ElfMemRead` callback (keeping elf_parser hardware-agnostic). It shall peel typedef/const/volatile (`dwarf_peel_type`) and switch on the type tag: base types by `DW_AT_encoding` (signed/unsigned with sign-extension, char as `N 'c'`, boolean as true/false, 4-byte float via `%g`); pointers as `0x%0*x`; enumerations by matching `DW_AT_const_value` to an enumerator name; structures/unions inline as `{member = value, …}` and arrays as `{v0, v1, …}` recursed to a bounded depth (≤ 3, arrays capped with an ellipsis). It shall set `*expandable` true for aggregates. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

`elf_type_children()` shall list the members or elements of the aggregate at (`addr`, `type_off`) as child `ElfVar`s. For a struct/union it shall emit one entry per `DW_TAG_member` — name, `addr + DW_AT_data_member_location` (constant or `DW_OP_plus_uconst`), and the member's type offset. For an array it shall derive the element type, element size (`dwarf_bytesize` of the peeled element type), and count (`DW_AT_count`, else `DW_AT_upper_bound + 1` of the `DW_TAG_subrange_type`) and emit `[i]` at `addr + i*elem_size`. Returns the count (capped at `max`), or -1 when the type is not an aggregate.

`elf_var_find()` shall resolve a variable `name` visible at a PC (local/parameter via `dwarf_getscopevar` + the frame regs, else file-scope global) to its data-space address and DWARF type DIE offset — the entry point for `evaluate` base identifiers. Returns 0 on success, -1 when not in scope or with no DWARF.

`elf_type_size()` shall return the byte size of the peeled type at `type_off` (`dwarf_bytesize`), clamped to 1..4 and defaulting to 2 for an absent/unknown type, so `setVariable` writes the correct scalar width.

`elf_line_range()` shall return the half-open code-space byte-address range `[*lo, *hi)` of the line-table row covering `byte_addr`: it locates the CU with `dwarf_addrdie()`, enumerates the rows with `dwarf_getsrclines()` / `dwarf_onesrcline()` / `dwarf_lineaddr()`, and sets `*lo` to the greatest row address `<= byte_addr` and `*hi` to the smallest row address `> byte_addr` (computed without assuming the table is address-sorted). It shall return 0 on success, or -1 when the ELF lacks DWARF, the address is in no CU, or no following row bounds the range (the caller then falls back to a single step). This is the address span a DAP source-line step single-steps within — the analogue of the range GDB sends on `vCont;r`.

`fsm_build_thread_list()` shall read `idx->fsm_table_count` consecutive 9-byte `fsmStateMachineDescr_t` records from the FLASH address `idx->fsm_table_addr` via `updi_mem_read()`. Each descriptor carries a 2-byte `name` pointer (FLASH), a 2-byte `stateMachine` pointer (SRAM, or NULL for an initializer slot that shall be skipped), a 2-byte `handler` function pointer, a 1-byte `priority`, and a 2-byte `instance`. The FLASH addresses (`fsm_table_addr` and the per-entry `name` pointers) are physical byte LMAs / translated by `idx->flash_lma_off` before the UPDI flash read, because the AVR-Dx mapped-flash window FLMAP is not applied to linear UPDI flash reads. For each non-NULL `stateMachine` pointer, the function shall read the 2-byte `currStateName` pointer at offset 0 of `fsmStateMachine_t` and resolve it (NUL-terminated; a non-printable byte is treated as the terminator) into `thread->state_name`; a NULL pointer (FSM not yet dispatched) yields an empty state name. A UPDI read failure at any point shall cause the function to return -1.

`fsm_build_thread_list()` shall read the 2-byte SRAM value at `idx->current_fsm_addr` (avrOS `currStateMachine`) and compare it against each retained FSM entry's `stateMachine` pointer. The matching entry shall have `thread->is_active = true` and its identifier stored in `ctx->active_id`. If no entry matches, `ctx->active_id` shall be set to 0.

function.title: src/monitor.c — avrOS System Introspection
function.name: monitor
function.intro: Requirements for `monitor_dispatch()` and its static sub-command helpers `cmd_events()` and `cmd_queues()`.

llr.text: `monitor_dispatch()` shall hex-decode the ASCII-hex-encoded `cmd` string (pairs of hex digit characters) into a plain-text command string before any prefix or sub-command matching is attempted. An odd-length or invalid hex-digit sequence shall be treated as an unrecognised command.

`monitor_dispatch()` shall verify that the decoded command string begins with the prefix `"avros "` (case-sensitive, including the trailing space). If the prefix does not match, the function shall send a usage-hint O-packet to the GDB console and return -2.

`cmd_events()` shall call `updi_mem_read()` to read `idx->event_count` consecutive 4-byte `evntDescriptor_t` records from FLASH at `idx->event_table_addr`. For each descriptor it shall dereference the `name` pointer (FLASH) to read the event's NUL-terminated display name (up to 31 chars) and the `status` pointer (SRAM) to read the 1-byte status flag, then append a line of the form `" <name>: <status>\n"` and send the complete buffer as RSP O-packets.

`cmd_queues()` shall call `updi_mem_read()` to read `idx->queue_count` consecutive 10-byte `queDescriptor_t` records from FLASH at `idx->queue_table_addr`. For each descriptor it shall extract and format the `capacity` and `sizeOfElement` fields as a one-line entry and send the complete table as RSP O-packets.

All monitor output shall be assembled into a temporary buffer of at most 512 bytes, hex-encoded (each ASCII byte converted to 2 hex characters per RSP O-packet spec), and transmitted to the GDB client as one or more RSP O-packets via `rsp_send_packet()`.

`monitor_dispatch()` and all of its static helpers (`cmd_events()`, `cmd_queues()`) shall use `updi_mem_read()` exclusively for all target memory access. None of these functions shall call `updi_halt()`, ensuring that monitor commands never interrupt firmware execution.

`monitor_dispatch_ex(int rsp_fd, RspContext *ctx, const char *cmd)` shall be the top-level entry for `qRcmd` packets and shall hex-decode `cmd` into a writable buffer of at least 256 bytes, then dispatch on the first whitespace-stripped token. If the token is `avros` followed by a space the call shall be forwarded verbatim to the legacy `monitor_dispatch()` so all pre-existing `monitor avros …` sub-commands keep working unchanged. Recognised top-level verbs are `reset`, `halt`, `go`, `erase`, `chip-erase`, `version`, `bp-mode`, and `help`. Any other first token shall emit an O-packet `"usage: monitor <reset|halt|go|erase|chip-erase|version|bp-mode|help|avros …>\n"` and return -2.

The `monitor reset` verb shall call `updi_enter_debug(ctx->updi_fd)` (issuing the OCD KEY + ASI_RESET_REQ pulse and waiting for the STOPPED bit so the CPU is halted at the reset vector), discard all hardware-breakpoint shadow entries via `rsp_hw_bp_clear_all(ctx)`, invalidate the FSM snapshot cache via `fsm_invalidate(ctx->fsm)` when `ctx->fsm` is non-NULL, emit one diagnostic O-packet line `"target reset, halted at reset vector\n"`, and return 0 so `dh_monitor` appends the trailing `OK`.

`monitor_dispatch()` shall route the decoded sub-command `tasks` to `cmd_tasks()`, which builds the FSM snapshot via `fsm_build_thread_list()` and emits one O-packet line per FSM (an active marker, the FSM name, and the current state name, or `(init)` when `currStateName` is NULL), returning 0. When no FSMs are registered it emits a single "(no FSMs registered)" line.

The `monitor halt` verb shall call `updi_halt(ctx->updi_fd)` and then emit the same stop-reply packet shape used by the step/continue paths — `T05thread:<id>;` where `<id>` is `fsm_get_active_thread(ctx->fsm)` (or 1 when no FSM mapping is available) — via `rsp_send_packet()`. The verb shall return -3 so `dh_monitor` suppresses the trailing `OK` and the GDB client sees exactly one packet per halt.

The `monitor go` verb shall call `updi_run(ctx->updi_fd)`, emit a diagnostic O-packet `"target running\n"`, and return 0. The subsequent stop-reply is emitted by the existing poll loop when the CPU next halts; the verb itself does not synthesise one.

The `monitor erase` verb (alias `monitor chip-erase`) shall consult `ctx->allow_erase` before issuing any UPDI traffic. When the flag is zero, the verb shall emit one diagnostic O-packet `"monitor erase: refused — launch the server with --allow-erase to enable.\n"` and return -1 so `dh_monitor` sends an `E22` error packet. When the flag is set the verb shall call `updi_chip_erase(ctx->updi_fd)`, then re-enter OCD via `updi_enter_debug()`, discard all BP/WP shadow entries, invalidate the FSM snapshot cache, emit a confirmation O-packet, and return 0.

The `monitor version` verb shall emit one O-packet of the form `"avrOSdb <version> (built <date>)\n"` where `<version>` is the compile-time string `AVROSDB_VERSION` (supplied by the Makefile via `-DAVROSDB_VERSION='"$(VERSION)"'`) and `<date>` is the standard `__DATE__` macro. It shall return 0.

The `monitor bp-mode <arg>` verb shall accept exactly three argument tokens: `auto` (sets `ctx->bp_mode = RSP_BP_MODE_AUTO`, the default — prefer a free HW comparator, fall back to the SW FLASH-`BREAK` patch), `sw` (sets `ctx->bp_mode = RSP_BP_MODE_SW` — force the FLASH patch for every `Z0`), and `hw-only` (sets `ctx->bp_mode = RSP_BP_MODE_HW_ONLY` — alias `Z0` to the HW comparators). With no argument it shall report the current setting (`auto`, `sw`, or `hw-only`). Any other argument shall emit an error O-packet (`argument must be 'auto', 'sw' or 'hw-only'`) and return -2. The mode persists for the lifetime of the server process and influences how `Z0` packets are routed (HLR-054).

trace.name: True Software Breakpoints via FLASH BREAK Opcode

llr.text: The `monitor help` verb shall emit one O-packet per recognised verb, each line briefly summarising the verb's syntax and side-effects, in the order: `reset`, `halt`, `go`, `erase`, `chip-erase`, `version`, `bp-mode`, `help`, `avros events`, `avros queues`. After the last line it shall return 0 so `dh_monitor` terminates the output with `OK`.

function.title: Makefile and Documentation
function.name: inst
function.intro: Requirements for the Makefile installation targets (`install`, `uninstall`, `check-tools`, `bundle`) and the documentation deliverables (`doc/UserManual.md`, `doc/avrOSdb.1`). Bundle artefacts are written to `dist/`.

llr.text: The Makefile shall provide a `check-tools` target that tests for the presence of every required host tool: `gcc` (or `cc`), `make`, `avr-gcc`, and `avr-nm`. For each absent tool the target shall print a diagnostic message to `stderr` naming the missing tool and then exit with status 1. The target shall exit with status 0 only when all required tools are found.

The Makefile `install` target shall accept a `PREFIX` variable (default `/usr/local`) and install: the compiled `avrOSdb` binary to `$(PREFIX)/bin/avrOSdb` and the man page `doc/avrOSdb.1` to `$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1/avrOSdb.1`. The target shall create any missing intermediate directories using `install -d`. The binary shall be installed with mode 0755 and the man page with mode 0644.

The Makefile `uninstall` target shall remove `$(PREFIX)/bin/avrOSdb` and `$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1/avrOSdb.1` using `rm -f`. The target shall be idempotent: running it when the files are already absent shall exit with status 0 without error.

The project shall include a user manual at `doc/UserManual.md` documenting: (1) prerequisites (required host tools and their minimum versions), (2) build instructions (`make`, `make test`), (3) connection wiring for the UPDI adapter (1 kΩ resistor on UPDI pin, serial adapter TX/RX orientation), (4) launch invocation and all CLI options, and (5) at least two complete usage examples (one with `--load`, one without).

trace.name: User Manual and Unix Man Page

llr.text: The project shall include a Unix man page at `doc/avrOSdb.1` in `groff`/`troff` format. The man page shall contain at minimum: NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS (one entry per CLI flag), OPERANDS, EXIT STATUS, EXAMPLES, and SEE ALSO sections. The man page shall be parseable by `man -l doc/avrOSdb.1` without error or warning on Linux.

trace.name: User Manual and Unix Man Page

llr.text: The Makefile `bundle` target shall produce a Debian binary package at `dist/avrOSdb_$(VERSION)_amd64.deb` using `dpkg-deb --build`. The package staging tree shall install the binary to `usr/bin/avrOSdb` (mode 0755) and the man page to `usr/share/man/man1/avrOSdb.1` (mode 0644). The `DEBIAN/control` file shall declare at minimum: `Package: avrOSdb`, `Version`, `Architecture: amd64`, `Maintainer`, and `Description` fields.

The Makefile `bundle` target shall produce an RPM binary package at `dist/avrOSdb-$(VERSION)-1.x86_64.rpm` using `rpmbuild`. A `.spec` file shall be generated in the build tree containing at minimum: `Name`, `Version`, `Release: 1`, `Summary`, `License`, `%description`, `%install`, and `%files` sections. The `%files` section shall list `/usr/bin/avrOSdb` and `/usr/share/man/man1/avrOSdb.1`.

The Makefile `bundle` target shall produce a Homebrew formula at `dist/avrOSdb.rb`. The formula shall be a valid Ruby file usable with `brew install --formula dist/avrOSdb.rb`. It shall define at minimum: `desc`, `homepage`, `url`, `sha256`, `version`, `license`, and an `install` block that places the binary using `bin.install` and the man page using `man1.install`.

The VS Code companion extension (`tools/vscode/avrosdb-dap`) shall, in `package.json`, contribute a `viewsContainers.activitybar` entry `avrosDebug` (title "avrOS", icon `media/avros.svg`) and six `views` under it: `avrosVariables`, `avrosCallStack`, `avrosBreakpoints`, `avrosStateMachines`, `avrosEvents`, `avrosQueues`. `extension.js` shall register a `TreeDataProvider` for each (`registerTreeDataProvider`): the State Machines / Events / Queues providers shall populate from `session.customRequest("avrosdb/fsmList" | "avrosdb/eventList" | "avrosdb/queueList")` on the active `avrosdb` session; the Variables provider shall proxy `threads`→`stackTrace`→`scopes`→`variables` with lazy aggregate expansion; the Call Stack provider shall proxy `threads`→`stackTrace`; and the Breakpoints provider shall list `vscode.debug.breakpoints`. A `DebugAdapterTracker` shall refresh the views on the DAP `stopped` event and clear the stack/variables snapshots on `continued`; an `avrosdb.refresh` command shall force a manual refresh. The activity-bar icon asset `media/avros.svg` shall be present in the extension.

`extension.js` shall register (`registerDebugConfigurationProvider`) a `DebugConfigurationProvider` for the `avrosdb` type whose `provideDebugConfigurations()` returns a self-starting `launch` configuration and whose `resolveDebugConfiguration()` seeds that default for an empty config and resolves the `avrOSdb` binary path — building it with `make` or falling back to `PATH` when it is absent, aborting the launch when unresolved. A `DebugAdapterDescriptorFactory` (`registerDebugAdapterDescriptorFactory`) shall, for a `launch` request, spawn `avrOSdb --dap --port <port> <serial> <elf>`, wait for the `listening on` banner (with a timeout fallback), connect via `DebugAdapterServer`, and kill the spawned server when the session terminates. The Makefile shall provide a `package-vscode` target that builds `dist/avrosdb-dap-$(VERSION).vsix` via `vsce`/`npx`, requiring no Node tooling from `make` or `make test`.

function.title: tests/hw/hw_test.c — On-Target Hardware Integration Test Harness
function.name: hwtest
function.intro: Requirements for the manual-only on-target hardware integration test program. The harness links against `src/updi.c` (and, for Group D, spawns the production `build/avrOSdb` binary via `fork`/`execl`) and runs against live AVR-Dx silicon connected via a UART/UPDI adapter.

llr.text: `tests/hw/hw_test.c` shall accept its configuration from environment variables and from long-form command-line options. Recognised settings: `HW_PORT` / `--port` (serial device path; default `/dev/ttyUSB0`), `HW_DEVICE_ID` / `--device-id` (expected 24-bit SIGROW signature as a hex literal; default `0x1E970A` for AVR128DA48), `HW_SRAM_ADDR` / `--sram-addr` (16-bit SRAM probe address; default `0x7000`), `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR` / `--flash-page` (FLASH page-aligned address used by Group C; default `0x1FE00`), `HW_RSP_PORT` / `--rsp-port` (TCP port for Group D; default `1234`), `HW_TEST_ELF` / `--elf` (optional ELF binary passed to the spawned RSP server in Group D), `HW_ADDR_24BIT` / `--addr-24bit` (boolean; when true, FLASH access uses the 24-bit UPDI addressing path), and `HW_VERBOSE` / `--verbose` (boolean; enables per-byte tracing). CLI flags shall override the corresponding environment values.

Group A (read-only link probes) shall execute the following ordered checks against the live target: **A1** open the serial port and perform the UPDI cold-start handshake (BREAK + SYNCH); **A2** call `updi_read_device_info()` and capture the result for downstream assertions; **A3** verify that the captured `DEVICEID0..2` bytes match the configured `HW_DEVICE_ID`; **A4** verify that the SIGROW signature is not all-zero and not all-`0xFF`; **A5** verify that `SYSCFG.REVID` is non-zero; **A6** verify that the 10-byte `SERNUM` field is not all-zero and not all-`0xFF`; **A7** verify that `ASI_SYS_STATUS.NVMPROG` is clear (target is not stuck in a programming session). Each individual check shall be reported as a separate `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]` line.

Group B (non-destructive SRAM round-trips) shall execute the following ordered checks at `HW_SRAM_ADDR`: **B0** single-byte write/read; **B1** 64-byte buffer write/read; **B1a** SIGROW read repeated twice and compared (isolates the read path from the write path); **B1b** write 64 bytes of constant `0xAA` then read back (value-independence check); **B1c** write a known pattern once then read it back twice and compare both reads (detects live CPU writes to the probed region — on failure the harness shall hint that the operator pick a different `--sram-addr` / `HW_SRAM_ADDR`); **B2** 600-byte buffer write/read (exercises multi-chunk transfer); **B3** when `HW_ADDR_24BIT` is true, a small write/read at the configured FLASH page address using the 24-bit UPDI addressing path. None of the Group B steps shall modify FLASH.

Group C (destructive FLASH write/verify) shall execute only when the environment variable `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES` is set; otherwise the group shall be reported as skipped. When confirmed, Group C shall perform: **C1** erase the FLASH page at `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR`, then write a deterministic pattern via the NVM controller; **C2** read the page back and verify a byte-for-byte match against the written pattern. The harness shall enter and leave the NVM programming session cleanly (NVMPROG key in, NVMPROG key cleared on exit) so that subsequent Group A/B checks find the target in a non-programming state.

Group D (RSP server spawn-and-probe) shall execute only when the environment variable `HW_TEST_RSP=YES` is set; otherwise the group shall be reported as skipped. When enabled, Group D shall `fork` and `execl` the production `build/avrOSdb` binary with the configured serial port and optional `HW_TEST_ELF`, wait briefly for the server's TCP listener to bind on `HW_RSP_PORT`, then perform: **D1** connect a TCP client to `127.0.0.1:HW_RSP_PORT` and verify the connection is accepted; **D2** send an RSP `qSupported` packet (`$qSupported#37`) and verify a non-empty, properly-framed RSP reply is received. The harness shall terminate the spawned server cleanly (SIGTERM + `waitpid`) on completion or on test failure.

The Makefile shall expose four targets that drive `tests/hw/hw_test.c`: `hw-test` runs Groups A+B (read-only); `hw-test-nvm` runs Groups A+B+C and forwards `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES`; `hw-test-rsp` runs Groups A+B+D and forwards `HW_TEST_RSP=YES`; `hw-test-all` runs all four groups. Every hw-test variable (`HW_PORT`, `HW_DEVICE_ID`, `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR`, `HW_RSP_PORT`, `HW_TEST_ELF`, `HW_ADDR_24BIT`, `HW_VERBOSE`) shall be passed through to the child process via the target recipes. None of these targets shall be a dependency of the default `make test` target or be built by `make all`. The `make help` output shall document each variable, its default, and a brief description.

Group F (Phase 9 link diagnostics) shall execute three on-target checks: **F1** call `updi_probe_baud(cfg->port, 8, visitor, NULL)`, record each rung's `{baud, errors, samples}`, and PASS if the chosen rate is ≥ 19200 baud (the slowest rung in the ladder); **F2** with the harness UPDI fd re-opened at the configured baud, read the FUSES window and the 4-byte LOCK window via `updi_nvm_read()`, format them via `updi_format_fuses()` into a 2 KiB buffer, and PASS if the output contains the literal substrings `WDTCFG`, `OSCCFG`, `SYSCFG0`, and `Lock:`; **F3** (destructive, gated by `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES`) fork the production `build/avrOSdb --prog --erase --baud <N> <port> <elf>` against the bench ELF, capture the child's stdout/stderr, and PASS if `WEXITSTATUS == 0` AND the captured output contains the literal `verify: OK`. F1 needs the harness UPDI fd closed before running (so the probe can open its own fd at each rung); the harness shall close fd before F1, re-open at `cfg->baud` for F2, then close again before F3.

trace.name: Auto-Baud Link-Quality Probe in Device Mode

llr.text: Group D's RSP-server smoke checks shall, after the existing D1–D3 (TCP accept, qSupported, Ctrl-C interrupt) pass, additionally exercise the Phase-10 RSP surface against the same spawned `build/avrOSdb` child over the same TCP socket: **D4** issue a framed `qC` packet and PASS if the reply payload begins with `QC` followed by a thread id; **D5** issue `qOffsets` and PASS if the reply payload begins with `Text=`; **D6** issue `qRcmd,696e666f` (the hex-encoded `monitor info` verb) and PASS if the reply payload is non-empty and does not begin with `E` (an error code); **D7** issue `Z2,<sram_addr|0x800000>,1` then `z2,<sram_addr|0x800000>,1` and PASS only if both replies are the empty packet (`$#00`, payload length zero) — the silicon has no data-watchpoint hardware (HLR-056); **D8** issue `vRun;` and PASS if the reply payload begins with `T` (any stop signal); **D9** (destructive, opt-in via `--with-nvm`) issue `vFlashErase:<flash_page>,200` followed by `vFlashDone` and PASS if both replies are `OK`; **D10** (destructive, opt-in via `--with-nvm`, must be ordered after D9 so the page baseline is 0xFF) issue `Z0,<flash_page>,2`, then read back with `m<flash_page>,2` expecting the 4-character hex literal `9895` (AVR `BREAK` opcode little-endian), then issue `z0,<flash_page>,2`, and PASS only when all three exchanges produce the expected replies. When `--with-rsp` is not set, D4–D10 shall be skipped together with D1–D3; when `--with-nvm` is not set, only D9–D10 shall be reported as SKIP. A short helper `send_rsp(fd, payload)` shall compute the modulo-256 RSP checksum and ship `+$<payload>#XX`; a companion `rsp_payload(buf, n, &p, &len)` shall locate the `$…#` payload in a raw reply buffer.

function.title: src/dap.c — Debug Adapter Protocol Front-End
function.name: dap
function.intro: Requirements for the DAP front-end (`src/dap.c`), a protocol front-end over the shared debug core parallel to `src/gdb_rsp.c`. Phase 16 implements the wire transport: a self-contained JSON codec and the Content-Length message framing. The accept/dispatch loop and the lifecycle/request handlers are added across Phases 16–19.

llr.text: `dj_parse()` shall tokenise a JSON text into a caller-supplied flat, pre-order array of `dj_tok_t` via recursive descent, returning the token count on success or -1 on malformed input or token-array overflow. Each token records its `type` (OBJECT/ARRAY/STRING/NUMBER/TRUE/FALSE/NULL), the source byte range `[start, end)` (for STRING, the content between the quotes), the `size` (OBJECT member count / ARRAY element count), and `next` (the index of the token following its entire subtree). The accessors shall include: `dj_member()` returning the value-token index for an object member by key (or -1); `dj_streq()` testing a STRING token against a C string; `dj_strcpy()` copying a STRING token's content into a bounded buffer while decoding the JSON escapes `\" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t` and `\uXXXX` (code points < 0x80 as the byte, otherwise `?`); and `dj_long()` parsing a NUMBER token as a `long`.

`dj_escape()` shall append a C string to a caller buffer as a JSON-escaped string body (without surrounding quotes), always NUL-terminating and never writing past `cap`. It shall emit the short escapes for `"`, `\\`, newline, carriage-return, tab, backspace, and form-feed, and shall emit any other control byte (< 0x20) as `\uXXXX`. It shall stop appending rather than overflow when the buffer would be exceeded.

`dap_read_message()` shall read one DAP message off a file descriptor: it shall consume CRLF-terminated header lines until a blank line, parsing the `Content-Length:` value (case-insensitive header name), then read exactly that many body bytes into the caller buffer and NUL-terminate it, setting `*out_len`. It shall read the body with exact-length reads so it never consumes bytes belonging to the next message. It shall return 1 when a message was read, 0 on EOF / peer close before any data, and -1 on read error, a missing/negative `Content-Length`, or a length that does not fit the caller buffer (`>= cap`). It shall retry `read()` on `EINTR`.

`dap_write_message()` shall write one DAP message to a file descriptor as `Content-Length: <len>\r\n\r\n` followed by the `len` body bytes, using length-complete writes that retry on `EINTR`. It shall return 0 on success and -1 on write error.

`dap_serve()` shall accept one client on the listener via `rsp_accept()`, allocate a `DAP_MSG_MAX` receive buffer, and run a dispatch loop that, each iteration, waits with `select()` (≈200 ms timeout) on the client fd so the loop re-checks the quit flag without busy-waiting. On a readable socket it shall call `dap_read_message()` and route the message to `dap_dispatch()`; it shall exit the loop on EOF (read returns 0), on a framing/read error (-1), when `dap_dispatch()` returns 1 (disconnect/terminate), or when the quit flag is set. On exit it shall free the buffer and `rsp_close()` the client. It shall return 0 on a clean shutdown and -1 on a fatal accept/read error.

`dap_dispatch()` shall tokenise the message, require a top-level OBJECT with a `command` member (ignoring anything else), read the request `seq`, and route on the command string. It shall emit replies through file-private builders that produce well-formed DAP messages with a monotonically increasing outgoing `seq`: a `response` builder (`request_seq`, `command`, `success`, optional `body`), an error builder (`success:false` + `message`), and an `event` builder (`event` + optional `body`); all dynamic string fields shall be JSON-escaped via `dj_escape()`. It shall return 0 to continue the session, 1 to disconnect, or -1 on a write failure.

`dap_dispatch()` shall implement the Phase-16 lifecycle commands: `initialize` → a capabilities response (`supportsConfigurationDoneRequest:true`) followed by the `initialized` event; `launch` / `attach` → success; `setExceptionBreakpoints` → success; `setBreakpoints` → success with an empty `breakpoints` array (real installation deferred to Phase 18); `configurationDone` → halt the target (`updi_halt()` when `updi_fd >= 0`) and emit a `stopped` event (`reason:"entry"`, `threadId:1`, `allThreadsStopped:true`); `threads` → one thread `{id:1,name:"cpu"}`; `disconnect` / `terminate` → resume the target (`updi_run()` when `updi_fd >= 0`), reply success, and return 1. Any other command shall receive a `success:false` response with an explanatory `message`. All UPDI side effects shall be guarded by `updi_fd >= 0` so the dispatch is exercisable without hardware.

`dap_dispatch()` shall implement the Phase-17 execution-control commands. `continue`: send a `{allThreadsContinued:true}` response and a `continued` event (`{threadId:1,allThreadsContinued:true}`), then — when `updi_fd >= 0` — call `updi_run()`; on success set `dap_session.running = true` (so `dap_serve()` polls for the halt), and on a run failure emit `stopped` (reason `breakpoint`) instead. `pause`: call `updi_halt()` (when `updi_fd >= 0`), clear `running`, reply success, and emit `stopped` reason `pause`. `stepIn` / `next` / `stepOut`: clear `running`, reply success, perform source-line-granular stepping via `dap_step_line()` / `dap_step_over()` / `dap_step_out()` (LLR-DAP-19) when `updi_fd >= 0`, and emit `stopped` reason `step`. `threads`: reply one thread `{id:1,name:"cpu"}`. `configurationDone` shall additionally clear `running` and emit its `stopped` via the shared helper with reason `entry`. `terminate` shall emit a `terminated` event before its success response (then return 1); `disconnect` returns 1 without the event. A shared `dap_emit_stopped(reason)` helper shall format the `stopped` event body (`{reason,threadId:1,allThreadsStopped:true}`) for all reasons. `dap_serve()` shall, on an idle `select()` tick while `running` and `updi_fd >= 0`, call `updi_ocd_poll_halted(updi_fd, 1)` and — on a halted result — clear `running` and emit `stopped` reason `breakpoint`; a poll I/O error shall end the session with a diagnostic. The idle tick shall be shortened while `running` so a halt surfaces promptly. All UPDI side effects shall be guarded by `updi_fd >= 0`.

trace.name: DAP Execution Control, Stop Events & Shallow stackTrace

llr.text: `dap_dispatch()` shall serve a shallow `stackTrace` via a private `dap_handle_stack_trace()` helper: when `updi_fd >= 0`, read the live PC with `updi_ocd_read_pc()`; when an `ElfContext` is present, resolve the PC to `file:line` with the libdw accessor `elf_addr_to_line()`. It shall emit a response `{stackFrames:[<frame0>],totalFrames:1}` where frame 0 is `{id:0,name:"0x<pc>",line:<n>,column:1,instructionPointerReference:"0x<pc>",source:{name:<basename>,path:<file>}}` with the `source` object and `line` present only when the DWARF lookup succeeds; otherwise a single frame with `line:0` and no `source` (so the client always has a valid stack). The source `name`/`path` strings shall be JSON-escaped via `dj_escape()`. `scopes` shall reply `{scopes:[]}` (frame variables are Phase 19). Real frame names and deeper frames (DWARF CFI unwinding) are Phase 18. The handler shall touch no target when `updi_fd < 0`, so it is unit-testable over a socketpair.

trace.name: DAP Execution Control, Stop Events & Shallow stackTrace

llr.text: `dap_dispatch()` shall serve `setBreakpoints` via a private `dap_handle_set_breakpoints()` helper, and `dap_session` shall carry the shared breakpoint state (`hw_bp_addr[2]`, `hw_bp_pinned[2]`, `sw_bp[RSP_MAX_SW_BREAKPOINTS]`, `bp_mode`, `pc_dirty`) plus a `bps[DAP_MAX_BREAKPOINTS]` table (`id`, `addr`, `line`, `verified`, `in_use`, `source`, `condition`) and `next_bp_id`; `dap_bp_reset()` shall initialise it (HW shadow slots `HW_BP_SLOT_EMPTY`, `bp_mode = RSP_BP_MODE_AUTO`, `next_bp_id = 1`) and shall be called at session start (`dap_serve`). The handler shall: (1) read `arguments.source.path` (falling back to `name`); (2) remove every existing breakpoint whose `source` equals that path — `bp_remove()` per installed entry — so the call replaces that source's set; (3) for each element of `arguments.breakpoints`, read `line` and optional `condition`, resolve `line` to a code byte address via `elf_line_to_addr(elf, path, line, &addr)`, and — when resolved and `updi_fd >= 0` — install it with `bp_insert(updi_fd, hw_bp_addr, hw_bp_pinned, sw_bp, bp_mode, &pc_dirty, '0', addr)` (verified iff `BP_OK`); record the entry (assigning `id = next_bp_id++`); (4) reply `{"breakpoints":[{"id":<id>,"verified":<bool>,"line":<line>}, …]}` in request order. When the target later halts while `running`, `dap_serve()` shall emit the `stopped` event via `dap_emit_stopped_breakpoint()`, which reads the live PC and, for every `bps[]` entry whose `addr` matches, includes its id in `hitBreakpointIds` (falling back to a plain reason-`breakpoint` stop when none match). `disconnect`/`terminate` shall `bp_remove()` every installed breakpoint before `updi_run()`. A sibling `dap_handle_set_instruction_breakpoints()` shall serve `setInstructionBreakpoints`: parse each entry's `instructionReference` (+ optional `offset`) to an address, install via `bp_insert('0', addr)`, mark the table entry with `line == -1`, and replace the prior instruction-breakpoint set (entries with `line == -1`) each call; `initialize` shall advertise `supportsInstructionBreakpoints`. Conditional-expression evaluation is LLR-DAP-12. All target side effects are guarded by `updi_fd >= 0`.

trace.name: True Software Breakpoints via Flash BREAK Opcode

llr.text: `dap_handle_stack_trace()` shall return the full call stack by unwinding through `.debug_frame` CFI via a private `dap_unwind()` helper. `dap_unwind()` shall read the innermost frame's live state — PC (`updi_ocd_read_pc`), SP (`updi_ocd_read_sp`), and the Y pair r28/r29 (`updi_ocd_read_gpr`) — then iterate: obtain the CFA rule at the current PC with `elf_cfi_cfa()` (LLR-ELF-14), compute `CFA = (cfa_reg == 32 ? SP : Y) + cfa_offset` (16-bit SRAM address), and recover the caller from target memory (`updi_mem_read`) using AVR conventions — the return-address word at [CFA-1, CFA] (high byte at CFA-1, low at CFA; caller byte PC = word << 1) and the caller's saved Y as r28@CFA-2 / r29@CFA-3. Each iteration sets the next frame's PC = caller byte PC, SP = CFA, Y = caller Y. It shall stop when the return word is 0, when the byte PC is outside `[0, flash_size)`, when no CFI covers the PC (`elf_cfi_cfa` returns -1 — e.g. the C-runtime frame above `main`), when the CFA fails to advance, or at `DAP_MAX_FRAMES`. `dap_handle_stack_trace()` shall format each recovered PC with `dap_format_frame()` — the frame `name` is the enclosing function from `elf_addr_to_func()` (LLR-ELF-16; the raw `0x…` address when no subprogram covers it) and the source is `file:line` via `elf_addr_to_line()`, both JSON-escaped — into `{stackFrames:[…],totalFrames:n}`, frame ids ascending from 0. With no target or no DWARF (`dap_unwind()` returns 0) it shall fall back to the single innermost frame so the client always has a valid stack. When `AVROSDB_DAP_UNWIND_LOG` is set, `dap_unwind()` shall emit a per-frame diagnostic to stderr.

`dap_dispatch()`/`dap_serve()` shall honour a DAP breakpoint `condition` (stored per `bps[]` entry by LLR-DAP-10). A private `dap_eval_condition()` shall parse `<ident> <relop> <integer>` (relop `== != < <= > >=`; integer via `strtol(...,0)` so decimal and `0x` hex are accepted), resolve `ident` with `elf_var_addr()` (LLR-ELF-15) using the live frame registers from a `dap_frame0()` helper (PC/SP/Y over OCD; CFA via `elf_cfi_cfa()`), read the value over `updi_mem_read()` (sign-extended per the type), and return 1 (true → stop), 0 (false → resume), or -1 (cannot evaluate). When the target halts while running, `dap_conditional_skip()` shall examine every installed breakpoint at the live PC: if any is unconditional, or any condition is true or returns -1, it shall return false so `dap_serve()` emits the `stopped` event; only when all matching breakpoints are conditional-and-false shall it step over them and auto-resume (returning true so the poll loop keeps running). Stepping over shall use `dap_resume_over_current()` — the GDB remove/single-step/insert dance: `bp_remove()` every breakpoint at the PC, `bp_step_over()` (the shared single-step core) one instruction, `bp_insert()` to re-arm, then `updi_run()`. `continue` shall resume via `dap_target_resume()`, which applies the same step-over when a breakpoint is parked at the live PC and otherwise issues a plain `updi_run()`. All paths are guarded by `updi_fd >= 0` so dispatch stays unit-testable without hardware.

trace.name: True Software Breakpoints via Flash BREAK Opcode

llr.text: `dap_handle_scopes()` and `dap_handle_variables()` shall serve `scopes`/`variables`. `dap_unwind()` (LLR-DAP-11) shall record each frame's PC and register context (`ElfFrameRegs`: CFA/Y/SP) into `s->frames[]`, indexed by `frameId`. `scopes` shall allocate variablesReferences (a `s->varrefs[]` table, 1-based) for a Locals scope (`DAP_VR_LOCALS`, carrying the frame PC + regs), a Globals scope (`DAP_VR_GLOBALS`), and — for `frameId == 0` only — a Registers scope (`DAP_VR_REGISTERS`). `variables` shall, by the reference's kind: list the live CPU registers (r0–r31 + SP/SREG/PC over OCD) for `DAP_VR_REGISTERS`; enumerate the scope via `elf_var_enum()` for Locals/Globals; or list aggregate children via `elf_type_children()` for `DAP_VR_AGGREGATE`. Each variable is rendered with `elf_type_render()` through a `dap_mem_cb()` data-space read (mapped-flash via `flash_to_updi`), and an aggregate is given a fresh `DAP_VR_AGGREGATE` reference for lazy drill-down. `dap_varref_reset()` shall invalidate the frame/varref tables on every resume (continue/step).

`dap_handle_evaluate()` shall serve `evaluate`. It shall map `arguments.frameId` to the recorded frame context, then `dap_resolve_expr()` shall parse a leading identifier and a chain of `.field` / `[index]` accessors: the identifier resolves via `elf_var_find()` (LLR-ELF-20), and each accessor descends through `elf_type_children()` (matching member name or array index) to a final (addr, type_off). The value is rendered with `elf_type_render()`; the reply carries `result`, a `variablesReference` (non-zero for an aggregate), and a `memoryReference`. An empty/unresolvable/unreadable expression shall reply `success:false` via `dap_send_error()`.

`dap_handle_read_memory()` and `dap_handle_write_memory()` shall serve `readMemory`/`writeMemory` using in-tree base64 (`dap_b64_encode`/`dap_b64_decode`). `readMemory` parses `memoryReference` + `offset` + `count` (capped at 1024), reads the data space via `updi_mem_read()` (mapped-flash window routed through `flash_to_updi`), and replies `{address, data}` (marking `unreadableBytes` on a short read). `writeMemory` decodes `data` and writes it to the writable data space (`addr < 0x8000`) via `updi_mem_write()`, replying `bytesWritten`. Both are guarded by `updi_fd >= 0`.

`dap_handle_set_variable()` shall serve `setVariable`. It shall locate the named child of the given `variablesReference` (via `elf_type_children()` for an aggregate, else `elf_var_enum()` for a scope) to obtain its address and type, parse the new `value` (`strtol(...,0)`), and write `elf_type_size()` little-endian bytes to the writable data space (`addr < 0x8000`) via `updi_mem_write()`, then re-render the stored value into the reply. An unknown reference/name shall reply `success:false`.

`dap_dispatch()` shall serve three avrOS-introspection custom requests through private handlers, each guarded by `updi_fd >= 0` and degrading to an empty array when no target link or no avrOS symbol index is present. `dap_handle_fsm_list()` (`avrosdb/fsmList`) shall, when the FSM context and symbol index are present, rebuild the thread list with `fsm_build_thread_list()` and reply `{"fsms":[{"id":<gdb_id>,"name":"…","state":"…","active":<bool>}]}` from each `FsmThread`'s `gdb_id` / `name` / `state_name` / `is_active`. `dap_handle_event_list()` (`avrosdb/eventList`) shall read the event table with `avros_read_events()` (LLR-AVROS-01) and reply `{"events":[{"name":"…","status":<n|null>}]}` — `status` is the JSON null literal when the descriptor carries no status pointer (`has_status` false). `dap_handle_queue_list()` (`avrosdb/queueList`) shall read the queue table with `avros_read_queues()` (LLR-AVROS-02) and reply `{"queues":[{"id":<i>,"capacity":<n>,"elemSize":<n>}]}`. All dynamic strings shall be JSON-escaped via `dj_escape()`; the handlers shall touch no target when `updi_fd < 0`, so dispatch is unit-testable over a socketpair.

trace.name: avrOS Introspection over DAP Custom Requests

llr.text: `dap_dispatch()` shall serve the DAP `source` request via a private `dap_handle_source()` helper, so a client that cannot open a frame's `Source.path` (now emitted absolute, LLR-ELF-12) still gets a clean answer rather than the generic unsupported-request error. The handler shall read `arguments.source.path`, open it on the debug host, and reply `{"content":"<file>"}` (`success:true`) with the file's text JSON-escaped via `dj_escape()`; because a source file can exceed the standard `DAP_OUT_MAX` response buffer it shall frame the reply through a heap buffer bounded by `DAP_MSG_MAX`. A path that is absent/unreadable, or whose content would not fit the frame, shall reply `success:false` with an explanatory message (e.g. "source file is not available on the debug host" / "source too large to stream over DAP; open it from the workspace"). Any request the adapter does not model shall likewise receive a `success:false` response (never silence/hang).

trace.name: DAP Execution Control, Stop Events & Shallow stackTrace

llr.text: Source-line stepping shall be served by three private handlers built on the shared core primitives (so the DAP front-end reuses the same stepping calls as the GDB-RSP path rather than duplicating them). `dap_step_line()` (stepIn) shall record the start `(file,line)` and repeatedly `bp_step_range()` (LLR-RSP-53) over the current line's address range from `elf_line_range()`, stopping when the live PC maps to a *different* source line — descending into calls naturally; when a PC has no line range it shall fall back to a single `updi_step()`. `dap_step_over()` (next) shall do the same but, when a range-step leaves the current line by descending into a callee (SP dropped below the line's start SP *and* the enclosing function from `elf_addr_to_func()` changed), shall run to the return address in the original frame — `dap_unwind()` gives `frames[1].pc` — via `dap_run_to()` instead of stepping through the callee, then continue, so stepping over a call (even a delay/loop) is immediate. `dap_step_out()` (stepOut) shall `dap_unwind()` and run to the caller's return (`frames[1].pc`) with a stop guard of `frames[0].fr.cfa` (the SP once the function returns). `dap_run_to(target, min_sp)` shall arm the reserved stepping comparator (`RSP_HW_BP_STEP_SLOT`) — never a user breakpoint slot — `updi_run()`, poll `updi_ocd_poll_halted()`, and stop when the target is reached with `SP >= min_sp` (re-running past a recursive re-entry at a deeper frame) or at any other breakpoint; it clears the comparator before returning. All paths are guarded so dispatch stays unit-testable without hardware (the handlers are only entered when `updi_fd >= 0`).

trace.name: DAP Execution Control, Stop Events & Shallow stackTrace

function.title: src/avros.c — avrOS Introspection Core
function.name: avros
function.intro: Requirements for the protocol-agnostic avrOS introspection core (`src/avros.c`): the single home for decoding the avrOS event/queue descriptor tables off the target, called by both the GDB-RSP `monitor avros` formatter and the DAP `avrosdb/*List` custom requests. Depends only on the UPDI and ELF layers (no front-end dependency).

llr.text: `avros_read_events()` shall decode the avrOS `EVNT_TABLE` event descriptors into a caller-supplied `AvrosEvent` array. It shall return -1 on a bad argument (`idx`/`out` NULL or `max <= 0`) and 0 immediately when `idx->event_count` is 0; otherwise it shall read `event_count` × 4-byte `evntDescriptor_t` records from `flash_to_updi(idx->event_table_addr)` with a single `updi_mem_read()`. For each record it shall extract the little-endian FLASH `name` pointer and SRAM `status` pointer: a null name pointer yields the name `<null>`, otherwise the name is followed (with `idx->flash_lma_off` applied) into the mapped-flash window by the private `read_target_string()` helper — a NUL-terminated `updi_mem_read()` loop that renders non-printable bytes as `?` and bounds the copy to the field width. A non-null status pointer shall be read as one byte and flagged `has_status`; a null pointer shall leave `has_status` false. It shall fill at most `max` entries and return the count, or -1 on any UPDI read error.

trace.name: avrOS Introspection over DAP Custom Requests

llr.text: `avros_read_queues()` shall decode the avrOS `QUE_TABLE` queue descriptors into a caller-supplied `AvrosQueue` array. It shall return -1 on a bad argument and 0 when `idx->queue_count` is 0; otherwise it shall read `queue_count` × 10-byte `queDescriptor_t` records from `flash_to_updi(idx->queue_table_addr)` with a single `updi_mem_read()`. From each record — three pointers (queue / buffer / event, 2 bytes each) followed by a 2-byte `capacity` and a 2-byte `sizeOfElement` — it shall report the little-endian `capacity` (offset 6) and `elem_size` (offset 8), filling at most `max` entries and returning the count, or -1 on a UPDI read error.

trace.name: avrOS Introspection over DAP Custom Requests

file.header: Unit tests for `src/main.c`: argument parsing, event loop, signal handling, and resource teardown. Uses `fork()`/`waitpid()` to test `exit()` paths and a mock UPDI/RSP layer to exercise the event loop without real hardware.

test.name: parse_args_valid_positional_args_populate_config
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with a valid `<serial-device>` and `<elf-file>` and verify that the returned `AppConfig` carries the correct device path and ELF path.

test.name: parse_args_unrecognised_flag_exits_1
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with an unrecognised flag and assert that the process exits with status 1 and that a usage message is present on `stderr`.

test.name: parse_args_default_port_baud_load_when_not_supplied
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with only the two mandatory positional arguments and verify that `cfg.gdb_port == 1234`, `cfg.baud_rate == 115200`, and `cfg.load_flash == false`.

test.name: parse_args_missing_serial_device_exits_1
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with no positional arguments and assert that the process exits with status 1 and emits a usage message.

test.name: parse_args_missing_elf_file_exits_1
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with only `<serial-device>` and no `<elf-file>` and assert that the process exits with status 1.

test.name: main_updi_open_failure_releases_resources_and_returns_1
test.purpose: Inject a mock `updi_open()` that returns -1 and verify that `main()` does not call `rsp_listen()`, releases any already-opened resources, and returns exit code 1.

test.name: main_rsp_listen_failure_closes_updi_and_returns_1
test.purpose: Inject a mock `rsp_listen()` that returns -1 and verify that `main()` calls `updi_close()` before returning exit code 1.

test.name: main_load_flag_writes_all_pt_load_segments_to_flash
test.purpose: With `cfg.load = true` and a mock ELF context containing two `PT_LOAD` segments, verify that `main()` calls `updi_nvm_write_flash()` exactly twice, once per segment, before entering `event_loop()`.

test.name: main_load_nvm_write_failure_prints_error_and_returns_1
test.purpose: With `cfg.load = true` and a mock `updi_nvm_write_flash()` that returns -1, verify that `main()` prints an error to `stderr` and returns exit code 1 without entering `event_loop()`.

test.name: event_loop_uses_single_select_no_pthread_create
test.purpose: Instrument `event_loop()` with mock file descriptors and verify that `select()` is called with all three fds (`listen_fd`, `gdb_fd`, `updi_fd`) in the read set, and that no calls to `pthread_create()` occur.

test.name: event_loop_accepts_gdb_client_when_gdb_fd_is_minus1
test.purpose: With `cfg.gdb_fd == -1` and `listen_fd` readable, verify that `event_loop()` calls `accept()` and updates `cfg.gdb_fd`.

test.name: sigint_handler_sets_g_quit_to_1
test.purpose: Send SIGINT to the test process and verify that the signal handler installed by `main()` sets `g_quit` to 1 without performing any other operation.

test.name: event_loop_exits_immediately_when_g_quit_is_1
test.purpose: Set `g_quit = 1` before calling `event_loop()` and verify that the function returns immediately without calling `select()`.

test.name: main_cleanup_closes_gdb_elf_updi_in_order
test.purpose: On a simulated clean shutdown, verify that `main()` calls `rsp_close(gdb_fd)`, `rsp_close(listen_fd)`, `elf_close()`, and `updi_close()` in that exact order, and returns exit code 0.

test.name: main_calls_updi_enter_debug_after_updi_open_before_rsp_listen
test.purpose: Run `main()` with mocked `updi_open()`, `updi_enter_debug()`, and `rsp_listen()` recording call order. Verify (a) `updi_enter_debug()` is called exactly once after `updi_open()` succeeds and before `rsp_listen()`, and (b) when `updi_enter_debug()` returns non-zero, `main()` invokes the LLR-MAIN-07 teardown sequence and exits with code 1 without calling `rsp_listen()`.

test.name: parse_args_allow_lock_updi_sets_flag
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with `--allow-lock-updi` present in argv and verify that the returned `AppConfig.allow_lock_updi` is `true`.

test.name: parse_args_force_device_captures_family
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with `--force-device=AVR-DD` in argv and verify that `AppConfig.force_device` points to the string `"AVR-DD"`.

test.name: parse_args_force_device_default_is_null
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with no `--force-device` flag and verify that `AppConfig.force_device` defaults to `NULL` (autodetect path will be used).

test.name: load_segments_dispatches_eeprom_segment_to_eeprom_writer
test.purpose: Build a one-segment ELF at vaddr `0x814000` size 8 and run `app_main(... --load ...)`. Verify wrapped `updi_nvm_write_eeprom` is called exactly once with `addr=0x814000` and `len=8`, while no other NVM writer is called.

test.name: load_segments_dispatches_fuses_segment_to_fuses_writer
test.purpose: Build a one-segment ELF at vaddr `0x820004` size 2 and run `app_main(... --load ...)`. Verify wrapped `updi_nvm_write_fuses` is called exactly once with `addr=0x820004` and `len=2`.

test.name: load_segments_dispatches_userrow_segment_to_userrow_writer
test.purpose: Build a one-segment ELF at vaddr `0x810080` size 16 and run `app_main(... --load ...)`. Verify wrapped `updi_nvm_write_userrow` is called exactly once with `addr=0x810080`. Regression test ensuring the classifier does not mis-route USERROW into the FLASH branch (the USERROW VMA lies between `UPDI_FLASH_BASE` and `UPDI_EEPROM_BASE`).

test.name: load_segments_lock_requires_erase_else_exit_1
test.purpose: Build a LOCK segment at vaddr `0x820040` size 4 and run `app_main(... --load ...)` WITHOUT `--erase`. Verify `app_main` returns 1 and that `updi_nvm_write_lockbits` was never called.

test.name: load_segments_lock_with_erase_dispatches_to_lockbits_writer
test.purpose: Build a LOCK segment at vaddr `0x820040` size 4 and run `app_main(... --erase --load ...)`. Verify wrapped `updi_chip_erase` was called exactly once, then wrapped `updi_nvm_write_lockbits` was called exactly once with `addr=0x820040` and the recorded `allow_updi_disable` flag matching `cfg.allow_lock_updi` (false in this case).

test.name: load_segments_sigrow_segment_is_skipped
test.purpose: Build a SIGROW segment at vaddr `0x811080` size 4 and run `app_main(... --load ...)`. Verify NONE of the FLASH/EEPROM/USERROW/FUSES/LOCK writers were called and `app_main` returns 0.

test.name: load_segments_unknown_window_returns_minus1
test.purpose: Build a segment at vaddr `0x830000` (outside every programmable UPDI window) and run `app_main(... --load ...)`. Verify `app_main` returns 1 (load failure) and that no NVM writer was called.

test.name: main_autoselects_family_from_elf_deviceinfo
test.purpose: Plant `mk_elf_planted_device_name = "avr64dd32"` (deviceinfo string for an AVR-DD part) and `mk_updi_get_device_family = "AVR-DD"` (silicon agrees). Run `app_main()` without `--force-device`. Verify that the wrapped `updi_select_device()` was called exactly once with `force_family == ""` (the wrap normalises `NULL` to `""`), confirming that the ELF deviceinfo is NOT used as a selection input — SIGROW autodetect runs unbiased — and that `app_main()` returns 0 because the autodetected family agrees with the ELF (no mismatch).

test.name: main_force_device_overrides_elf_deviceinfo
test.purpose: Plant `mk_elf_planted_device_name = "avr64dd32"` (would map to AVR-DD) but also pass `--force-device=AVR-DA`. Verify that the wrapped `updi_select_device()` was called with `force_family == "AVR-DA"` and that `app_main()` returned 0, demonstrating the documented precedence `--force-device > deviceinfo`.

test.name: main_aborts_on_elf_vs_silicon_family_mismatch
test.purpose: Plant `mk_elf_planted_device_name = "avr64dd32"` (AVR-DD) and override `mk_updi_get_device_family = "AVR-DA"` so the post-select check sees a family mismatch. Run `app_main()` with no `--force-device`. Verify that `app_main()` returns 1, that the wrapped `updi_select_device()` ran exactly once, and that the wrapped `rsp_listen()` was NOT invoked — i.e. the application aborted before opening the GDB listener.

test.name: main_passes_null_to_select_when_elf_lacks_deviceinfo
test.purpose: Leave `mk_elf_planted_device_name` empty (`\0`), run `app_main()` with no `--force-device`. Verify the wrapped `updi_select_device()` was called once and that the captured `force_family` argument was the empty string (the wrap normalises `NULL` to `""`), confirming that `app_main()` falls through to the SIGROW autodetect path when the ELF carries no deviceinfo note.

test.name: parse_args_prog_mode_sets_flag
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with argv `{ "prog", "--prog", "/dev/x", "a.elf" }` and assert `cfg.prog_mode == true`, `cfg.device_info == false`, and `cfg.load_flash == false` — confirming `--prog` is recognised, sets only `prog_mode`, and does not implicitly set the other operating-mode flags.

test.name: parse_args_no_verify_sets_flag
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with argv `{ "prog", "--load", "--no-verify", "/dev/x", "a.elf" }` and assert `cfg.no_verify == true` — confirming the verify-suppression flag is recognised and stored on `AppConfig`.

test.name: parse_args_no_autobaud_sets_flag
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with argv `{ "prog", "--device", "--no-autobaud", "/dev/x" }` and assert `cfg.no_autobaud == true` — confirming the autobaud-suppression flag is recognised and stored on `AppConfig` so `run_device_mode()` can gate its probe call accordingly.

test.name: test_parse_args_log_sets_flag
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with argv `{ "prog", "--log", "/dev/x", "a.elf" }` and assert `cfg.log == true` — confirming the logging flag is recognised by the option parser.

test.name: test_parse_args_start_sets_flag
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with argv `{ "prog", "--start", "/dev/x" }` (no ELF) and assert `cfg.start_cpu == true`, `cfg.stop_cpu == false`, and `cfg.elf_path == NULL` — confirming `--start` is recognised and makes the `<elf-file>` operand optional.

test.name: test_parse_args_stop_sets_flag
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with argv `{ "prog", "--stop", "/dev/x" }` (no ELF) and assert `cfg.stop_cpu == true`, `cfg.start_cpu == false`, and `cfg.elf_path == NULL` — confirming `--stop` is recognised and makes the `<elf-file>` operand optional.

test.name: test_run_start_mode_runs_cpu_and_detaches
test.purpose: With wrapped UPDI primitives, call `run_start_mode()` and assert it returns 0 having called `updi_open` → `updi_enter_debug` → `updi_run` once each and `updi_detach` once, with `updi_halt` and `updi_close` never called — i.e. it takes OCD control, runs the CPU, and detaches WITHOUT a reset so the target keeps running.

test.name: test_run_stop_mode_halts_cpu_and_detaches
test.purpose: With wrapped UPDI primitives, call `run_stop_mode()` and assert it returns 0 having called `updi_open` → `updi_enter_debug` → `updi_halt` once each and `updi_detach` once, with `updi_run` and `updi_close` never called — i.e. it takes OCD control, halts the CPU, and detaches WITHOUT a reset so the target stays halted.

test.name: parse_args_allow_erase_sets_flag
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with argv `{ "prog", "--allow-erase", "/dev/x", "a.elf" }` and assert `cfg.allow_erase == true` — confirming the destructive-erase gate is recognised by the option parser.

test.name: parse_args_allow_erase_defaults_false
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with argv that omits `--allow-erase` and assert `cfg.allow_erase == false` — confirming the safety default refuses destructive erase verbs unless the operator explicitly opts in.

test.name: test_sig_handler_records_signo_in_g_shutdown_signal
test.purpose: Reset `g_shutdown_signal` to 0, invoke `sig_handler(SIGTERM)`, and assert `g_quit == 1` and `g_shutdown_signal == SIGTERM`. Then invoke `sig_handler(SIGINT)` and assert `g_shutdown_signal` remains `SIGTERM` — confirming the first delivered signal is captured for the shutdown lifecycle log line and is not overwritten by a follow-up signal. Per LLR-MAIN-22.

test.name: test_event_loop_clears_disconnect_reason_after_drain
test.purpose: Stage `RspContext.disconnect_reason = "D"` and execute the event_loop drain contract: read the field, then NULL it. Assert the field is NULL afterwards. This locks in the no-duplicate-emission guarantee from LLR-MAIN-22 — a single disconnect line per fd-close.

file.header: Unit tests for `src/updi.c`: UART configuration, BREAK/SYNCH/LDCS link initialisation, three-frame block memory read/write, NVM flash programming, OCD-mode entry, OCD execution-control primitives (halt/run/step + poll_halted), OCD register-file access (GPR/SREG/SP/PC) and hardware-breakpoint comparator programming, link detach, and console polling. A loopback PTY pair substitutes for real UART hardware; a `--wrap=select` linker shim lets tests inject `select()` timeouts.

test.name: updi_detach_closes_fd_and_ignores_negative
test.purpose: Create a pipe, call `updi_detach(fds[1])`, and assert a subsequent `write()` to that fd fails with `EBADF` — proving the link was closed without a reset pulse. A second call `updi_detach(-1)` must be a harmless no-op. Per LLR-UPDI-37.

test.name: updi_open_sets_8e2_raw_half_duplex_via_termios
test.purpose: Open a PTY pair, call `updi_open()` on the slave side, and inspect the resulting `termios` structure to confirm `CS8`, `CSTOPB` (2 stop bits), even-parity intent (`PARODD` clear), and raw mode (no `ICANON`/`ECHO`/`ISIG`/`OPOST`). PARENB itself is not asserted because Linux PTYs strip parity on slave reopen; parity is verified on real serial hardware in Phase 3 integration.

test.name: updi_open_returns_minus1_on_device_open_failure
test.purpose: Call `updi_open()` with a path that does not exist and verify the return value is -1.

test.name: updi_open_asserts_wake_byte_then_stcs_ctrlb
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_open()` transmits a single 0x00 wake byte first, then the STCS CTRLB frame (SYNCH `0x55`, opcode `0xC0|ASI_CTRLB = 0xC3`, value `ASI_CTRLB_CCDETDIS = 0x08`) — the first half of the avrdude-matching cold-start sequence (issue #19).

test.name: updi_open_issues_stcs_ctrla_and_ldcs_statusa
test.purpose: Verify that after STCS CTRLB the SUT writes STCS CTRLA (`0xC2`, value `ASI_CTRLA_IBDLY = 0x80`) and then probes the link with LDCS STATUSA (`0x80|ASI_STATUSA = 0x80`) — the second half of the cold-start sequence (issue #19).

test.name: updi_open_restores_session_baud_after_break
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_open()` leaves the configured session baud rate (B115200) in effect after a successful cold-start sequence — i.e. it does not corrupt the termios baud setting. The PTY responder also feeds the 32-byte SIB payload (`SYNCH`+`0xE6` → `" AVR P:2D:1-3M2 (A7.KV001.0)\0"`), so a successful run additionally exercises the SIB-read SLEEP-wake step that `updi_open()` issues after the LDCS ASI_STATUSA link probe.

test.name: updi_open_retries_cold_start_3_times_on_no_ack
test.purpose: Simulate a target that never responds and verify that `updi_open()` runs all three cold-start attempts before giving up: attempt 0 emits 1× 0x00 wake byte then STCS+STCS+LDCS at session baud; attempts 1 and 2 each emit 2× 0x00 BREAK bytes (at 300 baud via `tcsetattr`) then STCS+STCS+LDCS at session baud. With no 0x00 byte present anywhere else in the frames, this yields 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 zero bytes on the wire.

test.name: updi_open_returns_minus1_after_3_consecutive_link_failures
test.purpose: After 3 failed cold-start attempts (wake + STCS CTRLB + STCS CTRLA + LDCS STATUSA) with no response, verify that `updi_open()` returns -1.

test.name: updi_mem_read_splits_request_larger_than_256_bytes
test.purpose: Request a read of 512 bytes and verify that `updi_mem_read()` issues two consecutive 256-byte three-frame bursts rather than a single oversized transfer.

test.name: updi_mem_read_uses_repeat_ld_auto_increment_sequence
test.purpose: Read a low SRAM address (`0x0100`) and capture the bytes written to the UART to verify the three-frame burst uses the 24-bit pointer-set even below 64 KiB: frame 1 = `ST_PTR_LONG` (`0x6A`, captured[1]) + 3 little-endian address bytes, frame 2 = `REPEAT` (`0xA0`, captured[6]) + count, frame 3 = `LD ptr++` (`0x24`, captured[9]) — a 10-byte burst. Regression guard for the always-24-bit pointer-set (LLR-UPDI-33).

test.name: updi_mem_read_uses_24bit_addressing_above_64kib
test.purpose: Request a read at address `0x012345` (above the 64 KiB boundary) and verify that `updi_mem_read()` emits the 24-bit pointer-set frame: `SYNCH`, `ST_PTR_LONG` (`0x6A`), then the address bytes in little-endian order (`0x45`, `0x23`, `0x01`), followed by the standard `REPEAT` + `LD ptr++` frames. Confirms automatic selection of the 24-bit form for AVR128DA/DB mapped-Flash access above 64 KiB.

test.name: updi_mem_read_calls_select_with_100ms_timeout_before_read
test.purpose: Using a `--wrap=select` shim that records the `timeval` argument, verify that `updi_mem_read()` passes a `timeval` of 0 seconds and 100,000 microseconds before every `read()` call.

test.name: updi_mem_read_returns_minus1_on_select_timeout
test.purpose: Inject a wrapped `select()` that returns 0 (timeout) and verify that `updi_mem_read()` immediately returns -1 without calling `read()`.

test.name: updi_mem_write_returns_0_on_success
test.purpose: Call `updi_mem_write()` targeting an SRAM address with a loopback PTY that echoes the expected ACK and verify the return value is 0.

test.name: updi_mem_write_returns_minus1_on_updi_nak
test.purpose: Inject a responder that returns a non-ACK byte instead of `UPDI_ACK` (0x40) and verify that `updi_mem_write()` returns -1.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_flash_rejects_unaligned_address
test.purpose: Call `updi_nvm_write_flash()` with a `word_addr` that is not a multiple of 512 and verify the function returns -1 without issuing any UART traffic.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_flash_rejects_non_multiple_of_512_length
test.purpose: Call `updi_nvm_write_flash()` with a `len` that is not a non-zero multiple of 512 and verify the function returns -1.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_flash_nvmprog_poll_timeout_returns_minus1
test.purpose: Inject a mock target that never sets the NVMPROG bit (`ASI_SYS_STATUS` bit 3) and verify that `updi_nvm_write_flash()` returns -1 after 100 polling iterations.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_flash_per_page_busy_timeout_returns_minus1
test.purpose: Inject a mock target that never clears `NVMCTRL_STATUS` BUSY (bit 0) after a page write and verify that `updi_nvm_write_flash()` returns -1 after 20 polling iterations.

test.name: updi_enter_debug_writes_key_pulses_reset_and_polls_ocd_stopped
test.purpose: Drive a PTY responder that emulates an AVR-Dx in OCD mode. Verify that `updi_enter_debug()` (a) issues the UPDI KEY opcode (`SYNCH`+`0xE0|UPDI_KEY_64`) followed by the 8 ASCII bytes `"OCD "` (reversed-byte order per the UPDI KEY protocol); (b) pulses `STCS ASI_RESET_REQ = 0x59` then `STCS ASI_RESET_REQ = 0x00`; (c) polls CS-space `ASI_OCD_STATUS` (LDCS opcode `0x80|0x05 = 0x85`) until `OCD_STATUS_STOPPED (0x01)` is observed, and returns 0.

test.name: updi_enter_debug_returns_minus1_when_ocd_status_never_stopped
test.purpose: Drive a PTY responder that completes the KEY and RESET pulses but always returns `OCD_STATUS = 0x00`. Verify that `updi_enter_debug()` polls `ASI_OCD_STATUS` for the LLR-bounded number of iterations and then returns -1.

test.name: updi_halt_writes_ocd_ctrla_stop_via_stcs
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_halt()` issues `STCS ASI_OCD_CTRLA = OCD_CTRLA_STOP (0x01)` and returns 0 on the responder ACK. No FLASH/SRAM frames must appear on the wire.

test.name: updi_run_writes_ocd_ctrla_run_via_stcs
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_run()` issues `STCS ASI_OCD_CTRLA = OCD_CTRLA_RUN (0x02)` and returns 0 on responder ACK.

test.name: updi_step_writes_ctrl0_step_bit_then_polls_stopped
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_step()` writes the STEP bit into the OCD `CTRL0` MMIO register at UPDI 0x0F80+offset and then polls `ASI_OCD_STATUS` for `STOPPED` before returning 0.

test.name: updi_ocd_poll_halted_returns_0_when_stopped_set
test.purpose: Stage `ASI_OCD_STATUS = OCD_STATUS_STOPPED (0x01)` in the PTY responder and verify that `updi_ocd_poll_halted(fd, deadline_ms=1)` returns 0 on the first poll. With `OCD_STATUS = 0x00` it must return 1 (still running) after the deadline elapses, and -1 on LDCS link failure.

test.name: updi_ocd_read_halt_status_returns_two_status_bytes
test.purpose: Stage `OCD_STATUS0 = 0x00`, `OCD_STATUS1 = OCD_STATUS1_EXTBRK (0x10)` in the responder's MMIO image. Verify that `updi_ocd_read_halt_status()` reads both bytes from UPDI 0x0F80+STATUS0/STATUS1 and writes them into the caller's out-parameters.

test.name: updi_ocd_read_gpr_reads_regfile_byte_at_ocd_offset
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_ocd_read_gpr(fd, n=5)` reads exactly one byte from UPDI address `0x0F80 + OCD_REGFILE_OFFSET + 5` and returns the responder-supplied value.

test.name: updi_ocd_write_gpr_writes_single_byte_at_ocd_offset
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_ocd_write_gpr(fd, n=12, val=0xAB)` issues an ST-byte to UPDI address `0x0F80 + OCD_REGFILE_OFFSET + 12` with value `0xAB` and returns 0 on ACK.

test.name: updi_ocd_read_write_sreg_round_trip
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_ocd_write_sreg(fd, 0x5A)` writes one byte to UPDI `0x0F80 + OCD_SREG_OFFSET` and that `updi_ocd_read_sreg(fd, &out)` reads it back from the same address.

test.name: updi_ocd_read_write_sp_round_trip_little_endian
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_ocd_write_sp(fd, 0x3FFE)` writes two bytes little-endian to UPDI `0x0F80 + OCD_SP_OFFSET` and that `updi_ocd_read_sp(fd, &out)` reads them back as a 16-bit LE value.

test.name: updi_ocd_read_write_pc_round_trip_32bit_le_byte_addr
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_ocd_write_pc(fd, 0x00012345)` writes four bytes little-endian (PC as byte address) to UPDI `0x0F80 + OCD_PC_OFFSET` and that `updi_ocd_read_pc(fd, &out)` reads them back as a 32-bit LE value.

test.name: updi_ocd_set_hw_bp_writes_bp_addr_and_enables_ctrl1
