test.purpose: Verify that `updi_ocd_set_hw_bp(fd, idx=0, addr=0x001234)` writes the 32-bit address (little-endian) to `BP0A` at UPDI `0x0F80 + OCD_BP0A_OFFSET` and then sets the corresponding enable bit in `CTRL1` at UPDI `0x0F80 + OCD_CTRL1_OFFSET`. With `idx=1` the same sequence targets `BP1A` and the BP1 enable bit.

test.name: updi_ocd_clear_hw_bp_clears_only_target_slot
test.purpose: After setting both BP0 and BP1, verify that `updi_ocd_clear_hw_bp(fd, idx=0)` clears only the BP0 enable bit in `CTRL1` (read-modify-write) and leaves BP1 armed.

test.name: updi_console_poll_returns_pending_bytes_without_halting
test.purpose: Pre-stuff the master end of the PTY with 4 bytes and verify that `updi_console_poll()` returns 4 and copies the bytes to the output buffer without calling `updi_halt()`.

test.name: updi_console_poll_returns_0_when_output_buffer_empty
test.purpose: With no data pending on the master end, verify that `updi_console_poll()` returns 0 in a non-blocking manner.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_eeprom_rejects_addr_below_window
test.purpose: Call `updi_nvm_write_eeprom(fd, UPDI_EEPROM_BASE - 1, data, 1)` and verify the function returns -1 without transmitting any bytes on the UPDI line (drain the master end and assert zero bytes captured). Confirms the EEPROM window guard rejects out-of-window addresses before any NVM activity.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_eeprom_rejects_addr_above_window
test.purpose: Call `updi_nvm_write_eeprom(fd, UPDI_EEPROM_BASE + UPDI_EEPROM_SIZE - 1, data, 2)` and verify the function returns -1: the second byte (at `UPDI_EEPROM_BASE + UPDI_EEPROM_SIZE`) lies past the EEPROM window.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_fuses_rejects_len_exceeds_window
test.purpose: Call `updi_nvm_write_fuses(fd, UPDI_FUSES_BASE, data, UPDI_FUSES_SIZE + 1)` and verify the function returns -1: the payload extends one byte past the FUSES window.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_userrow_rejects_zero_length
test.purpose: Call `updi_nvm_write_userrow(fd, UPDI_USERROW_BASE, NULL, 0)` and verify the function returns -1 without UPDI traffic.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_lockbits_returns_locked_when_lockstatus_set
test.purpose: Pre-stuff the LDCS ASI_SYS_STATUS response with `0x02` (LOCKSTATUS asserted) and call `updi_nvm_write_lockbits(fd, UPDI_LOCK_BASE, unlock_pattern, 4, allow=true)`. Verify the function returns `UPDI_ERR_LOCKED` (-3) — even with the unlock pattern and `allow_updi_disable=true`, a locked device cannot be written.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_lockbits_refuses_updidis_value_without_flag
test.purpose: Pre-stuff the LDCS ASI_SYS_STATUS response with `0x00` (LOCKSTATUS clear, post-erase state) and call `updi_nvm_write_lockbits(fd, UPDI_LOCK_BASE, {0,0,0,0}, 4, allow=false)`. Verify the function returns `UPDI_ERR_LOCKED`: only the `UPDI_LOCK_UNLOCKED` (`0x5CC5C55C`) 4-byte pattern is accepted without `--allow-lock-updi`.

test.name: updi_get_device_default_is_avrda
test.purpose: Call `updi_get_device()` before any `updi_select_device()` invocation and verify the returned descriptor names AVR-DA, exposes the historical `UPDI_USERROW_BASE`/`UPDI_USERROW_SIZE` and `UPDI_EEPROM_BASE`/`UPDI_EEPROM_SIZE` constants, and has `hw_tested == true`.

test.name: updi_select_device_force_avrdd_sets_active_descriptor
test.purpose: Call `updi_select_device(-1, "avr-dd")` (case-insensitive force path, no UPDI traffic). Verify the function returns 0, `updi_get_device()` now returns the AVR-DD descriptor (`userrow_size == 128`, `hw_tested == false`), then restore the AVR-DA default for subsequent tests.

test.name: updi_select_device_unknown_family_returns_minus1
test.purpose: Call `updi_select_device(-1, "AVR-XYZ")` and verify the function returns -1 (unknown family name) without modifying the active descriptor.

test.name: updi_family_from_partname_maps_all_known_prefixes
test.purpose: Call `updi_family_from_partname()` once per supported family with a representative lowercase part-name (`"avr128da28"`, `"avr128db48"`, `"avr64dd32"`, `"avr32du28"`, `"avr32sd20"`) and verify the returned string equals the matching `g_device_table[]` family literal (`"AVR-DA"`, `"AVR-DB"`, `"AVR-DD"`, `"AVR-DU"`, `"AVR-SD"`).

test.name: updi_family_from_partname_rejects_invalid_inputs
test.purpose: Verify `updi_family_from_partname()` returns `NULL` for `NULL`, the empty string, strings not beginning with `"avr"` (`"not-an-avr"`), the unsupported NVMCTRL v3 families (`"avr32ea48"`, `"avr16eb14"`), and inputs missing the digit run between `"avr"` and the family-letters (`"avrda28"`). NULL signals "no usable identification" to `app_main()` (LLR-MAIN-13).

test.name: updi_crc32_returns_zero_for_empty_buffer
test.purpose: Call `updi_crc32(NULL, 0)` and assert the result equals `0x00000000` — the canonical IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 of the empty message (verified against zlib and crc32 CLI tools).

test.name: updi_crc32_matches_known_vector_for_123456789
test.purpose: Call `updi_crc32()` with the canonical IEEE 802.3 / zlib test vector — the 9-byte ASCII string `"123456789"` — and assert the result equals the published expected value `0xCBF43926`.

test.name: updi_crc32_matches_known_vector_for_single_zero_byte
test.purpose: Call `updi_crc32()` with a single 0x00 byte and assert the result equals `0xD202EF8D`, the canonical IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 of a one-byte zero message. Confirms that the polynomial reflection, initial value (`0xFFFFFFFF`), and final XOR (`0xFFFFFFFF`) are all implemented correctly even on the shortest non-empty input.

test.name: updi_apply_debug_in_sleep_asserts_clkreq_when_enabled
test.purpose: With debug-in-sleep enabled (the default, via `updi_set_debug_in_sleep(true)`), call `updi_apply_debug_in_sleep()` over a PTY and verify it emits exactly the STCS bytes `0x55 0xCA 0x01` (SYNCH, `STCS|ASI_SYS_CTRLA`, `CLK_REQ`) — the write that keeps the system clock alive across SLEEP. The 3-byte half-duplex echo is prestuffed so `updi_write_bytes()` completes.

test.name: updi_apply_debug_in_sleep_emits_nothing_when_disabled
test.purpose: With debug-in-sleep disabled (`updi_set_debug_in_sleep(false)`, the `--sleep` case), call `updi_apply_debug_in_sleep()` over a PTY and verify it returns 0 and sends no bytes — native target sleep behaviour is left intact.

test.name: updi_save_restore_peripherals_noop_when_disabled
test.purpose: With debug-in-sleep disabled (`--sleep`), call `updi_save_peripherals()` and `updi_restore_peripherals()` over a PTY and verify both return 0 and emit no UPDI traffic. (The enabled path issues a peripheral-window UPDI burst and is validated on hardware by the SW-breakpoint-survives-sleep acceptance: a Z0/z0/Z0/continue sequence times out stuck-in-sleep with `--sleep` and hits the post-sleep breakpoint by default.)

file.header: Unit tests for `src/gdb_rsp.c`: socket configuration, RSP packet framing, register and memory handlers, hardware-breakpoint comparator management, OCD-based execution control, async Ctrl-C interrupt, detach cleanup, session lifecycle packets, and monitor relay. Uses a `socketpair()` as a drop-in socket substitute and replaces every `updi_*`, `fsm_*`, and `monitor_dispatch` call site with `ld --wrap` mocks so all tests run without real silicon.

test.name: rsp_listen_sets_so_reuseaddr_before_bind
test.purpose: Verify that `rsp_listen()` calls `setsockopt()` with `SO_REUSEADDR` enabled before calling `bind()`.

test.name: rsp_accept_sets_tcp_nodelay_on_client_socket
test.purpose: After `rsp_accept()` returns a client socket, verify that `TCP_NODELAY` has been set on that socket via `getsockopt()`.

test.name: rsp_recv_packet_discards_leading_ack_nak_bytes
test.purpose: Feed a byte stream that begins with `+` and `-` characters before the `$` delimiter and verify that `rsp_recv_packet()` discards them and correctly decodes the payload that follows.

test.name: rsp_recv_packet_sends_plus_on_valid_checksum
test.purpose: Feed a well-formed RSP packet with a correct XOR checksum and verify that `rsp_recv_packet()` writes `+` to the socket and returns the payload length.

test.name: rsp_recv_packet_sends_minus_and_returns_minus1_on_bad_checksum
test.purpose: Feed an RSP packet with a deliberately corrupted checksum and verify that `rsp_recv_packet()` writes `-` to the socket and returns -1.

test.name: on_read_regs_g_returns_78_char_hex_string
test.purpose: With the mock OCD layer returning canned values for `updi_ocd_read_gpr/sreg/sp/pc`, dispatch a `g` packet and verify that the RSP reply payload is exactly 78 hex characters in GDB's AVR register-block layout.

test.name: on_read_regs_g_places_pc_little_endian_at_positions_70_77
test.purpose: Inject a known PC byte address via the mocked `updi_ocd_read_pc()` and verify that hex characters at positions 70–77 of the `g` reply encode the PC as 4-byte little-endian.

test.name: on_write_regs_G_writes_all_registers_via_ocd
test.purpose: Dispatch a `G` packet containing 78 hex characters and verify that the handler calls `updi_ocd_write_gpr()` 32 times (one per GPR) plus `updi_ocd_write_sreg()`, `updi_ocd_write_sp()`, and `updi_ocd_write_pc()` once each with the decoded values, and replies `OK`.

test.name: on_write_regs_P_writes_single_register_via_ocd
test.purpose: Dispatch a `P5=AB` packet and verify that the handler calls `updi_ocd_write_gpr(n=5, val=0xAB)` exactly once and that no other OCD writer is invoked.

test.name: on_read_mem_m_calls_updi_mem_read_and_returns_hex
test.purpose: Dispatch an `m addr,4` packet for a SRAM address and verify that the handler calls `updi_mem_read()` with the UPDI physical address (bit 23 flipped) and length, and returns an 8-character hex string.

test.name: on_read_mem_mapped_flash_translates_via_flash_lma_off
test.purpose: With `ctx.idx` set to an index whose `flash_lma_off = 0x6000`, dispatch `m808156,2` (a data-space read in the mapped-flash window, off16 0x8156 >= 0x8000) and verify the handler served it from the physical flash LMA: `updi_mem_read()` is called once at `flash_to_updi(0x8156 + 0x6000) = 0x80E156` and the canned bytes are returned as hex (`4869`), not `E14`. Guards the flash-resident `.rodata` read path that makes `stateMachine->currStateName` readable. Per LLR-RSP-52.

test.name: on_read_mem_mapped_flash_without_idx_is_not_translated
test.purpose: Without an ELF index (`ctx.idx == NULL`), dispatch `m808156,2` and verify the mapped-flash translation does NOT apply: the read falls through to the ordinary data-space path and `updi_mem_read()` is called at `0x8156` (no flash-LMA translation). Confirms the mapped-flash capability is gated on the symbol index. Per LLR-RSP-52.

test.name: on_write_mem_M_calls_updi_mem_write_for_sram_address
test.purpose: Dispatch an `M addr,4:data` packet targeting a GDB data-space address and verify that the handler calls `updi_mem_write()` (not `updi_nvm_write_flash`) and replies `OK`.

test.name: on_write_mem_X_calls_nvm_write_flash_for_flash_address
test.purpose: Dispatch an `X addr,2:data` packet targeting a GDB program-space address and verify that the handler calls `updi_nvm_write_flash()` and replies `OK`.

test.name: on_insert_bp_calls_updi_ocd_set_hw_bp_with_byte_addr
test.purpose: Dispatch a `Z0 addr,2` packet and verify that the handler calls `updi_ocd_set_hw_bp(idx, byte_addr)` with the GDB byte address (masked to 23 bits) into the first free `RspContext.hw_bp_addr[]` slot, and replies `OK`. The handler shall not call `updi_nvm_write_flash()`.

test.name: on_insert_bp_second_slot_fails
test.purpose: Dispatch two `Z0` inserts at distinct addresses and verify that `updi_ocd_set_hw_bp()` is called once for slot 0, then fails for slot 1 because it is reserved for the 32-bit stepping errata workaround, returning `E08`.

test.name: on_insert_bp_duplicate_returns_ok_without_reprogramming
test.purpose: Dispatch the same `Z0 addr,2` breakpoint insert twice and verify that `updi_ocd_set_hw_bp()` is called only once and that the second call returns `OK` immediately.

test.name: on_remove_bp_calls_updi_ocd_clear_hw_bp
test.purpose: After inserting a breakpoint with `Z0`, dispatch `z0` for the same address and verify that `updi_ocd_clear_hw_bp()` is called with the slot index that held it, the shadow slot is reset to `0xFFFFFFFF`, and the reply is `OK`.

test.name: on_remove_bp_unknown_address_returns_ok_for_resync
test.purpose: Dispatch `z0` for an address that is not present in either `RspContext.hw_bp_addr[]` slot (e.g. after a server restart that lost the shadow) and verify that the handler replies `OK` rather than an error, so GDB resync after reconnect is non-fatal.

test.name: on_insert_bp_returns_E08_when_slot_occupied
test.purpose: Fill the single available `RspContext.hw_bp_addr[]` slot with an address, then dispatch a second `Z0`/`Z1` insert at a different address and verify the reply is `E08` and that no further `updi_ocd_set_hw_bp()` call is made.

test.name: on_step_s_calls_updi_step_and_sends_T05_stop_reason_16bit
test.purpose: Dispatch an `s` packet for a 16-bit instruction, with the mock `updi_ocd_read_halt_status()` returning `OCD_STATUS1 = 0x00`, and verify that the handler calls `updi_step()` once, rebuilds the FSM thread list, and sends a stop-reason reply of the form `T05thread:<id>;`.

test.name: on_step_s_calls_updi_run_and_sends_T05_stop_reason_32bit
test.purpose: Dispatch an `s` packet for a 32-bit instruction (e.g., `CALL`, `JMP`, `LDS` or `STS`), and verify that the handler sniffs the instruction, correctly calculates the target PC, temporarily installs a hardware breakpoint at slot 1, calls `updi_run()`, clears slot 1, rebuilds the FSM thread list, and sends a stop-reason reply of the form `T05thread:<id>;`.

test.name: on_continue_calls_updi_run_then_fsm_invalidate
test.purpose: Dispatch a `c` packet with the mock `updi_ocd_poll_halted()` returning 0 on the first poll, and verify that the handler calls `updi_run()` and then `fsm_invalidate()` before entering the poll loop.

test.name: on_continue_rebuilds_thread_list_after_halt_and_sends_stop
test.purpose: After the simulated halt triggered by `on_continue` (mock `updi_ocd_poll_halted()` returns 0 on the Nth call), verify that `fsm_build_thread_list()` is called and the handler sends a stop-reason packet to the GDB client.

test.name: on_continue_ctrl_c_returns_T02
test.purpose: Dispatch a `c` packet, then while `on_continue` is in its select/poll loop write `\x03` to the GDB client side of the socketpair. Verify that the handler calls `updi_halt()` and replies `T02thread:<id>;` (SIGINT).

test.name: on_continue_returns_E01_after_UPDI_FAIL_MAX_consecutive_poll_failures
test.purpose: Configure the mock `updi_ocd_poll_halted()` to return -1 unconditionally. Dispatch a `c` packet and verify that the handler gives up after `UPDI_FAIL_MAX` (8) consecutive failures and replies `E01` rather than spinning indefinitely.

test.name: on_continue_emulates_leading_32bit_call_before_run
test.purpose: Park the live PC (mock `updi_ocd_read_pc()`) on a direct 32-bit `CALL 0x1238` opcode (mock `updi_mem_read()` canned bytes `0e 94 1c 09`), with the mock `updi_ocd_poll_halted()` halting on the first poll. Dispatch a `c` packet and verify the handler emulates the change-of-flow once via `updi_ocd_emulate_cof_32bit()` with return address `0x3f4` (PC+4) and branch target `0x1238` before calling `updi_run()`, working around the AVR-Dx OCD first-change-of-flow-after-RUN errata (issue #40) so breakpoints inside the callee are not skipped.

test.name: on_continue_does_not_emulate_when_pc_not_on_cof
test.purpose: Park the live PC on a non-change-of-flow opcode (mock `updi_mem_read()` canned bytes for `SEC`, `08 94 00 00`). Dispatch a `c` packet and verify the handler performs no change-of-flow emulation (`updi_ocd_emulate_cof_32bit()` is not called) and free-runs directly via `updi_run()`.

test.name: on_halt_reason_returns_T02_when_extbrk_set
test.purpose: Set the mock `updi_ocd_read_halt_status()` to return `OCD_STATUS1 = OCD_STATUS1_EXTBRK (0x10)`, dispatch a `?` packet, and verify the reply is `T02thread:<id>;` (SIGINT). With `OCD_STATUS1 = 0x00` the reply must be `T05thread:<id>;` (SIGTRAP).

test.name: rsp_dispatch_qsupported_returns_feature_string_no_target_access
test.purpose: Dispatch a `qSupported` packet and verify that a non-empty feature string is returned and that no UPDI calls are made.

test.name: rsp_dispatch_qattached_returns_1_no_target_access
test.purpose: Dispatch a `qAttached` packet and verify the reply is `1` and that no UPDI calls are made.

test.name: on_detach_D_resumes_target_closes_socket_resets_gdb_fd
test.purpose: Dispatch a `D` packet and verify that the handler calls `updi_run()`, closes the GDB client socket, and sets `*ctx->gdb_fd_p` to -1 without exiting the server process.

test.name: on_detach_clears_hw_bps_before_run
test.purpose: Insert a `Z0` breakpoint, dispatch a `D` packet, and verify the call sequence: `updi_ocd_clear_hw_bp()` is called for the occupied slot 0 BEFORE `updi_run()`, and afterwards the `RspContext.hw_bp_addr[0]` slot is `0xFFFFFFFF`. This guarantees the next GDB session inherits a clean user silicon comparator.

test.name: on_kill_k_sets_g_quit_to_1
test.purpose: Dispatch a `k` packet and verify that `g_quit` is set to 1, causing the event loop to exit on its next iteration.

test.name: on_monitor_qRcmd_passes_hex_body_to_monitor_dispatch
test.purpose: Dispatch a `qRcmd` packet with a hex-encoded command body and verify that `monitor_dispatch()` receives the same hex-encoded string without any pre-decoding.

test.name: on_monitor_returns_ok_when_monitor_dispatch_succeeds
test.purpose: Inject a mock `monitor_dispatch()` that returns 0 and verify that the `qRcmd` handler sends `OK` to the GDB client.

test.name: on_monitor_sends_o_packet_error_on_updi_failure
test.purpose: Inject a mock `monitor_dispatch()` that returns -1 and verify that the `qRcmd` handler sends an O-packet error message to the GDB console.

test.name: H_packet_minus1_and_0_both_map_to_active_fsm_thread
test.purpose: Dispatch `Hg-1` and `Hg0` in turn, each followed by a `g` packet, and verify that both select the active FSM thread's register frame.

test.name: qC_returns_QC0_when_no_c_thread_selected
test.purpose: Dispatch `qC` with no prior `Hc` and verify the reply is the literal `QC0` and that the handler issues no UPDI memory reads, OCD register reads, or `fsm_*` calls.

test.name: qC_returns_selected_c_thread_in_hex
test.purpose: Pre-set `*ctx->c_thread_p` to 0x2a, dispatch `qC`, and verify the reply is `QC2a` (lowercase hex, no padding).

test.name: qOffsets_returns_text_data_bss_all_zero
test.purpose: Dispatch `qOffsets` and verify the reply is the literal `Text=0;Data=0;Bss=0` with no UPDI memory access.

test.name: T_packet_returns_OK_for_live_thread
test.purpose: Populate `ctx->fsm->threads[]` with GDB ids 1 and 3, dispatch `T3`, and verify the reply is `OK`.

test.name: T_packet_returns_E01_for_unknown_thread
test.purpose: Populate `ctx->fsm->threads[]` with only GDB id 1, dispatch `T2a` (tid 42), and verify the reply is `E01`.

test.name: R_packet_invalidates_fsm_runs_and_emits_stop
test.purpose: Dispatch `R00` and verify that `fsm_invalidate()` is called, `updi_run()` is called exactly once (via the delegated `c`), the thread list is rebuilt on halt, and a `T05` stop packet is emitted on the wire.

test.name: vRun_invalidates_fsm_runs_and_emits_stop
test.purpose: Dispatch `vRun;;arg1` (empty filename, ignored arg) and verify the GDB-protocol-compliant halt-at-entry behaviour: `fsm_invalidate()` called, thread list rebuilt via `fsm_build_thread_list()`, a `T05` stop reply emitted, and `updi_run()` NOT called (the client decides when to resume execution).

test.name: vAttach_halts_target_and_emits_stop_reply
test.purpose: Dispatch `vAttach;1` and verify that `updi_run()` and `updi_step()` are NOT called, that `fsm_invalidate()` and `fsm_build_thread_list()` are called, and that the reply is a `T05` stop packet containing a `thread:<hex>;` suffix.

test.name: vKill_replies_ok_closes_socket_does_not_set_quit
test.purpose: Dispatch `vKill;1` and assert the HLR-064 per-session-disconnect contract: the reply is the literal `OK`, `*quit_p` remains `0` (server does NOT shut down), `updi_halt()` was invoked at least once, both HW-BP comparators were released via `rsp_hw_bp_clear_all()`, and the GDB socket pointed-at by `ctx->gdb_fd_p` was closed and reset to `-1`. Per LLR-RSP-25.

test.name: qSupported_advertises_vRun_vAttach_vKill_no_multiprocess
test.purpose: Dispatch `qSupported` and verify the reply does NOT contain `multiprocess+` (FSM threading is demoted to introspection; the live CPU is the sole GDB thread) and DOES contain `vRun+`, `vAttach+`, and `vKill+`.

test.name: captured_session_replay_holds_demote_invariants
test.purpose: Replay the demote-correctness invariants from a real captured GDB session (tests/fixtures/rsp/break_hit_bt.log, AVR128DA28 hardware: the monitor-reset/break/hit/bt/info-threads/monitor-avros-tasks sequence that previously crashed avr-gdb). Feed the captured GDB request packets through the server and assert: the qSupported reply omits multiprocess+ (keeps vRun+), qfThreadInfo replies l, qThreadExtraInfo,1 replies empty, and bare Hg0 is accepted. Proves FSM-as-GDB-threads cannot reappear, which is what makes bt safe. Per LLR-RSP-26.

test.name: step_over_32bit_lds_uses_reserved_slot_and_keeps_user_hw_bp
test.purpose: Insert a user HW breakpoint (Z1 -> comparator 0) and confirm it occupies the silicon slot, then dispatch a single-step over a 32-bit LDS (opcode w0=0x9000). Assert the step used updi_step_32bit with the RESERVED comparator (slot 1, RSP_HW_BP_STEP_SLOT) and that the user HW breakpoint in slot 0 is left untouched (silicon and shadow). Confirms the HW-comparator arbiter keeps single-stepping always possible regardless of the user breakpoint, per HLR-016.

test.name: Z2_replies_empty_packet_so_gdb_falls_back_to_sw_watch
test.purpose: Dispatch `Z2,800100,1` and verify the reply is the empty RSP packet (payload length zero), proving the server signals \"unsupported\" so GDB transparently falls back to software watchpoints. No call into the UPDI layer is made.

test.name: z3_remove_also_replies_empty_packet
test.purpose: Dispatch `z3,800200,1` and verify the reply is the empty RSP packet (payload length zero); the `z` form must behave identically to the `Z` form for the unsupported Z2/Z3/Z4 family.

test.name: vFlashErase_allocates_buffer_and_replies_ok_for_flash_range
test.purpose: Dispatch `vFlashErase:100,200`, verify reply is `OK`, `ctx.flash_xact_buf` is non-NULL, `ctx.flash_xact_base==0`, `ctx.flash_xact_len==2*UPDI_FLASH_PAGE_SIZE` (the range straddles two 512-byte pages), and the buffer is pre-filled with `0xFF`.

test.name: vFlashErase_E22_for_data_space_address
test.purpose: Dispatch `vFlashErase:810000,10` (EEPROM window on the GDB side) and verify reply is `E22` and `ctx.flash_xact_buf` remains NULL.

test.name: vFlashWrite_copies_payload_into_buffer_at_offset
test.purpose: After a `vFlashErase:0,200`, dispatch `vFlashWrite:10:\x11\x22\x33\x44`, verify reply is `OK`, the four bytes appear in `ctx.flash_xact_buf` at offsets 0x10..0x13, and the surrounding bytes remain `0xFF`.

test.name: vFlashWrite_decodes_0x7D_xor_0x20_binary_escape
test.purpose: Construct a packet `vFlashWrite:0:` followed by `0x7D 0x03 0x7D 0x0A` and dispatch via `rsp_dispatch_n()` with the explicit byte length, verify reply is `OK`, and the buffer contains `0x23` (`'#'`) at offset 0 and `0x2A` (`'*'`) at offset 1.

test.name: vFlashDone_flushes_buffer_via_nvm_write_flash_and_replies_ok
test.purpose: After `vFlashErase:0,200` + `vFlashWrite:0:\x98\x95` and pre-loading `ctx.hw_bp_addr[0]=0x42`, dispatch `vFlashDone`. Verify reply is `OK`; `mock_flash_write_count==1`; `mock_flash_writes[0].addr==UPDI_FLASH_BASE`; the first two bytes of the captured page buffer are `0x98 0x95`; `ctx.flash_xact_buf==NULL`; `ctx.flash_xact_len==0`; and `ctx.hw_bp_addr[0]==0xFFFFFFFF` (HW-BP shadow cleared per the HLR-053 spec).

test.name: vFlashDone_with_no_active_transaction_replies_ok_noop
test.purpose: Dispatch `vFlashDone` with no preceding `vFlashErase` and verify reply is `OK` and `mock_flash_write_count==0` (no FLASH writes attempted).

test.name: m_packet_mid_vflash_transaction_aborts_and_returns_E22
test.purpose: After `vFlashErase:0,200`, dispatch `m800100,4` and verify reply is `E22` and `ctx.flash_xact_buf` is NULL (the abort path freed the in-progress buffer).

test.name: qSupported_advertises_vFlash_packets
test.purpose: Dispatch `qSupported:multiprocess+` and verify the reply payload contains the substrings `vFlashErase+`, `vFlashWrite+`, and `vFlashDone+`.

test.name: Z0_in_sw_mode_patches_BREAK_opcode_via_flash_patch
test.purpose: With default `bp_mode == RSP_BP_MODE_SW`, dispatch `Z0,400,2` and verify the reply is `OK`, `updi_nvm_flash_patch()` was invoked exactly once with `addr == UPDI_FLASH_BASE + 0x400`, `len == 2`, and payload `{0x98, 0x95}` (the AVR `BREAK` opcode little-endian), while no HW comparator was touched.

test.name: Z0_in_sw_mode_records_original_opcode_from_flash
test.purpose: Pre-load the `__wrap_updi_mem_read()` canned buffer with `{0xCD, 0xAB}`, dispatch `Z0,500,2`, and verify `ctx.sw_bp[0]` is `{addr=0x500, orig={0xCD, 0xAB}, in_use=true}`.

test.name: z0_in_sw_mode_restores_original_opcode
test.purpose: Pre-load the canned read buffer with `{0x42, 0xC9}`, dispatch `Z0,600,2` followed by `z0,600,2`, and verify two `updi_nvm_flash_patch()` calls were made — the second writing `{0x42, 0xC9}` back to `UPDI_FLASH_BASE + 0x600` — and that `ctx.sw_bp[0].in_use == false` afterward.

test.name: Z0_in_sw_mode_refuses_data_space_address_with_E22
test.purpose: Dispatch `Z0,810000,2` (data-space address with `GDB_AVR_DATA_FLAG` set, EEPROM window) and verify the reply is `E22`, `updi_nvm_flash_patch()` was not called, and `ctx.sw_bp[0].in_use == false`.

test.name: Z0_in_sw_mode_snapshots_and_restores_cpu_state
test.purpose: Pre-load `mock_ocd_gpr[i] = 0x10 + i`, `mock_ocd_sreg = 0xAA`, `mock_ocd_sp = 0xBEEF`, `mock_ocd_pc = 0xCAFE`, dispatch `Z0,700,2`, and verify ≥32 GPR writes, ≥1 SREG write, ≥1 SP write, and ≥1 PC write were observed, and that the shadow mock state still matches the pre-load values after the round-trip.

test.name: Z0_in_hw_only_mode_falls_back_to_HW_BP_path
test.purpose: Set `ctx.bp_mode = RSP_BP_MODE_HW_ONLY`, dispatch `Z0,800,2`, and verify `mock_hw_bp_set_calls == 1`, `mock_flash_patch_count == 0`, and `ctx.sw_bp[0].in_use == false` — preserving the Phase 1–8 legacy semantics.

test.name: Z0_in_sw_mode_idempotent_on_same_address
test.purpose: Dispatch `Z0,900,2` twice and verify `mock_flash_patch_count == 1` — the second install on a shadowed address shall reply `OK` without re-patching FLASH.

test.name: Z0_in_auto_mode_prefers_hw_comparator
test.purpose: Set `ctx.bp_mode = RSP_BP_MODE_AUTO`, dispatch `Z0,400,2`, and verify the reply is `OK`, the free user comparator was used (`mock_hw_bp_set_calls == 1`, `mock_hw_bp_silicon[0] == 0x400`), and no FLASH was patched (`mock_flash_patch_count == 0`, `ctx.sw_bp[0].in_use == false`) — the glitch-free, sleep-safe common case for a single breakpoint.

test.name: Z0_in_auto_mode_falls_back_to_sw_when_hw_slot_occupied
test.purpose: Set `ctx.bp_mode = RSP_BP_MODE_AUTO`, dispatch `Z0,400,2` (takes the single user comparator) then `Z0,500,2`, and verify the second install fell back to the SW FLASH-`BREAK` patch: exactly one new patch (`mock_flash_patch_count == 1` at `UPDI_FLASH_BASE + 0x500`), the comparator retained (`ctx.hw_bp_addr[0] == 0x400`), and `ctx.sw_bp[0]` recording `{addr=0x500, in_use=true}`.

test.name: z0_in_auto_mode_removes_both_hw_and_sw
test.purpose: Set `ctx.bp_mode = RSP_BP_MODE_AUTO`, install a HW breakpoint (`Z0,400,2`) and a SW fallback (`Z0,500,2`), then verify removal drains the correct table for each: `z0,500,2` clears the SW shadow (`ctx.sw_bp[0].in_use == false`) without touching the comparator (`mock_hw_bp_clear_calls == 0`), and `z0,400,2` then frees the comparator (`mock_hw_bp_clear_calls == 1`).

test.name: Z0_in_auto_mode_idempotent_on_hw_address
test.purpose: Set `ctx.bp_mode = RSP_BP_MODE_AUTO` and dispatch `Z0,400,2` twice; verify the second insert is idempotent — `mock_hw_bp_set_calls == 1` and `mock_flash_patch_count == 0` — confirming a re-insert of an address already on the (now-occupied) comparator does not wrongly install a duplicate SW patch.

test.name: continue_after_sw_bp_install_injects_leading_instruction
test.purpose: Regression for the SW-breakpoint resume skip (LLR-RSP-50 / LLR-UPDI-34). Prime the opcode at PC as a non-CoF `ldi` (`0xE087`) and dispatch `Z0,200,2`; assert `ctx.pc_dirty` is set by the patch. Then dispatch `c` and assert the resume executed the leading instruction via injection (`mock_inject_step_calls == 1`) BEFORE the free-run (`mock_run_calls == 1`, `EV_STEP` precedes `EV_RUN`) and that `ctx.pc_dirty` was consumed (cleared). Without the fix the silicon's fresh-PC-write skip drops the instruction the CPU was halted on, which surfaced on hardware as function arguments read as 0 after a breakpoint.

test.name: step_after_sw_bp_install_injects_leading_instruction
test.purpose: Companion to the continue case (LLR-RSP-50 / LLR-UPDI-34) for single-step. After a `Z0,200,2` install marks `ctx.pc_dirty`, dispatch `s` and assert the step over the freshly-restored PC was performed by injection (`mock_inject_step_calls == 1`) and NOT by a plain `updi_step()` (`mock_step_calls == 0`), and that `ctx.pc_dirty` was cleared.

test.name: vFlashDone_also_clears_sw_bp_shadow
test.purpose: Install a SW breakpoint via `Z0,A00,2`, run a `vFlashErase:0,200` / `vFlashDone` cycle, and verify `ctx.sw_bp[0].in_use == false` afterward — the BREAK opcode is no longer in FLASH so the shadow must be dropped.

test.name: on_detach_D_sets_disconnect_reason_to_D
test.purpose: Build a default `RspContext`, assert `ctx.disconnect_reason == NULL`, dispatch the RSP packet `D`, and assert `ctx.disconnect_reason` is now the string `"D"`. Confirms `dh_detach` records the disconnect classification before closing the GDB socket so the entry-layer lifecycle logger can name the cause without a reverse include. Per LLR-RSP-43.

test.name: vKill_sets_disconnect_reason_to_vKill
test.purpose: Build a default `RspContext`, assert `ctx.disconnect_reason == NULL`, dispatch `vKill;1`, and assert `ctx.disconnect_reason == "vKill"`. Confirms the vKill handler records its classification on the upward-only field so the disconnect lifecycle line can name the cause as `vKill` rather than the generic `EOF`. Per LLR-RSP-43.

test.name: qSupported_advertises_swbreak_and_hwbreak
test.purpose: Dispatch `qSupported:multiprocess+;swbreak+;hwbreak+` and assert the reply payload contains the substrings `swbreak+` and `hwbreak+` so a multiprocess-capable GDB sees the new stop-cause tags advertised. Per LLR-RSP-45.

test.name: continue_emits_swbreak_when_pc_matches_sw_bp_shadow
test.purpose: Install a software breakpoint at `0x100` via `Z0,100,2` (default `bp_mode == sw`), arrange `mock_ocd_pc = 0x100` and the OCD poll script to deliver an immediate halt, dispatch `vCont;c`, drain the reply, and assert the last RSP packet's payload begins with `T05swbreak:;thread:` so GDB sees the SW-BP cause. Per LLR-RSP-44 / LLR-RSP-45.

test.name: continue_emits_hwbreak_when_pc_matches_hw_bp_shadow
test.purpose: Switch to `bp_mode == hw-only`, install a hardware breakpoint at `0x200` via `Z0,200,2`, arrange `mock_ocd_pc = 0x200` and the OCD poll script to deliver an immediate halt, dispatch `vCont;c`, drain the reply, and assert the last RSP packet's payload begins with `T05hwbreak:;thread:` so GDB sees the HW-BP cause. Per LLR-RSP-44 / LLR-RSP-45.

test.name: continue_emits_bare_T05_when_pc_matches_no_breakpoint
test.purpose: With no breakpoints installed, arrange `mock_ocd_pc = 0xCAFE` and the OCD poll script to deliver an immediate halt, dispatch `vCont;c`, drain the reply, and assert the last RSP packet's payload begins with `T05thread:` (no `swbreak:` or `hwbreak:` tag). Confirms the classifier returns the caller's `SC_NONE` hint when neither shadow matches and the formatter therefore emits no extra tag. Per LLR-RSP-44 / LLR-RSP-45.

test.name: vCont_probe_advertises_range_step
test.purpose: Dispatch `vCont?` and assert the reply payload is exactly `vCont;c;s;r` so a range-step-capable GDB activates its range-step optimisation. Per LLR-RSP-46.

test.name: vCont_range_step_steps_until_pc_leaves_range
test.purpose: Build the context, set `mock_ocd_pc = 0x100`, arrange `__wrap_updi_step` to advance `mock_ocd_pc` by 2 each call (script: 0x100, 0x102, 0x104, 0x200), dispatch `vCont;r100,200`, drain, assert the payload begins with `T05` (no `swbreak:`/`hwbreak:` tag because PC 0x200 matches no shadow) and that `mock_step_calls >= 1` (the loop must call `updi_step` at least once before exiting). Exercises the shared `bp_step_range()` core via the RSP handler. Per LLR-RSP-46 / LLR-RSP-53.

test.name: vCont_range_step_returns_immediately_when_pc_already_outside
test.purpose: Set `mock_ocd_pc = 0x500` and dispatch `vCont;r100,200`. Assert `mock_step_calls == 0` (loop must check PC before stepping) and the payload begins with `T05thread:`. Per LLR-RSP-46.

test.name: vCont_range_step_emits_T02_on_ctrl_c
test.purpose: Set `mock_ocd_pc = 0x100` (inside `[100,200)`) and arrange `__wrap_updi_step` to keep PC inside the range; write a single `\x03` byte to the GDB-side socket before dispatching `vCont;r100,200`. Assert the payload begins with `T02thread:` (Ctrl-C → SIGINT). Per LLR-RSP-46.

test.name: vCont_range_step_rejects_malformed_packet_with_E22
test.purpose: Dispatch `vCont;rZZ,200` (non-hex `start`) and assert the last reply payload is `E22`. Per LLR-RSP-46.

test.name: qSupported_advertises_qXfer_memory_map_read
test.purpose: Dispatch `qSupported:multiprocess+;swbreak+;hwbreak+`, drain, and assert the reply payload contains the substring `qXfer:memory-map:read+`. Confirms the new capability is advertised so a memory-map-aware GDB requests the document. Per LLR-RSP-47.

test.name: qXfer_memory_map_read_returns_xml_with_flash_and_ram_regions
test.purpose: Set `ctx.flash_size = 0x20000`, `ctx.sram_base = 0x803000`, `ctx.sram_size = 0x4000`. Dispatch `qXfer:memory-map:read::0,800`, drain, and assert the reply payload begins with `l<memory-map>` and contains the substrings `<memory type="flash" start="0x0" length="0x20000">`, `<property name="blocksize">0x200</property>`, and `<memory type="ram" start="0x803000" length="0x4000"/>`. Per LLR-RSP-47.

test.name: qXfer_memory_map_read_advertises_mapped_flash_rom_with_idx
test.purpose: With `ctx.idx` set and `ctx.map.flash_size = 0x20000`, dispatch `qXfer:memory-map:read::0,800` and assert the reply contains `<memory type="rom" start="0x808000" length="0x8000"/>` — the AVR-Dx mapped-flash data window advertised so GDB will issue reads of flash-resident `.rodata` (e.g. an avrOS `currStateName` string) instead of refusing them client-side. Per LLR-RSP-47 / LLR-RSP-52 (HLR-067).

test.name: qXfer_memory_map_read_omits_mapped_flash_rom_without_idx
test.purpose: Without an ELF index (`ctx.idx == NULL`) and with only Flash/SRAM sizes set (NVM region sizes left zero, so the SIGROW `rom` element is also absent), dispatch `qXfer:memory-map:read::0,800` and assert the reply contains no `type="rom"` element — the server does not advertise the mapped-flash window it cannot translate. Per LLR-RSP-47 / LLR-RSP-52.

test.name: qXfer_memory_map_read_includes_eeprom_fuses_lock_sigrow_userrow
test.purpose: With Flash/SRAM sizes populated, dispatch `qXfer:memory-map:read::0,800` and assert the reply payload begins with `l` and contains all five non-FLASH NVM region elements at their GDB-visible ELF VMA bands: `<memory type="flash" start="0x810000" length="0x200">` (EEPROM), `<memory type="flash" start="0x820000" length="0x10">` (FUSES), `<memory type="flash" start="0x830000" length="0x4">` (LOCK), `<memory type="rom" start="0x840000" length="0x40"/>` (SIGROW), `<memory type="flash" start="0x850000" length="0x20">` (USERROW). Confirms the device-class constants from `src/updi.h` are emitted alongside the ELF-derived Flash/SRAM regions so `(gdb) info mem` reports all seven AVR-Dx memory regions. Per LLR-RSP-47.

test.name: qXfer_memory_map_read_supports_chunked_offset_length
test.purpose: Set the same Flash/SRAM sizes as above, dispatch `qXfer:memory-map:read::0,10` first, assert the payload begins with `m` (more available) and is exactly 0x10 bytes after the framing prefix. Then dispatch `qXfer:memory-map:read::10,800` and assert the payload begins with `l` (last chunk) and equals the remainder of the document so concatenating both windows reproduces the full XML. Per LLR-RSP-47.

test.name: qXfer_memory_map_read_replies_l_when_no_elf_loaded
test.purpose: Build the context with all three sizing fields zero (no ELF supplied), dispatch `qXfer:memory-map:read::0,200`, and assert the reply payload is exactly `l` (end-of-transfer with no document). Confirms the server declines to fabricate a memory map when it cannot derive one from the ELF. Per LLR-RSP-47.

test.name: on_read_mem_returns_E14_for_address_outside_advertised_map
test.purpose: Negative bounds-check test reproducing the silicon scenario captured on 2026-05-20. Set `ctx.flash_size = 0x4740`, `ctx.sram_base = 0x804000`, `ctx.sram_size = 0x10e` (so the memory map is advertised); dispatch `m807ff8,2` — an address 0x3eea bytes past the advertised SRAM end and inside none of the seven advertised regions. Drain and assert the reply payload is exactly `E14`. Also assert `mock_read_count == 0` to prove the bounds check short-circuits before any UPDI transaction is issued. Per LLR-RSP-48.

test.name: on_read_mem_allows_address_inside_eeprom_band
test.purpose: Positive whitelist test confirming the bounds check accepts addresses that lie inside any of the five non-FLASH NVM bands, not just FLASH and SRAM. Set the same Flash/SRAM sizing as above so the advertisement is active; prime the UPDI mock with two canned bytes `0xCA 0xFE`; dispatch `m810000,2` (EEPROM base, GDB-side VMA — bit-23 flip yields UPDI 0x010000). Drain and assert the reply payload is exactly `cafe`, `mock_read_count == 1`, and `mock_reads[0].addr == 0x10000`. Confirms the EEPROM/FUSES/LOCK/SIGROW/USERROW ELF VMA bands are part of the whitelist. Per LLR-RSP-48.

test.name: on_read_mem_permissive_when_no_memory_map_advertised
test.purpose: Regression guard for the no-ELF startup mode (where HLR-063 replies `l` with no map and GDB falls back to its built-in defaults). Leave all three sizing fields zero (`build_ctx` default); prime the UPDI mock with one canned byte `0x5A`; dispatch `m807ff8,1` — an address that would be rejected if the bounds check were active. Drain and assert the reply payload is exactly `5a` and `mock_read_count == 1`, proving the bounds check is correctly bypassed when no map was advertised. Per LLR-RSP-48.

test.name: rsp_logging_enabled_emits_tx_and_rx_markers_to_stderr
test.purpose: Verify --log RSP traffic logging. Call `rsp_set_logging(true)`, then capture fd-level stderr (pipe + dup2 of STDERR_FILENO) across each call. `rsp_send_packet(fd, "qSupported")` must emit a line containing `RSP > qSupported` before sending; after framing `g` to the peer, `rsp_recv_packet()` must return 1 with payload `g` and emit a line containing `RSP < g` after receipt. Confirms both the TX and RX markers and the `rsp_set_logging()` setter wired to `g_log_rsp`. Per LLR-RSP-49.

test.name: rsp_logging_disabled_emits_no_markers
test.purpose: Negative companion: with `rsp_set_logging(false)` (the default, i.e. no `--log`), `rsp_send_packet(fd, "OK")` writes nothing to the captured stderr (captured length is 0), proving the `RSP > ` / `RSP < ` markers are gated entirely on `g_log_rsp`. Per LLR-RSP-49.

file.header: Unit tests for the elfutils-based `src/elf_parser.c`: ELF validation, avrOS sentinel symbol discovery, Harvard / mapped-flash address conversion, fail-safe degradation, deviceinfo note extraction, DWARF source-line round-trip, and handle release. Fixture ELF binaries (compiled with `-g`) are generated under `tests/fixtures/`. The former heap symtab/strtab and malloc-injection tests are retired — libelf owns that memory now.

test.name: elf_open_accepts_valid_avr_elf32_binary
test.purpose: Call `elf_open()` with a well-formed AVR ELF32 fixture file and verify the return value is 0, `ctx.elf` is non-NULL, and `ctx.fd` is open.

test.name: elf_open_returns_minus1_on_invalid_elf_magic
test.purpose: Call `elf_open()` with a file whose first 4 bytes are not the ELF magic sequence and verify the return value is -1.

test.name: elf_open_returns_minus1_on_wrong_machine_type
test.purpose: Call `elf_open()` with a valid ELF32 file that has `e_machine != EM_AVR` and verify the return value is -1.

test.name: elf_find_avros_tables_populates_all_7_avros_sentinel_fields
test.purpose: Call `elf_find_avros_tables()` with a fixture ELF that contains all 7 avrOS sentinel symbols (`__start_FSM_TABLE`, `__stop_FSM_TABLE`, `__start_QUE_TABLE`, `__stop_QUE_TABLE`, `__start_EVNT_TABLE`, `__stop_EVNT_TABLE`, `currStateMachine`) and verify every populated field of `AvrOsSymbolIndex` is non-zero.

test.name: elf_flash_addr_applies_vma_minus_base_over_2_formula
test.purpose: Call `elf_flash_addr()` with known `vma` and `ctx.flash_base` values and verify the return equals `(vma - flash_base) / 2`.

test.name: elf_find_avros_tables_translates_flash_but_not_sram
test.purpose: After `elf_find_avros_tables()` on the full fixture, verify the FLASH-resident table addresses (`fsm_table_addr`, `queue_table_addr`, `event_table_addr`) are physical FLASH byte LMAs below the 0x800000 data band (i.e. mapped-flash-translated), while the SRAM-resident `current_fsm_addr` is a raw VMA at or above 0x800000.

test.name: elf_find_avros_tables_returns_0_on_partial_symbol_match
test.purpose: Call `elf_find_avros_tables()` with a fixture ELF containing only some of the avrOS sentinels and verify the return value is 0 (not -1).

test.name: elf_find_avros_tables_zero_initialises_absent_symbol_fields
test.purpose: After `elf_find_avros_tables()` on a partial-symbol ELF, verify that each field in `AvrOsSymbolIndex` that corresponds to a missing symbol is zero.

test.name: elf_has_fsm_symbols_requires_non_zero_table_address_and_count
test.purpose: Verify `elf_has_fsm_symbols()` returns 0 for a zero-initialised `AvrOsSymbolIndex` and 1 once both `fsm_table_addr` and `fsm_table_count` are non-zero.

test.name: elf_close_releases_handles_and_closes_fd
test.purpose: After a successful `elf_open()`, call `elf_close()` and verify `ctx.elf` and `ctx.dwarf` are NULL, `ctx.fd` is -1, and the OS file descriptor is actually closed (`fcntl(saved_fd, F_GETFD)` fails with `EBADF`).

test.name: elf_close_safe_on_partially_initialised_context
test.purpose: Call `elf_close()` on a zero-initialised `ElfContext` (NULL handles, `fd = -1`) and verify no crash or double-free occurs and the handles/fd remain cleared.

test.name: elf_open_sets_flash_base_and_sram_base_from_pt_load_segments
test.purpose: After a successful `elf_open()` on the full fixture, verify `ctx.sram_base` equals the VMA of the second `PT_LOAD` segment (0x00804000 for the AVR128DA28 fixture) and `ctx.flash_size` is non-zero.

test.name: elf_open_extracts_device_name_from_deviceinfo_note
test.purpose: After `elf_open()` on every AVR fixture (all built for AVR128DA28), verify `ctx.device_name` equals `"avr128da28"` — the lowercase part-name string extracted from the `.note.gnu.avr.deviceinfo` ELF note via libelf section data.

test.name: elf_open_leaves_device_name_empty_when_note_absent
test.purpose: Copy the full fixture to a temp path and zero every `"avr<digit>"` ASCII triplet so the deviceinfo heuristic finds nothing, then `elf_open()` the rewritten ELF and verify it still returns 0 and `ctx.device_name` is the empty string. Proves the note-extraction step is non-fatal on inputs that lack the note.

test.name: elf_dwarf_accessors_round_trip
test.purpose: On a `-g` fixture, verify `elf_dwarf_available()` returns 1; map the entry-point code address to a source `file:line` via `elf_addr_to_line()` (when it resolves, assert line > 0 and a non-empty file, and that `elf_line_to_addr()` returns a real address for that `file:line`); verify `elf_line_range()` brackets the entry address with a non-empty half-open range (`lo <= addr < hi`); and verify both `elf_addr_to_line()` and `elf_line_range()` on an address far outside any CU return -1 without crashing.

test.name: elf_cfi_cfa_extracts_avr_frame_rules
test.purpose: On the gdb_debug_session fixture, derive a post-prologue address inside `leaf()` from its source line via `elf_line_to_addr()` (so the test is independent of the toolchain's code layout) and assert `elf_cfi_cfa()` returns a Canonical-Frame-Address rule based on the Y frame-pointer pair (r28) with a positive offset; an address past the last FDE returns -1 without crashing. Deterministic / hardware-free guard for the in-tree `.debug_frame` interpreter. Per LLR-ELF-14.

test.name: elf_var_addr_resolves_globals_and_locals
test.purpose: On the gdb_debug_session fixture, derive a PC inside `leaf()` from its source line (`elf_line_to_addr()`) and assert `elf_var_addr()` resolves variable locations/types from DWARF: the global `g_marker` (DW_OP_addr) to a non-zero masked SRAM address with size 2 / unsigned; the leaf() parameter `b` (a Y-relative local) to a size-2 address above the supplied synthetic Y; and an unknown name to -1 without crashing. Exact addresses/offsets are toolchain-specific, so only type and Y-relative placement are asserted. Deterministic / hardware-free guard for the variable-resolution backing conditional breakpoints. Per LLR-ELF-15.

test.name: elf_addr_to_func_resolves_enclosing_function
test.purpose: On the gdb_debug_session fixture, derive PCs inside leaf() and main() from their source lines (`elf_line_to_addr()`) and assert `elf_addr_to_func()` maps them to "leaf" and "main" respectively, and returns -1 for an address outside any subprogram. Deterministic / hardware-free guard for the DAP stackTrace frame names. Per LLR-ELF-16.

test.name: elf_value_model_enumerates_and_renders
test.purpose: On the gdb_debug_session fixture, enumerate the file-scope globals with `elf_var_enum()` and find the struct `g_cfg` and array `g_arr`; assert `elf_type_render()` marks them expandable and renders the struct inline (`{base = …`), `elf_type_children()` returns base/gain (gain at offset 2) and the array's 4 elements at a 2-byte stride, and that an all-0xFF memory stub renders the uint16 member as 65535 vs the int16 member as -1 (signed/unsigned by encoding); locals (a/b/prod/sum) enumerate at leaf. Deterministic / hardware-free guard for the DWARF value model. Per LLR-ELF-17 / LLR-ELF-18 / LLR-ELF-19.

test.name: elf_var_find_and_type_size
test.purpose: On the gdb_debug_session fixture, assert `elf_var_find()` resolves `g_marker` (a PC inside leaf derived from its source line) to a non-zero address and type DIE offset, that `elf_type_size()` reports 2 bytes for that uint16_t type, and that an unknown name returns -1. Deterministic / hardware-free guard for the DAP evaluate / setVariable resolution. Per LLR-ELF-20 / LLR-ELF-21.

file.header: Unit tests for `src/fsm_mapper.c`: FSM table reading, stable GDB thread ID assignment, active-thread identification, g-packet register frame construction, thread count capping, and stack-free guarantees. All UPDI calls are stubbed via a mock layer.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_reads_fsm_table_from_flash_via_updi
test.purpose: Verify that `fsm_build_thread_list()` calls `updi_mem_read()` targeting `idx->fsm_table_addr` and reads `idx->fsm_table_count` consecutive 9-byte `fsmStateMachineDescr_t` records.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_returns_minus1_on_updi_failure
test.purpose: Inject a mock `updi_mem_read()` that returns -1 and verify that `fsm_build_thread_list()` propagates the error by returning -1.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_sets_active_thread_from_current_fsm_ptr
test.purpose: Inject a mock `currStateMachine` SRAM value matching the second FSM entry's `stateMachine` pointer and verify that only that entry has `is_active == true` and `ctx->active_id == 2`.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_sets_active_id_0_when_no_entry_matches
test.purpose: Inject a `current_fsm` SRAM value that does not match any registered FSM and verify that `ctx->active_id == 0`.

file.header: Unit tests for `src/monitor.c`: hex command decoding, prefix matching, per-sub-command UPDI reads, O-packet output formatting, 512-byte buffer constraint, and the no-halt guarantee. All UPDI calls are intercepted by a mock layer that records calls and returns injected data.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_hex_decodes_cmd_before_prefix_matching
test.purpose: Pass `monitor_dispatch()` a hex-encoded `"avros events"` command and verify the function routes to `cmd_events()`, confirming that decoding occurs before prefix matching.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_avros_tasks_routes_to_cmd_tasks
test.purpose: Dispatch hex-encoded `avros tasks` with a non-empty FSM table (fsm_table_count=2). Assert monitor_dispatch returns 0, that cmd_tasks invoked fsm_build_thread_list (wrapped), and that at least one O-packet was emitted. Confirms `tasks` routes to cmd_tasks and renders the FSM introspection snapshot. Per LLR-MON-10.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_treats_invalid_hex_sequence_as_unrecognised
test.purpose: Pass `monitor_dispatch()` an odd-length hex string and verify it returns -2 without crashing or producing partial output.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_rejects_cmd_without_avros_space_prefix
test.purpose: Pass a hex-encoded command that decodes to `"other events"` and verify `monitor_dispatch()` returns -2.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_sends_usage_hint_o_packet_on_bad_prefix
test.purpose: Pass a command with an unrecognised prefix and verify that `monitor_dispatch()` sends at least one RSP O-packet containing a usage-hint string before returning -2.

test.name: cmd_events_reads_event_count_descriptors_from_evnt_table
test.purpose: Dispatch `"avros events"` and verify that `updi_mem_read()` is called with address `idx->event_table_addr` and a length equal to `idx->event_count` × 4 bytes (`evntDescriptor_t` size).

test.name: cmd_events_reports_name_and_status_value_per_descriptor
test.purpose: Inject two `evntDescriptor_t` records pointing at FLASH names `"RX"`, `"TX"` and 1-byte SRAM status values `0x01`, `0x00` and verify the decoded O-packet text contains both names and both status bytes formatted as `0xXX`.

test.name: cmd_events_output_is_hex_encoded_o_packet
test.purpose: Dispatch `"avros events"` and verify the single captured `rsp_send_packet()` payload begins with `'O'` and every subsequent character is an uppercase hex digit (`[0-9A-F]`), with an overall odd length.

test.name: cmd_queues_reads_queue_count_descriptors_from_que_table
test.purpose: Dispatch `"avros queues"` and verify that `updi_mem_read()` is called with `idx->queue_table_addr` and a length equal to `idx->queue_count` × 10 bytes (`queDescriptor_t` size).

test.name: cmd_queues_formats_capacity_and_sizeofelement_for_each_entry
test.purpose: Inject two `queDescriptor_t` records with `(capacity, sizeOfElement)` of `(8, 1)` and `(16, 4)` respectively and verify the decoded O-packet text contains `"capacity=8 sizeOfElement=1"` and `"capacity=16 sizeOfElement=4"`.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_and_helpers_never_call_updi_halt
test.purpose: Execute both sub-commands (`events`, `queues`) through `monitor_dispatch()` and verify that `updi_halt()` is never called by inspecting the mock call log.

test.name: verb_reset_pulses_updi_and_clears_shadows
test.purpose: Hex-encode `"reset"` through `monitor_dispatch_ex()` with a stub `RspContext` and verify that `updi_enter_debug()` and `rsp_hw_bp_clear_all()` are each called exactly once and that `updi_halt()` is not called.

test.name: verb_halt_emits_T05_stop_reply_and_suppresses_OK
test.purpose: Hex-encode `"halt"` through `monitor_dispatch_ex()` and verify the captured `rsp_send_packet()` payload starts with the literal three characters `T05`, and that the dispatcher returns -3 so the caller suppresses the trailing `OK`.

test.name: verb_go_calls_updi_run_and_returns_OK
test.purpose: Hex-encode `"go"` through `monitor_dispatch_ex()` and verify `updi_run()` is invoked exactly once and the dispatcher returns 0 so the caller emits `OK`.

test.name: verb_erase_refused_without_allow_erase_flag
test.purpose: Dispatch `"erase"` with `ctx.allow_erase = 0` and verify `updi_chip_erase()` is NOT called, the captured O-packet text mentions `--allow-erase`, and the dispatcher returns -1 so the caller emits `E22`.

test.name: verb_erase_allowed_when_flag_set_clears_shadows
test.purpose: Dispatch `"chip-erase"` with `ctx.allow_erase = 1` and verify `updi_chip_erase()`, `updi_enter_debug()`, and `rsp_hw_bp_clear_all()` are each called exactly once.

test.name: verb_version_emits_o_packet_with_version_and_date
test.purpose: Dispatch `"version"` and verify the captured O-packet decodes to a string containing both `"avrOSdb"` and `"built"`.

test.name: verb_bp_mode_sw_and_hw_only_mutate_ctx
test.purpose: Dispatch `"bp-mode hw-only"` then `"bp-mode sw"` on the same `RspContext` and verify `ctx.bp_mode` cycles through `RSP_BP_MODE_HW_ONLY` and back to `RSP_BP_MODE_SW`; an invalid argument returns -2.

test.name: verb_help_emits_one_line_per_recognised_verb
test.purpose: Dispatch `"help"` and verify that at least 8 O-packets are sent (one per documented top-level verb) before the dispatcher returns 0.

test.name: unknown_top_level_verb_emits_usage_hint
test.purpose: Dispatch a token that is neither a known verb nor `avros …` and verify the captured O-packet text contains `"usage:"` and the dispatcher returns -2.

test.name: avros_prefix_still_routed_to_legacy_dispatch
test.purpose: Dispatch `"avros events"` through `monitor_dispatch_ex()` and verify the call is forwarded to `monitor_dispatch()` (none of the top-level verb side-effects fire: `updi_enter_debug`, `updi_chip_erase`, and `updi_halt` all remain at zero invocations).

file.header: Integration tests validating system-level properties not covered by per-LLR unit tests: server startup latency (HLR-005), RSP protocol purity (HLR-020), and build portability (HLR-033, HLR-034).

test.name: integration_server_ready_within_2_seconds_of_client_connect
test.purpose: Launch `avrOSdb` against a loopback UPDI stub and a fixture ELF, connect a GDB client, and measure the elapsed time from TCP accept to the first valid RSP response. Assert the elapsed time is less than 2.0 seconds.

test.name: integration_server_emits_only_standard_rsp_no_ide_extensions
test.purpose: Capture all TCP traffic from a full debug session (connect, register read, memory read, continue, breakpoint, detach) and verify that every server-originated packet conforms to the GDB RSP specification with no DAP, Cortex-Debug, or other IDE-specific packet types present.

test.name: build_compiles_clean_on_linux_with_c99_and_posix
test.purpose: Execute `make` with `CC=gcc CFLAGS="-std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L"` and assert that the build exits with status 0 and produces no compiler warnings or errors on a Linux x86-64 host.

test.name: runtime_links_only_libc_and_elfutils
test.purpose: Run `ldd avrOSdb` on the linked binary and verify the only shared-library dependencies are libc, the loader/vDSO, libutil, and the required elfutils stack (libdw, libelf) plus libdw's compression backends (libz, libzstd, liblzma, libbz2). Assert that no Java runtime, Python interpreter, Electron libraries, or other heavyweight dependency appears.

file.header: Verification tests for the Makefile install/uninstall targets, the `check-tools` pre-flight target, and the Unix man page. Tests fork a subprocess or invoke `make` directly and inspect the resulting file-system state or exit codes.

test.name: check_tools_exits_nonzero_when_required_tool_is_absent
test.purpose: Temporarily shadow a required tool (e.g. `avr-gcc`) with a dummy wrapper that is not executable, then run `make check-tools` and verify it exits with a non-zero status and prints a diagnostic to stderr naming the missing tool.

test.name: make_install_places_binary_at_prefix_bin
test.purpose: Run `make install PREFIX=/tmp/aod_test_$$` (using a temporary directory as the prefix) and verify that the file `$(PREFIX)/bin/avrOSdb` exists and is executable after the target completes.

test.name: make_install_places_man_page_at_prefix_man1
test.purpose: After `make install PREFIX=...`, verify that the file `$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1/avrOSdb.1` exists and that `man -l` parses it without error.

test.name: make_uninstall_removes_all_installed_files
test.purpose: After `make install PREFIX=...`, run `make uninstall PREFIX=...` and verify that both `$(PREFIX)/bin/avrOSdb` and `$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1/avrOSdb.1` no longer exist.

test.name: user_manual_exists_and_contains_required_sections
test.purpose: Read `doc/UserManual.md` and verify the file exists and contains all required section headings: Prerequisites, Build, Connection Wiring, Usage (or Options), and at least one Example.

test.name: make_bundle_produces_deb_package
test.purpose: Run `make bundle VERSION=0.1.0` and verify that `dist/avrOSdb_0.1.0_amd64.deb` exists, that `dpkg-deb --info` exits 0, and that `dpkg-deb --contents` lists both `./usr/bin/avrOSdb` and `./usr/share/man/man1/avrOSdb.1`.

test.name: make_bundle_produces_rpm_package
test.purpose: Run `make bundle VERSION=0.1.0` and verify that `dist/avrOSdb-0.1.0-1.x86_64.rpm` exists and that `rpm -qp --list` exits 0 and lists both `/usr/bin/avrOSdb` and `/usr/share/man/man1/avrOSdb.1`.

test.name: make_bundle_produces_homebrew_formula
test.purpose: Run `make bundle VERSION=0.1.0` and verify that `dist/avrOSdb.rb` exists, is valid Ruby syntax (parseable by `ruby -c`), and contains the required fields: `desc`, `url`, `sha256`, `version`, and an `install` block.

test.name: test_vscode_extension_declares_avros_debug_view
test.purpose: Statically verify the VS Code companion extension declares the avrOS Debug View: `tools/vscode/avrosdb-dap/package.json` contributes the `avrosDebug` activity-bar container, all six views (`avrosVariables`/`avrosCallStack`/`avrosBreakpoints`/`avrosStateMachines`/`avrosEvents`/`avrosQueues`) and the `media/avros.svg` icon (which must exist on disk); `extension.js` references the three introspection custom requests (`avrosdb/fsmList|eventList|queueList`) and `registerTreeDataProvider`. When `node` is available, `extension.js` additionally passes `node --check`.

test.name: test_vscode_extension_provides_turnkey_launch_config
test.purpose: Statically verify the extension's turnkey debug flow: `package.json` declares an `initialConfigurations` entry with `request:"launch"` plus `program`/`serial`/`elf`, and `extension.js` registers the configuration provider and adapter-descriptor factory (`registerDebugConfigurationProvider`, `registerDebugAdapterDescriptorFactory`, `resolveDebugConfiguration`) and waits for the server's `listening on` banner.

file.header: Unit and harness-level tests covering the `--device` one-shot diagnostic mode and the `--rsp`/`--dap` front-end selection: argument parsing, mutual exclusion (with `--load`, and between `--rsp`/`--dap`), `updi_read_device_info()` success and failure paths over a PTY, the human-readable report format, and verification that the diagnostic path bypasses the GDB listener.

test.name: emit_vscode_config_prints_attach_launch_json
test.purpose: Capture stdout while calling `emit_vscode_config()` and assert the printed launch.json carries the `avrosdb` debug type, a self-starting `request: "launch"` config with `program`/`serial`, the `request: "attach"` alternative, and the default port 1234 — the `--emit-vscode-config` helper. Per LLR-MAIN-26.

test.name: parse_args_accepts_device_flag_without_elf_operand
test.purpose: Invoke `parse_args()` with `argv = {"avrOSdb", "--device", "/dev/ttyUSB0"}` and assert `cfg.device_info == true`, `cfg.serial_device == "/dev/ttyUSB0"`, `cfg.elf_path == NULL`, and `parse_args()` returns without exiting.

test.name: parse_args_rejects_device_combined_with_load
test.purpose: Fork a subprocess that calls `parse_args()` with `--device --load /dev/ttyUSB0 fw.elf`; assert the child exits with status 1 and that captured stderr contains `"--device is mutually exclusive with --load"`.

test.name: parse_args_mode_defaults_to_rsp_and_honours_dap_rsp
test.purpose: Invoke `parse_args()` three ways and assert `cfg.dap_mode`: with no mode flag it is `false` (default RSP); with `--dap` it is `true`; with `--rsp` it is `false`.

test.name: parse_args_rejects_rsp_combined_with_dap
test.purpose: Fork a subprocess that calls `parse_args()` with `--rsp --dap /dev/ttyUSB0 fw.elf`; assert the child exits with status 1 and that captured stderr contains `"--rsp and --dap are mutually exclusive"`.

test.name: updi_read_device_info_returns_sigrow_and_asi_bytes
test.purpose: Open a PTY pair; in a helper thread script the slave end to echo half-duplex bytes and respond to a SIGROW DEVICEID read at `0x1100`-`0x1102` with canned signature `0x1E 0x97 0x0A`, a SYSCFG.REVID read at `0x0F01` returning `0xA6`, a SIGROW.SERNUM read at `0x1110`-`0x111F` returning a canned 16-byte serial number, and to LDCS reads of SYS_STATUS / KEY_STATUS / STATUSB. Call `updi_read_device_info()` and assert all struct fields match the canned values and that the function returns 0 with `info.fail_op == NULL`.

test.name: updi_read_device_info_reports_failed_step_on_nak
test.purpose: Drive the PTY harness to return an unexpected byte in place of the SIGROW response. Assert `updi_read_device_info()` returns -1, `info.fail_op` equals the string `"sigrow"`, and `info.fail_errno` is negative.

test.name: parse_args_sleep_flag_disables_debug_in_sleep
test.purpose: Verify `parse_args()` defaults `cfg.debug_in_sleep` to true and that passing `--sleep` sets it false (HLR-077 / LLR-MAIN-25).

test.name: run_device_mode_prints_report_to_stdout
test.purpose: Capture `stdout` from `run_device_mode()` driven by the PTY harness with signature `0x1E 0x97 0x0A`. Assert the captured output contains the literal lines `Serial device:`, `Baud rate:`, `Signature:`, `Family:`, `Revision:`, `Serial:`, and `UPDI status:` (case-sensitive prefix match).

test.name: device_mode_does_not_call_rsp_listen
test.purpose: Link the test binary with a stub `rsp_listen()` that flags a global. Invoke `run_device_mode()` to completion and assert the flag remains clear, proving the diagnostic path bypasses GDB listener startup.

file.header: On-target hardware integration test harness for the AVR-Dx UPDI driver, device-info report, SRAM/FLASH memory access, and the GDB RSP server. Manual-only: never invoked by `make test`. Driven by the Makefile targets `hw-test`, `hw-test-nvm`, `hw-test-rsp`, and `hw-test-all`. Configurable via `HW_PORT`, `HW_DEVICE_ID`, `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR`, `HW_RSP_PORT`, `HW_TEST_ELF`, `HW_ADDR_24BIT`, `HW_VERBOSE` (env or CLI). Destructive groups gated by `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES` (FLASH) and `HW_TEST_RSP=YES` (RSP).

test.name: A1_port_open_and_cold_start_handshake
test.purpose: Open the configured serial device and execute the UPDI cold-start handshake (BREAK + SYNCH). Assert that `updi_open()` returns a valid file descriptor and that the handshake completes without error. Implicitly verifies that `HW_PORT` / `--port` resolution and CLI-overrides-environment precedence work end-to-end.

test.name: A2_read_device_info
test.purpose: Call `updi_read_device_info()` against the live target and capture the returned struct. Assert the call returns 0 and `info.fail_op == NULL`; the captured fields are reused by A3..A7.

test.name: A3_deviceid_matches_expected
test.purpose: Compare the SIGROW `DEVICEID0..2` bytes against the configured `HW_DEVICE_ID` (default `0x1E970A`). Assert exact byte-for-byte match.

test.name: A4_signature_non_zero_non_ff
test.purpose: Assert that the captured SIGROW signature is neither all `0x00` nor all `0xFF` (catches dead-bus / pull-up-only conditions that A3 might miss if `HW_DEVICE_ID` were misconfigured).

test.name: A5_revid_non_zero
test.purpose: Assert that the captured `SYSCFG.REVID` byte is non-zero.

test.name: A6_sernum_non_zero_non_ff
test.purpose: Assert that the 10-byte SIGROW `SERNUM` field is neither all `0x00` nor all `0xFF`.

test.name: A7_nvmprog_bit_clear
test.purpose: Assert that the `ASI_SYS_STATUS.NVMPROG` bit is clear, proving the target is not stuck in a programming session at harness start-up.

test.name: B0_sram_single_byte_round_trip
test.purpose: Write one byte to `HW_SRAM_ADDR` via `updi_mem_write()`, read it back via `updi_mem_read()`, and assert byte-equality. Reaching this test through any of the four `hw-test*` Makefile targets implicitly verifies that the recipes forward `HW_PORT`, `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, and related variables to the child process.

test.name: B1_sram_64_byte_round_trip
test.purpose: Write a 64-byte deterministic pattern to `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, read it back, and assert byte-for-byte match.

test.name: B1a_sigrow_read_repeatability
test.purpose: Read SIGROW twice via `updi_mem_read()` and assert both reads return identical bytes. Isolates the read path from the write path; a failure indicates a bus or framing problem rather than RAM corruption.

test.name: B1b_sram_constant_0xAA_round_trip
test.purpose: Write 64 bytes of constant `0xAA` to `HW_SRAM_ADDR` and read back. Asserts that data fidelity does not depend on byte value (rules out value-dependent framing or escape-byte bugs).

test.name: B1c_sram_write_once_read_twice
test.purpose: Write a known pattern to `HW_SRAM_ADDR` once, then read the region back twice; assert both reads are identical. On failure, the harness shall print a hint instructing the operator to choose a different `--sram-addr` / `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, because the live target CPU is writing to the probed region.

test.name: B2_sram_600_byte_round_trip
test.purpose: Write a 600-byte buffer to `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, read it back, and assert byte-equality. Exercises multi-chunk transfer and any internal block-size boundary handling in the UPDI driver.

test.name: B3_flash_24bit_addressing_smoke
test.purpose: When `HW_ADDR_24BIT` is true, perform a small read at `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR` using the UPDI 24-bit addressing path; assert the call returns the expected number of bytes. Skipped when `HW_ADDR_24BIT` is false.

test.name: C1_flash_erase_and_write
test.purpose: When `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES`, erase the FLASH page at `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR` and write a deterministic pattern via the NVM controller; assert all NVM controller status checks succeed. Skipped otherwise.

test.name: C2_flash_read_back_verify
test.purpose: Read the FLASH page written by C1 and assert a byte-for-byte match against the written pattern. Skipped unless `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES`.

test.name: D1_rsp_server_accepts_tcp_connection
test.purpose: When `HW_TEST_RSP=YES`, `fork`+`execl` the production `build/avrOSdb` against the configured serial port; open a TCP client to `127.0.0.1:HW_RSP_PORT` and assert the connect succeeds within a bounded timeout. Skipped otherwise.

test.name: D2_rsp_qsupported_round_trip
test.purpose: Send an RSP `$qSupported#37` packet to the spawned server and assert a non-empty, properly-framed RSP reply is received. Skipped unless `HW_TEST_RSP=YES`. On completion the harness shall terminate the spawned server cleanly via SIGTERM + `waitpid`.

test.name: D3_rsp_ctrl_c_interrupt_returns_T02
test.purpose: With the spawned server running and a connected TCP client, dispatch a `c` (continue) RSP packet, wait long enough for the loop to enter its poll/select state, then send a single `0x03` byte (GDB Ctrl-C async-interrupt) on the same TCP connection. Assert that the server replies with a stop-reason packet whose signal field is `T02` (SIGINT) and that the live target is observably halted afterwards (via a subsequent `g` packet succeeding). Skipped unless `HW_TEST_RSP=YES`. Exercises the production async-interrupt path end-to-end through real silicon, validating both LLR-RSP-11 (Ctrl-C path) and LLR-UPDI-08 (`updi_halt()`).

test.name: D4_rsp_qC_current_thread
test.purpose: Send a framed `qC` packet over the same TCP socket used by D1–D3 and assert the reply payload begins with the two-character prefix `QC` followed by a thread id. Validates HLR-059's qC handler against live silicon.

test.name: D5_rsp_qOffsets_section_bases
test.purpose: Send `qOffsets` and assert the reply payload begins with the literal `Text=` (the avrOSdb stub always reports `Text=0;Data=0;Bss=0` because the firmware image is linked at fixed addresses). Validates HLR-059's qOffsets handler against live silicon.

test.name: D6_rsp_monitor_info_verb
test.purpose: Send `qRcmd,696e666f` (the hex-encoded ASCII string `info`) and assert the reply payload is non-empty and does not begin with `E` (i.e. is not an `Exx` error code). Validates HLR-055's `monitor info` verb wiring against live silicon.

test.name: D7_rsp_Z2_z2_replies_empty_packet_unsupported
test.purpose: Send `Z2,<sram_addr|0x800000>,1` (request a 1-byte write watchpoint on the configured SRAM scratch address) followed by `z2,<sram_addr|0x800000>,1`. Assert both replies are the empty RSP packet (`$#00`, payload length zero), proving the server signals "unsupported" so GDB falls back to software watchpoints. Validates HLR-056 against live silicon — AVR-Dx UPDI exposes no data-watchpoint hardware.

test.name: D8_rsp_vRun_reload_returns_Tstop
test.purpose: Send `vRun;` and assert the reply payload begins with `T` (any stop signal — typically `T05` SIGTRAP after run-to-main). Validates HLR-058's vRun handler — full reload + reset + halt-at-entry — against live silicon.

test.name: D9_rsp_vFlashErase_vFlashDone_smoke
test.purpose: Destructive — opt-in via `--with-nvm`. Send `vFlashErase:<flash_page>,200` and assert reply is `OK`; then send `vFlashDone` and assert reply is `OK`. Erases one 512-byte FLASH page on live silicon; the subsequent vFlashDone flushes an all-0xFF buffer (the cleared state) which is a valid no-op. Validates HLR-053's vFlash* state machine end-to-end.

test.name: D10_rsp_Z0_z0_sw_bp_flash_break_round_trip
test.purpose: Destructive — opt-in via `--with-nvm` AND must run after D9 so the FLASH page baseline is 0xFF. Send `Z0,<flash_page>,2` and assert reply is `OK`; then `m<flash_page>,2` and assert the 4-character hex payload equals `9895` (AVR `BREAK` opcode `0x9598` little-endian); then `z0,<flash_page>,2` and assert reply is `OK`. Validates HLR-054's full SW-BP install/restore loop — FLASH patch with BREAK, read-back, and restore of original opcode — against live silicon.

test.name: F1_autobaud_picks_reliable_rung
test.purpose: Close the harness UPDI fd, then call `updi_probe_baud(cfg->port, 8, visitor, NULL)`. The visitor records each rung's `{baud, errors, samples}` triple for the log. PASS if the returned baud is ≥ 19200 (the slowest rung in the ladder) — proving the probe walked the ladder, observed at least one zero-error rung on live silicon, and returned the highest-rate working candidate. Exercises the full read-only probe path end-to-end.

test.name: F2_fuse_pretty_print_round_trip
test.purpose: With the harness UPDI fd re-opened at `cfg->baud`, read the FUSES window and the 4-byte LOCK window via `updi_nvm_read()`, then call `updi_format_fuses()` into a 2 KiB stack buffer. PASS if the formatted output contains the literal substrings `WDTCFG`, `OSCCFG`, `SYSCFG0`, and `Lock:` — confirming the per-family fuse decode table fired and the lock-byte trailer was emitted.

test.name: F3_prog_mode_end_to_end_with_verify
test.purpose: Destructive — gated by `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES`. With the harness UPDI fd closed, `fork` and `execl` the production `build/avrOSdb --prog --erase --baud <N> <port> <elf>` against the bench ELF (`build/fixtures/all_nvm.elf` by default, which intentionally avoids FUSES/LOCK windows so the bench stays in a known state). Capture the child's stdout+stderr through an 8 KiB buffer. PASS if `WEXITSTATUS == 0` AND the captured output contains the literal `verify: OK`. Validates `--prog` end-to-end including chip-erase, FLASH/EEPROM/USERROW programming, and read-back verify against live silicon.

file.header: On-target GDB acceptance harness (Group-G tests) that drives a real `avr-gdb` against a live AVR-Dx through `avrOSdb` over UPDI, scripting `-batch` command sequences and applying per-test verdict functions to the transcript. Manual-only: never invoked by `make test`. Driven by `make hw-test-gdb`. The ST_PTR_LONG SRAM-read regression guard (G17) and the Phase-14 interactive debug-session suite (G18–G24, HLR-070) are individually tracked here; the remaining early Group-G protocol-primitive cases (G1–G16) are not yet individually tracked.

test.name: G17_local_variable_values_and_backtrace
test.purpose: Regression guard for the always-24-bit `ST_PTR_LONG` pointer-set (LLR-UPDI-33). Break inside `locals_probe()` in the `-O0` `gdb_locals` fixture where one local of each representative C type is assigned and still live, then `print` each local and run `bt`. Every local must read back the exact constant the fixture assigned and the backtrace must reach `main`. Both surfaces read SRAM off the stack and both were corrupted by the stale-high-byte bug — a Flash read by GDB left the UPDI pointer high byte at `0x80`, so the following 16-bit-pointer SRAM read was misdirected into mapped Flash and returned erased `0xFF`, yielding `0xFF`/garbage locals and a bogus `0x1fffe` return-address frame. With the 24-bit fix every local reads its known value and `bt` is clean.

test.name: G18_multiframe_backtrace_and_frame_selection
test.purpose: Phase-14 interactive debug-session coverage (HLR-070). Break at `leaf` in the `-O0` `gdb_debug_session` fixture and stop in `leaf(7, 2)`, then `bt` must unwind the full `leaf -> mid -> top -> main` chain in frame order and reach `main`. Frame selection (`frame 1`, `frame 2`, `up`, `down`) followed by `info args` must report each frame's own parameter (`mid`'s `n = 7`, `top`'s `seed = 7`), proving avrOSdb's per-frame SP/unwind and SRAM-read plumbing is correct across a multi-frame stack, not just at the innermost frame.

test.name: G19_step_into_next_over_finish_return_value
test.purpose: Phase-14 interactive debug-session coverage (HLR-070). From a breakpoint at `top`, `step` must descend into `mid` (verified by a `bt` showing `#0 mid` / `#1 top`); `next` must step over the `leaf(7, 2)` call without descending; a further `step` must descend into `leaf(7, 3)`; and `finish` must run out of that frame and report the exact returned value (`Value returned is ... = 49405`). Exercises source-level step/next/finish across frames and the function-return-value read, which together require correct change-of-flow emulation, step-comparator use, and stack unwinding on live silicon.

test.name: G20_multiple_breakpoints_hit_in_call_order
test.purpose: Phase-14 interactive debug-session coverage (HLR-070). Set three simultaneous breakpoints (`top`, `mid`, `leaf`), confirm `info breakpoints` lists all three, then `continue` three times. The hit banners must appear in call order — `top`, then `mid`, then `leaf` — proving multiple breakpoints coexist and fire in the order the call chain reaches them.

test.name: G21_conditional_breakpoint_honoured
test.purpose: Phase-14 interactive debug-session coverage (HLR-070). A conditional breakpoint `break leaf if b == 3` must skip the first call `leaf(7, 2)` (condition false) and stop only at `leaf(7, 3)`; the hit banner must show `leaf (a=7, b=3)` and must never show `leaf (a=7, b=2)`. Verifies GDB-side condition evaluation drives repeated host-side resume/inspect cycles correctly against live silicon.

test.name: G22_global_scalar_struct_array_reads
test.purpose: Phase-14 interactive debug-session coverage (HLR-070). Stopped in `leaf`, read globals from the data space: a scalar (`g_marker = 49374`, also `print/x` as `0xc0de`), a struct (`g_cfg = { base = 100, gain = -7 }` and its individual fields), and an array (`g_arr = { 10, 20, 30, 40 }` and the element `g_arr[2] = 30`). Each must read back its exact initialised value, exercising the SRAM/data-space read path for aggregate and indexed expressions.

test.name: G23_per_frame_info_args_and_locals
test.purpose: Phase-14 interactive debug-session coverage (HLR-070). Stopped at `leaf(7, 2)`, `info args` must show `a = 7` and `b = 2`; after two `next` steps execute the local assignments, `info locals` and `print` must show `prod = 14` and `sum = 9`. Verifies per-frame argument and local reads return the exact fixture constants once the locals are live, complementing G17's single-type sweep with the call-chain fixture.

test.name: G24_capstone_full_interactive_session
test.purpose: Phase-14 interactive debug-session coverage (HLR-070). One capstone case driving a realistic session start to finish: break at `top` (confirm `seed = 7` and a `bt` reaching `main`), set a conditional `break leaf if b == 3`, continue to `leaf(7, 3)` (confirm a full `leaf -> mid -> top -> main` backtrace and `a=7, b=3`), read a global (`g_marker = 49374`), and `finish` out of `leaf` reporting the return value `49405`. Combines breakpoints, conditions, multi-frame backtrace, global reads, and finish in a single end-to-end transcript.

test.name: G25_avros_fsm_state_name_string_read
test.purpose: Mapped-flash string read regression (HLR-067 / LLR-RSP-52). Break at the avrOS FSM state handler `ledsFlash` in the example fixture and continue to a hit, then `print stateMachine->currStateName` — a `char *` into the AVR-Dx mapped-flash data window (`.rodata` aliased at data >= 0x8000), which GDB reads as data at `0x80_8xxx`. Before the fix GDB refuses the read ("Cannot access memory at address 0x80....") because the window is undescribed; after advertising it as `rom` and translating the read through the flash LMA, the flash-resident state-name string reads back as a non-empty quoted string. The verdict fails on any "Cannot access memory" diagnostic and passes only when a non-empty string is resolved (`"ledsFlash"` on the bench). Also the end-to-end regression guard for the `flash_lma_off` 16-bit-mask fix (LLR-ELF-04): with the avr-gcc 14.2 full-VMA `.rodata`, the pre-fix delta misdirected the read to unrelated rodata even once the window was advertised. Manual-only (`make hw-test-gdb`).

file.header: Unit tests for the DAP front-end: the wire transport (HLR-075) — the JSON codec (`dj_*` recursive-descent tokenizer, member/string/number accessors, escape decode, and the emission escaper) and the Content-Length message framing (`dap_read_message` / `dap_write_message`) — and the connection lifecycle dispatch (HLR-076) driven over a `socketpair` with `updi_fd = -1` so no hardware is touched. Framing is exercised over an anonymous pipe.

test.name: dj_parse_extracts_request_fields
test.purpose: Tokenise a representative DAP `initialize` request and verify the accessors: the root is an OBJECT; `command` is the STRING `initialize`; `seq` is the NUMBER 3; `arguments` is a nested OBJECT whose `clientID` copies to `vscode` and whose `linesStartAt1` is the TRUE token; a missing member returns -1.

test.name: dj_parse_handles_arrays_and_nesting
test.purpose: Parse `{"a":[1,2,3],"b":{"c":"x"}}` and verify `a` is an ARRAY of size 3, `b` is an OBJECT, and `b.c` copies to `x` — confirming subtree skipping and nested member lookup.

test.name: dj_strcpy_decodes_escapes
