test.purpose: Copy a STRING value containing `\\`, `\"`, and `\n` escapes and verify the decoded bytes are the literal backslash, double-quote, and newline.

test.name: dj_escape_quotes_backslash_and_controls
test.purpose: Escape a string containing `"`, `\\`, and a newline and verify the output uses the short JSON escapes (`\"`, `\\`, `\n`).

test.name: dj_parse_rejects_malformed
test.purpose: Verify `dj_parse()` returns -1 for a member with no value (`{"x":}`), a truncated object (`{"x"`), and an unterminated array (`[1,2`).

test.name: dj_parse_respects_token_cap
test.purpose: Verify `dj_parse()` returns -1 (rather than overrunning) when the token array is too small for the input.

test.name: dap_framing_round_trip_over_pipe
test.purpose: Write two framed messages to a pipe with `dap_write_message()` and read them back with `dap_read_message()`; verify each body and length round-trips exactly with no over-read into the second message, and that closing the write end then yields EOF (return 0).

test.name: dap_read_rejects_oversize_body
test.purpose: Feed a header advertising a `Content-Length` larger than the reader's buffer and verify `dap_read_message()` returns -1 rather than overflowing.

test.name: dap_initialize_handshake
test.purpose: Dispatch an `initialize` request over a socketpair and verify the adapter writes a `response` with `request_seq:1`, `command:"initialize"`, `success:true`, and the `supportsConfigurationDoneRequest` capability, immediately followed by the `initialized` event.

test.name: dap_configuration_done_emits_stopped_entry
test.purpose: Dispatch `configurationDone` (with `updi_fd = -1`) and verify a `success:true` response for that command followed by a `stopped` event with `reason:"entry"` and `threadId:1`.

test.name: dap_disconnect_closes_session
test.purpose: Dispatch `disconnect` and verify `dap_dispatch()` returns 1 (close the session) after writing a `success:true` response for the `disconnect` command.

test.name: dap_unknown_request_returns_error
test.purpose: Dispatch an unimplemented command and verify the adapter replies with a `success:false` response echoing the command and carrying a `message`, rather than leaving the client waiting.

test.name: dap_continue_responds_and_emits_continued
test.purpose: Dispatch `continue` (updi_fd = -1) and verify the adapter replies `{allThreadsContinued:true}` and emits a `continued` event. Per LLR-DAP-08.

test.name: dap_pause_emits_stopped_pause
test.purpose: Dispatch `pause` and verify a `success:true` response followed by a `stopped` event with `reason:"pause"`. Per LLR-DAP-08.

test.name: dap_step_emits_stopped_step
test.purpose: For each of `next`, `stepIn`, `stepOut`, dispatch the request and verify a `success:true` response followed by a `stopped` event with `reason:"step"`. Per LLR-DAP-08.

test.name: dap_stack_trace_returns_one_frame
test.purpose: Dispatch `stackTrace` (no target/DWARF) and verify the response carries a `stackFrames` array with a single frame `id:0` and `totalFrames:1`. Per LLR-DAP-09.

test.name: dap_scopes_returns_locals_registers_globals
test.purpose: Dispatch `scopes` for frameId 0 and verify the response carries Locals, Registers, and Globals scopes (each with a variablesReference). Per LLR-DAP-13.

test.name: dap_variables_unknown_ref_is_empty
test.purpose: Dispatch `variables` with an out-of-range reference (no ELF/target) and verify an empty `variables` array rather than an error. Per LLR-DAP-13.

test.name: dap_evaluate_unresolved_is_error
test.purpose: Dispatch `evaluate` for an expression with no ELF/target and verify the response is `success:false` (the adapter never fabricates a value). Per LLR-DAP-14.

test.name: dap_read_memory_responds_with_data_field
test.purpose: Dispatch `readMemory` with no target and verify the response is well-formed and carries a `data` field (base64, possibly empty/unreadable) rather than erroring. Per LLR-DAP-15.

test.name: dap_set_variable_unknown_ref_errors
test.purpose: Dispatch `setVariable` with an out-of-range reference and verify the response is `success:false`. Per LLR-DAP-16.

test.name: dap_set_breakpoints_responds_with_per_line_entries
test.purpose: Dispatch `setBreakpoints` with two source breakpoints (`{line:139}`, `{line:141,condition:"n==3"}`) and no ELF/target; verify the response carries a `breakpoints` array with per-line entries (`id:1`/`line:139`, `id:2`/`line:141`), that both entries are recorded in the session table with the condition captured, and that `next_bp_id` advanced to 3. Per LLR-DAP-10.

test.name: dap_set_breakpoints_replaces_prior_set_for_source
test.purpose: Dispatch `setBreakpoints` for `main.c` with two lines, then again with one line; verify the second call replaces the source's set wholesale — only the single new breakpoint remains in the session table. Per LLR-DAP-10.

test.name: dap_set_instruction_breakpoints_responds_with_refs
test.purpose: Dispatch `setInstructionBreakpoints` with two entries (`instructionReference:"0x40c"`, and `"0x400"` with `offset:4`) and no target; verify the response carries per-entry `{id,verified,instructionReference}`, that the addresses resolve (0x40c; 0x400+4=0x404), and that the table entries are marked as instruction breakpoints (`line == -1`). Per LLR-DAP-10.

test.name: test_dap_source_returns_file_content
test.purpose: Write a small temp `.c` file, then dispatch a `source` request with `arguments.source.path` set to it; assert the response is `success:true` for command `source` and its `body.content` carries the file text — confirming the DAP source fallback streams host file content.

test.name: test_dap_source_missing_file_fails
test.purpose: Dispatch a `source` request for a non-existent path and assert the response is `success:false` for command `source` — a clean failure rather than the generic unsupported-request error or a hang.

test.name: dap_serve_runs_handshake_to_disconnect
test.purpose: Drive `dap_serve()` end-to-end without hardware: a stubbed `rsp_accept()` hands it a pre-connected socketpair end whose request stream is pre-loaded with `initialize` then `disconnect`. Verify the accept/select/read/dispatch loop processes both (emitting the initialize response, the `initialized` event, and the disconnect response) and returns 0 when the client disconnects.

test.name: test_dap_fsm_list_empty_without_target
test.purpose: The `avrosdb/fsmList` custom request, dispatched with `updi_fd = -1` (no target), returns a successful response whose body carries an empty `"fsms":[]` array — graceful degradation, no hardware touched.

test.name: test_dap_event_list_empty_without_target
test.purpose: The `avrosdb/eventList` custom request, dispatched with `updi_fd = -1`, returns a successful response whose body carries an empty `"events":[]` array.

test.name: test_dap_queue_list_empty_without_target
test.purpose: The `avrosdb/queueList` custom request, dispatched with `updi_fd = -1`, returns a successful response whose body carries an empty `"queues":[]` array.

file.header: On-target DAP acceptance harness (the DAP analogue of the Group-G GDB harness): spawns a fresh `avrOSdb --dap` against live AVR-Dx silicon and drives it with the real nvim-dap client (headless Neovim) over TCP, applying per-case verdicts to the connection lifecycle. Manual-only (`make hw-test-dap`); never invoked by `make test`. Phase 16 covers the handshake (DAP1–DAP4); execution control, breakpoints, and variables grow this suite in Phases 17–19.

test.name: DAP1_initialize_handshake
test.purpose: nvim-dap attaches to the `avrOSdb --dap` server; verify the `initialize` request completes (capabilities received) and the adapter emits the `initialized` event, i.e. the session becomes active on live silicon.

test.name: DAP2_configuration_done_stopped_entry
test.purpose: After the configuration phase, verify the adapter emits a `stopped` event with reason `entry`, reaching the stopped-at-entry state on the target.

test.name: DAP3_threads_single_cpu
test.purpose: Issue a `threads` request and verify the adapter reports exactly one live CPU thread.

test.name: DAP4_continue_pause_stopped
test.purpose: Phase-17 execution control. Issue `continue` (the target runs), then `pause`, and verify the adapter emits a `stopped` event with reason `pause` — re-halting a freely running target (no breakpoints are installed yet, Phase 18). Per HLR-078 / LLR-DAP-08.

test.name: DAP5_step_stopped
test.purpose: Phase-17 execution control. From the halted target, issue `stepIn` and verify the adapter emits a `stopped` event with reason `step`. Per HLR-078 / LLR-DAP-08.

test.name: DAP6_stacktrace_source_line
test.purpose: Phase-17 shallow stackTrace. Issue `stackTrace` and verify frame 0 resolves the live PC to a source line (numeric `line > 0`) via DWARF, with a `source` object — proving the OCD PC read + libdw line lookup work end-to-end on silicon. Per HLR-078 / LLR-DAP-09.

test.name: DAP7_source_breakpoint_hit
test.purpose: Phase-18 source breakpoints. `setBreakpoints` for a reachable source line in the loaded fixture (default `gdb_target.c:51` — the `blink()` call in the main loop; override via `DAP_BP_SOURCE`/`DAP_BP_LINE`) — verify it resolves+verifies via DWARF and installs through the shared breakpoint core — then `continue` and verify the adapter emits a `stopped` event with reason `breakpoint`, proving file:line breakpoint resolution + install + hit end-to-end on silicon. The harness reflashes `HW_DAP_ELF` first so the running firmware matches the ELF handed to the server. Per HLR-079 / LLR-DAP-10.

test.name: DAP9_scopes_variables_lists_a_global
test.purpose: At the breakpoint, request `scopes` then `variables` on the Globals scope through the real nvim-dap client and verify the firmware global `g_counter` is listed — proving the variables request path works end to end via VS Code/Neovim (the rich per-type cases are in tests/hw/dap_vars.py). Per HLR-082 / LLR-DAP-13.

test.name: DAP8_disconnect_clean
test.purpose: Issue a `disconnect` request and verify the session tears down cleanly (installed breakpoints removed, target resumed) — accepting either the disconnect response or the session object going away, since nvim-dap does not always deliver the response callback as the adapter closes the socket. Per HLR-076 / HLR-079.

file.header: On-target DAP multi-frame stackTrace acceptance harness (Phase 18, the DAP analogue of GDB G18). A pure-Python DAP client spawns `avrOSdb --dap` against live AVR-Dx silicon running the `gdb_debug_session` fixture (`main->top->mid->leaf` nested call chain), breaks inside `leaf` via an instruction breakpoint, and verifies the DWARF-CFI unwinder reports the full call chain. The expected per-frame functions and the break address are derived from the ELF (`avr-nm -S` / `avr-objdump`) at runtime, so the test survives a fixture recompile. Manual-only (`make hw-test-dap-unwind`) — never wired into `make test`.

test.name: DAP_U1_instr_bp_at_leaf_verified
test.purpose: `setInstructionBreakpoints` at a post-prologue address inside `leaf` returns a verified breakpoint, installed through the shared core on silicon. Per LLR-DAP-10.

test.name: DAP_U2_continue_to_breakpoint
test.purpose: `continue` from reset runs the `main->top->mid->leaf` chain and halts at the `leaf` instruction breakpoint, emitting `stopped` with reason `breakpoint`. Per HLR-079.

test.name: DAP_U3_stacktrace_depth
test.purpose: `stackTrace` at the `leaf` stop returns at least four frames — proving the CFI unwinder walks past frame 0. Per HLR-080 / LLR-DAP-11.

test.name: DAP_U4_frames_map_to_call_chain
test.purpose: Each of the first four stack frames' PCs falls inside the expected function of the call chain (`leaf`, `mid`, `top`, `main`), checked against the functions' address ranges from `avr-nm -S` — proving the recovered return addresses are correct, not just non-empty. Per HLR-080 / LLR-DAP-11 / LLR-ELF-14.

test.name: DAP_U5_frames_resolve_source_lines
test.purpose: Each chain frame resolves to a source line (`line > 0`) via DWARF, confirming the unwound caller PCs map to real source through `elf_addr_to_line()`. Per HLR-080 / HLR-072.

test.name: DAP_U6_frames_named_for_function
test.purpose: Each of the first four stack frames carries the name of its function — `leaf`, `mid`, `top`, `main` — proving the adapter resolves the enclosing subprogram via `elf_addr_to_func()` for the frame name (not the raw PC). Per HLR-080 / LLR-ELF-16.

file.header: On-target DAP conditional-breakpoint acceptance harness (Phase 18, the DAP analogue of GDB G21). A pure-Python DAP client spawns `avrOSdb --dap` against live AVR-Dx silicon running the `gdb_debug_session` fixture (whose `main -> top -> mid -> leaf` chain calls `leaf(7,2)` then `leaf(7,3)` every loop), sets a *source* breakpoint in `leaf` carrying a DAP `condition`, and verifies the adapter evaluates it on the live target — auto-resuming when false, stopping when true. The leaf source line is derived from the ELF with `avr-addr2line` at runtime. Manual-only (`make hw-test-dap-cond`) — never wired into `make test`.

test.name: DAP_K1_false_local_condition_skips
test.purpose: A source breakpoint in `leaf` with the always-false local condition `b == 99` (b is only ever 2 or 3): after `continue` the target keeps running and NO breakpoint stop arrives within the window — proving the adapter reads the local over DWARF/OCD, evaluates the condition false, steps over and auto-resumes. Per HLR-081 / LLR-DAP-12 / LLR-ELF-15.

test.name: DAP_K2_true_local_condition_stops
test.purpose: A source breakpoint in `leaf` with the true local condition `b == 2` (hit on the `leaf(7,2)` call): after `continue` the adapter emits `stopped` with reason `breakpoint` — proving a true local condition stops. Per HLR-081 / LLR-DAP-12.

test.name: DAP_K3_true_global_condition_stops
test.purpose: A source breakpoint in `leaf` with the true global condition `g_marker == 49374` (a constant): after `continue` the adapter emits `stopped` with reason `breakpoint` — proving global-variable conditions (DW_OP_addr resolution) work on silicon. Per HLR-081 / LLR-DAP-12 / LLR-ELF-15.

file.header: On-target DAP variables / evaluate / memory acceptance harness (Phase 19, the DAP analogue of GDB Group-G state inspection — G17/G22/G23). A pure-Python DAP client spawns `avrOSdb --dap` against live AVR-Dx silicon running the `gdb_debug_session` fixture, breaks inside `leaf`, and verifies scopes, variables (with struct/array expansion), per-frame locals, evaluate, read/write memory, and setVariable against the fixture's documented values. Manual-only (`make hw-test-dap-vars`) — never wired into `make test`.

test.name: DAP_V1_scopes_locals_registers_globals
test.purpose: `scopes` for frame 0 returns Locals, Registers, and Globals scopes. Per HLR-082 / LLR-DAP-13.

test.name: DAP_V2_global_scalar_reads_back
test.purpose: Expanding the Globals scope, the scalar `g_marker` reads its constant 49374. Per HLR-082 / LLR-ELF-18.

test.name: DAP_V3_struct_expands_to_members
test.purpose: The struct global `g_cfg` carries a child reference that expands to members `base = 100` and `gain = -7` (signed/unsigned by type). Per HLR-082 / LLR-ELF-19.

test.name: DAP_V4_array_expands_to_elements
test.purpose: The array global `g_arr` expands to elements `[0..3] = 10,20,30,40` at the element stride. Per HLR-082 / LLR-ELF-19.

test.name: DAP_V5_frame_locals_read_back
test.purpose: The Locals scope of the leaf frame reports the parameters `a = 7` and `b = 2`, resolved against the frame's registers. Per HLR-082 / LLR-ELF-17.

test.name: DAP_V6_evaluate_field_and_element
test.purpose: `evaluate` resolves `g_cfg.base` (= 100), `g_arr[2]` (= 30), and `g_marker` (= 49374) — identifier + `.field` / `[index]` navigation. Per HLR-083 / LLR-DAP-14.

test.name: DAP_V7_read_memory_array_bytes
test.purpose: `readMemory` of `g_arr` returns the 8 bytes that decode (little-endian) to the u16 sequence 10,20,30,40. Per HLR-084 / LLR-DAP-15.

test.name: DAP_V8_set_variable_writes_back
test.purpose: `setVariable` writes `g_counter = 1234`; a subsequent `evaluate` reads back 1234 — proving the write reached silicon at the right address and width. Per HLR-084 / LLR-DAP-16.

test.name: DAP_V9_frame_source_path_absolute
test.purpose: Stopped inside `leaf`, the `stackTrace` frame's `source.path` is an absolute path that exists on the debug host (resolved from the CU `comp_dir`), so a DAP client opens the source directly instead of falling back to the `source` request. Per LLR-ELF-12.

test.name: DAP_V10_source_request_returns_content
test.purpose: A `source` request for that frame's path returns `success:true` with non-empty `body.content` — the source fallback streams the host file content over DAP. Per LLR-DAP-18.

file.header: On-target DAP avrOS-introspection acceptance harness (Phase 21): a pure-Python DAP client spawns `avrOSdb --dap` against live AVR-Dx silicon and drives the `avrosdb/fsmList` / `avrosdb/eventList` / `avrosdb/queueList` custom requests that feed the VS Code avrOS view, confirming they read the avrOS descriptor tables off the target and return well-formed JSON. Run against the `avros_full` fixture, whose FSM/event/queue table sections hold one zero-filled descriptor each — enough to exercise the count>0 reader path on silicon deterministically. Manual-only (`make hw-test-dap-introspect`) — never wired into `make test`.

test.name: DAP_I1_fsm_list_well_formed
test.purpose: `avrosdb/fsmList` returns a well-formed `fsms` array (the zero descriptor's null state-machine pointer is skipped, so 0 entries — graceful). Per HLR-086 / LLR-DAP-17.

test.name: DAP_I2_event_list_reads_table
test.purpose: `avrosdb/eventList` reads the `EVNT_TABLE` off silicon: against `avros_full` it returns one event whose name is `<null>` (null name pointer) and whose status is the JSON null literal (null status pointer) — exercising the count>0 decode and the null-pointer rendering. Per HLR-086 / LLR-AVROS-01.

test.name: DAP_I3_queue_list_reads_table
test.purpose: `avrosdb/queueList` reads the `QUE_TABLE` off silicon: against `avros_full` it returns one queue with `capacity = 0` (the zero descriptor) — exercising the count>0 decode path on hardware. Per HLR-086 / LLR-AVROS-02.

file.header: On-target acceptance for the `--start` / `--stop` / `--reset` one-shot CPU run-state modes (HLR-089). Spawns the real `avrOSdb` binary against live AVR-Dx silicon and drives each run-state mode in turn, asserting it takes OCD control and exits cleanly with its success banner, and that the UPDI link stays healthy across the repeated attach/detach cycles — exercising the on-silicon `updi_open` → `updi_enter_debug` → `updi_run`/`updi_halt` → `updi_detach` path the host unit tests can only stub. Manual-only (`make hw-test-start-stop`) — never wired into `make test`. Needs only the serial device.

test.name: SS0_start_stop_mutually_exclusive
test.purpose: `avrOSdb --start --stop <serial>` exits non-zero with a "mutually exclusive" diagnostic — the run-state modes reject combination before touching hardware. Per LLR-MAIN-27.

test.name: SS1_stop_halts_cpu
test.purpose: `avrOSdb --stop <serial>` takes OCD control, halts the CPU on live silicon, and exits 0 printing `stop: OK`. Per HLR-089 / LLR-MAIN-28.

test.name: SS2_start_runs_cpu
test.purpose: `avrOSdb --start <serial>` takes OCD control, runs the CPU on live silicon, and exits 0 printing `start: OK`. Per HLR-089 / LLR-MAIN-28.

test.name: SS3_reset_sibling
test.purpose: `avrOSdb --reset <serial>` pulses the UPDI system reset and exits 0 printing `reset: OK`, confirming the sibling run-state mode still works after a start/stop cycle. Per HLR-089.

test.name: SS4_link_healthy_after_cycle
test.purpose: After the start/stop/reset cycle, a fresh `avrOSdb --device <serial>` re-opens the link and reads the SIGROW report (exit 0) — proving `updi_detach()` left the link in a re-openable state. Per HLR-089 / LLR-UPDI-37.

test.name: SS5_stop_repeatable
test.purpose: A second `avrOSdb --stop <serial>` after the full cycle still succeeds (exit 0, `stop: OK`), confirming repeated OCD attach/detach cycles are stable. Per HLR-089 / LLR-MAIN-28.

file.header: On-target DAP source-line stepping acceptance (HLR-078). Spawns `avrOSdb --dap` against live AVR-Dx silicon running the `gdb_debug_session` fixture (call chain main -> top -> mid -> leaf) and verifies stepIn/next/stepOut have source-line granularity and distinct semantics — the regression being that all three single-stepped one instruction. Breakpoints are set at function entries via `setInstructionBreakpoints` (addresses from `avr-nm`). Manual-only (`make hw-test-dap-step`) — never wired into `make test`.

test.name: ST1_stepIn_advances_one_source_line
test.purpose: From `top`'s entry, one `stepIn` advances a whole source line within `top` (the reported line changes in a single step) — proving source-line, not single-instruction, granularity. Per HLR-078 / LLR-DAP-19.

test.name: ST2_stepIn_descends_into_callee
test.purpose: Continued `stepIn` at the `mid()` call line descends into the callee — the stackTrace frame name becomes `mid`. Per HLR-078 / LLR-DAP-19.

test.name: ST3_stepOut_returns_to_caller
test.purpose: `stepOut` from `mid` runs to the return and stops back in the caller `top` (frame name `top`) — distinct from stepIn. Per HLR-078 / LLR-DAP-19.

test.name: ST4a_next_steps_over_calls
test.purpose: From `mid`'s entry, repeated `next` walks mid's body and never enters `leaf` — `next` steps OVER the two `leaf()` calls (running to the return) rather than descending. Per HLR-078 / LLR-DAP-19.

test.name: ST4b_next_is_line_granular
test.purpose: The lines visited by successive `next` within `mid` are monotonic and span several source lines over a handful of steps (instruction-granularity would crawl within one line); a call line may legitimately appear twice (avr-gcc -O0 splits `acc += leaf(...)` into a call row then a post-call assign row). Per HLR-078 / LLR-DAP-19.
